Actor Chase Stokes says that some of his organs were “failing” after he finished filming Outer Banks.

The Maryland-born star played John B in the Netflix series, which released its fifth and final season this week.

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, Stokes, 33, said there was “so much s*** wrong” with his body after filming wrapped.

“I left that show … my liver was failing, my kidney was failing. I had so many health issues that I had to figure out, and my brain was all out of whack,” he told the publication.

“It was a really important time for me to get my bearings right versus just go back into work and mask it.”

The actor said that he discovered he had “alarmingly low” testosterone levels and started undertaking blood tests twice a month, along with transcranial magnetic stimulation therapy, a non-invasive form of brain stimulation.

open image in gallery Chase Stokes attends SiriusXM's Front Row with the cast of 'Outer Banks' ( Getty )

He also entered into “deep, intensive therapy work”, he said.

“Hindsight is 20/20, but I probably, unfortunately, wouldn’t have been around much longer if I didn’t take care of my body, which is a really jarring thought.

“Unfortunately, we’ve seen great people leave this earth too soon for just continuing to go [on], and I have a lot to live for. I have a lot that I want to do, and a lot I want to accomplish.”

The actor added that he now feels “great for the first time in a long time”.

In the interview, Stokes also admitted that the success of the show and his resulting fame left him facing a “really hard time”.

open image in gallery 'Outer Banks' actors, from left, Carlacia Grant, Drew Starkey, Madison Bailey, Chase Stokes, Jonathan Daviss and Madelyn Cline ( AFP/Getty )

He remembered a time when he was walking his dog in Los Angeles and a tour bus stopped next to him.

People were “just taking photos of me”, he said.

“There isn’t really an idiot’s guide of how to navigate success in this space.”

Outer Banks, which was first released in 2020, is set in a community in the Outer Banks of North Carolina and follows two groups of teenagers as they search for a lost treasure.

Before being cast, Stokes previously had small roles in other shows including Stranger Things, Daytime Divas and Tell Me Your Secrets.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

Sports.title: England legend Steven Gerrard’s bizarre secret skill revealed just a week after being handed biggest TV role to date
Sports.content:
IF he didn’t choose football, maybe Steven Gerrard would have been a padel superstar.

Earlier this week, the Liverpool legend, 46, took on current aces Milos Kerkez and Dominik Szoboszlai in a brutal padel match.



Szoboszlai pulled the curtain back on the box office showdown as he posted a snap of the three of them together on the court.

But it seems the iconic former Reds skipper schooled Kerkez, who is a self-professed novice, and his fellow Hungary team-mate.



The left-back told club media: “Yes, it was good. We talked with a friend, with Steven to play one day.

“I wanted to come, so obviously I needed a teammate. I called Dom and Dom came with me.



“I don’t play often, so we got beat because Stevie plays good. It was fun.

“You go to play for fun. I’m learning to play it, I’m having fun playing it. It’s a nice sport, quite nice, and it was a good day. A good day off.”

But the answer to the question everyone wanted to know – will they play again?

Sports.title: Former Man Utd star, 32, defends shock music video showing own club’s headquarters IN FLAMES after bitter contract war
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED flop Memphis Depay has defended a music video depicting the headquarters of Brazilian club Corinthians up in flames.

The Dutch forward, who joined Corinthians in 2024, has had a series of contract disputes with the club.



Depay came under scrutiny recently as the video for his new single “don’t panic” caused controversy.

Corinthians’ headquarters, Parque Sao Jorge, is shown burning down in a grim scene.



Depay has called it “just art” in a response on his social media.

Despite no explicit reference to Corinthians in the lyrics of the song, one of Depay’s lines is: “I know a vice-president who is now my enemy.”

It comes after the 32-year-old took a pay-cut to stay at the club just a week after being released.

He previously slammed the club for “unacceptable behaviour” and threatened to take action, after a supposedly agreed extension was withdrawn.



However, the Netherlands international put an end to the saga by penning a new contract with the Sao Paulo outfit until 2028.

And Corinthians president Osmar Stabile confirmed the ex-Manchester United player “significantly” reduced his financial demands.

Sports.title: Gloating Hull fans waste no time poking fun of Joe Cole during Man Utd game after TNT Sports pundit’s ‘disrespect’
Sports.content:
HULL fans wasted no time giving Joe Cole a taste of his own medicine after the TNT Sports pundit appeared to write off their Premier League survival chances.

The Tigers supporters teased former Chelsea and England star during their blockbuster opener against Manchester United – and they had the perfect chant ready.



As Hull stunned Michael Carrick’s side by winning 2-0 and recording their first ever league win over United, fans could be heard singing: “Are you watching, Joe Cole?”

It came after Cole had made a brutal prediction about Hull on The Dressing Room Podcast, saying: “Hull are gone, man.”



He then claimed the Tigers had “slipped in” to the Premier League through the play-offs, despite their promotion being secured after a 1-0 victory over Middlesbrough in May.

Cole was referring to the fact that Hull were supposed to play Southampton, who beat Boro in the semis before being suspended due to the Spygate scandal – meaning Boro took their place.

He said: “I want to make a confession here today, right. TNT Sports have contacted me for the new season. They’ve tried to slip in the Hull one on the first day of the season. I put my phone on do not disturb!”

But the comments appeared to come back to haunt him as Hull produced a stunning start against United.

The Tigers were backed by a raucous MKM Stadium crowd and quickly showed they were not interested in listening to the doubters, with Semi Ajayi opening the scoring before Nobel Mendy added another.

That was when supporters made sure Cole knew exactly what they thought, belting out: “Are you watching, Joe Cole?”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The pundit’s comments had already caused plenty of anger among Hull fans before a ball was kicked, with one supporter responding online: “You should be ashamed of yourselves.”

Another wrote: “Predicting us to go down is fine but the disrespect is disgusting.”

Hull owner Acun Ilicali also hit back at the criticism before the season began.

The Turkish businessman said: “It is disappointing to see my beautiful city criticised by people who should know better.”



“As a club we are used to being underestimated and we enjoy it, and we enjoyed it more when we were promoted last season.”

“For me, seeing ex-players making fun of a deservedly promoted club, is more laughable than the things they were laughing at.”

There is also a familiar feeling around Hull’s return to the top flight, with their promotion this year coming a decade after they won the Championship play-off final in 2016.

That year, Hull also stunned the odds on the opening day of their Premier League campaign, beating reigning champions Leicester City 2-1.



The Tigers ultimately went down that season, conceding 80 goals, and their defence will once again be under the microscope after they finished with the fourth-worst defensive record in the Championship last term.

But on this evidence, that may not be the weakness Cole and others were expecting.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hull looked organised, aggressive and extremely difficult to break down as they took the game to United as Sergej Jakirovic’s side deservedly won.

Chants of: “And now you’re gonna believe us, were gonna win the league” rang around the MKM Stadium towards the end of the game in what is a delightful day for the city of Hull.

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Dorgu dismal in attacking role as Heaven endures hellish game but Mbeumo rare bright spark
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED suffered a dreadful defeat at newly-promoted Hull City – who are tipped for relegation this season.

Michael Carrick’s side were thoroughly outplayed and suffered two goals from two set-pieces as Marcus Rashford was brought on at half-time.



United were second to every pass, duel and tackle as injury-ridden Hull were also forced to take their goalscorers Semi Ajayi and debutant Nobel Mendy off.

No second half onslaught from United arrived, with Hull No1 Konstantinos Tzolakis seeing out the game comfortably.



Here’s how Katherine Walsh rated the United players from a bouncing MKM Stadium.

Senne Lammens – 6

The Belgian started brilliantly and could not have done anything about Semi Ajayi’s opener after three saves, including from a free Oli McBurnie in the lead up to the goal. Mendy’s header from six yards was unsaveable too.

Noussair Mazraoui – 4

The Moroccan was not at the races. After starting well to head clear at the back post to deny Lewis Coyle an opener inside four minutes, Hull began to exploit the space down his channel.

The World Cup international then failed to get goal side of debutant Mendy’s header for the Hull star’s goal.

Harry Maguire – 5

The 33-year-old endured a shaky start but recovered in his distribution, delivering a great cross into the mixer on 30 minutes. Bizarrely became a forward in the second half, that’s how poor United were.

Ayden Heaven – 4

The 19-year-old started every game of pre-season, but was slow to react often and got the run around by Hull hero McBurnie, also leaving the veteran striker unmarked in the lead up to the opener.



Heaven is still raw and developing and there’s some time yet before he’s ready to consistently start at this level. He lost six out of his nine duels before the break.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Luke Shaw – 5

The left-back department is sparse and United are in the market for reinforcements before the end of the window. And Shaw did not cover himself in glory, struggling to contain Mohamed Belloumi.

Andrey Santos – 5

A tough afternoon for the £48m signing. The 22-year-old looked like a deer in headlights at times and was taken out of his misery by Carrick on 68 minutes.

Youri Tielemans – 5

Like his pivot partner, the former Villa man struggled on his official United debut in a poor afternoon across the board. Pace was a issue.

Showed signs of the strong leadership shown at Villa and in his role as Belgium captain. With 22-year-old Carlos Baleba set to arrive to complete United’s £150m midfield revamp, Tielemans will have to step up and show more this season.



Bruno Fernandes – 4

As is often the case: if Fernandes is bad, United are bad. The skipper did more complaining than creating. Fernandes has not got up to speed after underperforming against Milan in Wroclaw last weekend.

Bryan Mbeumo – 6

The best of a bad bunch. The forward was denied an opener by excellent one-handed save from Konstantinos Tzolakis and put two chances on a plate for Patrick Dorgu in the first half.

The Cameroonian was forced into three positions and tricked to make things happen, often on his own.

Patrick Dorgu – 3

The Dane, 21, endured a dismal afternoon as he struggled to threaten down the left hand side and his finishing left a lot to be desired. He paid the price at the break.



Perhaps Carrick will be secretly delighted that Rashford is around amid the will-he-won’t-he leave saga. The England star replaced Dorgu at half time.

Hull’s three-man defence took the Brazilian out of the game and he did not get a sniff in the first half.

A player who had not made a competitive appearance for United since December 2024 was brought on to save them.

Some tidy balls but failed to make an impact.

Sports.title: Hull 2 Man Utd 0: Carrick’s new-look midfield abysmal as newly-promoted Tigers maul Red Devils in shock first-half blitz
Sports.content:
THE TEAMSHEETS at Hull City were sponsored by McVitie’s and Manchester United crumbled.

It took less than 40 minutes for the home followers to goad the visiting supporters with a rendition of “Mauled by the Tigers” after goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy.



Hull sharpened their claws and knives may be sharpened for Michael Carrick after his worst day in charge as the kind of records tumbled that put a United manager under immediate scrutiny.

This was Hull’s first-ever top-flight victory against United, defeated by a newly-promoted side in an opening fixture for the first time ever.



Carrick may feel a sense of vindication for considering it “ridiculous” to consider Hull away an easy start. His players seemed intent on making it appear as hard as possible.

The circumstances were so dire that Carrick turned to Marcus Rashford at half-time as he made his first competitive United appearance in 20 months.

Rashford came off the bench to win it for United in their last Premier League fixture at Hull. Lightning did not strike twice.

Rashford got a warm hand from the United supporters too dumbfounded to retreat to the concourse for a half-time refreshment as he warmed up.

A new forward is not on the horizon for United. Their dozy defenders will doubtless welcome the imminent arrival of a minder in Carlos Baleba.

United are expected to overhaul their defence next summer but there will be a renewed clamour among the fanbase to strengthen it before the September 1 transfer deadline.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Carrick was insistent on a right-footed-left-footed partnership at centre back. That made Ayden Heaven – the rawest defender – an automatic pick with Lisandro Martinez not up to speed after his World Cup exploits.

That played into battering ram Oli McBurnie’s hands. McBurnie was once on United’s books and upset them with a late equaliser for Sheffield United in 2019.

He threatened to top that from three crosses before the breakthrough, the second shovelled away by Senne Lammens.

United’s new No.1 clawed another centre away but his one-man defence was eventually breached from the resultant corner by Semi Ajayi.

McBurnie pulled onto Heaven, caught ball-watching, and was remarkably denied by Lammens only for Ajayi to pounce on the rebound.



Heaven bickered with McBurnie as the pair made their way off at the interval. That further publicised Heaven’s inferiority complex against someone who has made mince meat of bullying more experienced defenders than the 19-year-old Heaven.

There were more complaints from Heaven, convinced the ball had crept out, after McBurnie bulldozed his way through the United midfield as the clock ticked towards the hour mark.

McBurnie did not get a goal but this was a more memorable afternoon for the man of the match than his late leveller at Bramall Lane nearly seven years ago.



With recruitment still topical at United, it did not reflect favourably on director of football Jason Wilcox that Patrick Dorgu, unveiled at the same time as Heaven in February 2025, had such a dismal day he made way for Rashford at half-time.

Lammens fished the ball out of his net after another set piece, guided in effortlessly by Nobel Mendy.

Opting for Noussair Mazraoui over Diogo Dalot at right back is hardly headline team news but the Moroccan mustered 11 starts for United last term and has always been viewed as a squad player.

Hull had space to pepper Lammens down Mazraoui’s side before Ajayi’s breakthrough. Mazraoui lost Mendy when he shaved Regan Slater’s inswinger for 2-0.

Carrick also got it wrong at the other end of the pitch. Bryan Mbeumo, playing ahead of Mazraoui, was United’s standout performer in pre-season after five starts as the striker. He suddenly shifted to the right to offset the absence of the injured Amad.



With Benjamin Sesko not fit for 45 minutes Carrick picked Matheus Cunha up front after an hour-long stint there against AC Milan in Poland.

Cunha was ill-suited to facing a three-man defence and Dorgu does not convince as a left winger, despite the odd wonder goal.

Mbeumo had a right-footed volley repelled by Konstantinos Tzolakis, who made an even better stop from the Cameroonian late in the second half.



Carrick completely rejigged the attack with Rashford on for the second half. Rashford played on the left, Mbeumo went up front and Cunha headed to the right.

Rashford’s body language used to irritate United fans and he could not conceal his disappointment at an overhit Youri Tielemans pass. Rashford had strayed offside amid the delay.

Tielemans warned us at United’s training camp in Ireland last week that his body “switched off” at the World Cup. He was not switched on and left fellow midfield debutant Andrey Santos exposed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Both were removed for Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo as Carrick attempted to salvage something.

But Hull did not crumble. “Can we play you every week?” their fans asked.

Sports.title: Chelsea blasted for selling tickets for Shakhtar games to their OWN fans with Champions League package costing £218
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans have blasted the club after being offered the chance to pay up to £218 to watch Shakhtar Donetsk in the Champions League at Stamford Bridge.

The Ukrainian giants are set to use the Blues’ home ground for their European fixtures during the 2026-27 season.



Shakhtar have been exiled from their home stadium, the Donbas Arena, since conflict broke out in Donetsk in 2014.

Due to Uefa safety mandates requiring European matches to be played outside Ukraine, the club has previously staged home games across the continent in cities such as Warsaw, Hamburg, and Gelsenkirchen.



Chelsea failed to qualify for European competition following a 10th-place Premier League finish last season, leaving Stamford Bridge without midweek Uefa fixtures.

The club subsequently offered the 40,000-capacity ground to Shakhtar, allowing the Ukrainian champions to capitalise on London’s large Ukrainian diaspora and transport links.

Chelsea have now contacted supporters with details of a four-match ticket bundle covering all of Shakhtar’s home league-phase fixtures.

The message read: “We are giving supporters the opportunity to secure their place with a four-match ticket bundle, giving access to all four of Shakhtar’s home Champions League fixtures at Stamford Bridge.”

Season-ticket holders have been offered all four games for £185, working out at £46.25 per match, despite Chelsea themselves not being involved in the fixtures.

Supporters without a season ticket face an even bigger bill, with packages going on general sale from £218.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Single-match tickets will also be made available once the Champions League draw has taken place.

However, the offer sparked fury among several Blues fans online, with one supporter raging: “From £46 to watch someone that ain’t your own team, while acting like they are doing you a favour giving you a discount.”

Another added: “This is f***ing grim.”

A third reacted: “What an awful email to receive.”

Sports.title: Man Utd fans hit by travel nightmare as trains home from Hull CANCELLED with visitors 2-0 down in Premier League opener
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans were watching their team trail 2-0 at Hull when they were told over the stadium speakers that their trains home had been cancelled.

United travelled to the MKM Stadium for their Premier League opener against newly-promoted Hull City.

And things went from bad to worse for the travelling Old Trafford faithful in the 73rd minute when Hull’s stadium announcer took to the tannoy to reveal the cancellation of multiple trains back to Manchester.



He said: “The 15:03 and 16:03 services towards Manchester have been cancelled.

“Passengers affected by these cancellations should check the latest service information.”



The home supporters sarcastically cheered the announcement, which left many supporters who made the near 100-mile journey wondering how they’d get home.

The ITV and TNT Sports presenter is, unfortunately, regularly targeted by lowlifes on social media – despite being a credentialed presenter who has more than earned her stripes.

Sports.title: Dismal Man Utd sent brutal reality check after opening day defeat by Hull - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Dismal Man Utd sent brutal reality check after opening day defeat by Hull - 5 talking points

HULL CITY 2-0 MANCHESTER UNITED: Newly-promoted Tigers get their Premier League campaign off to a roaring start by outplaying and easily beating an abject United side

View 5 Images Michael Carrick had no answer to Hull City (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United kicked off their Premier League season with a woeful defeat by Hull City in Michael Carrick's first game as permanent manager. Having arrived on Humberside full of optimism, they left having put in one of the worst performances in recent memory.

‌



Hull took the lead when Semi Ajayi smashed in a loose ball from a corner in the 17th minute. It was 2-0 to the newly-promoted side in the 38th minute when Regan Slater's fantastic free-kick was nodded in by Nobel Mendy.

‌



United went in at the half-time break having seen 70 per cent of the ball but having truly tested Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis once with Bryan Mbeumo's effort at the back post.

‌



Carrick reacted by sending on Marcus Rashford for Patrick Dorgu at half-time but got zero reaction from his players, who remained sloppy in possession and lacking intensity out of it. Their first real chance came in the 78th minute, when Hull had substituted their two starting centre-backs, with Tzolakis saving from Mbeumo one-on-one.

In truth they didn't even huff and puff. United mustered next to nothing of note and were deservedly beaten by organised and determined opponents. Here are the talking points.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Lammens powerless

United goalkeeper Lammens had already been forced into making three decent stops before Hull hit the front. The Belgian pushed away a header from Ollie McBurnie, tipped over Ryan Giles' shanked cross and kept out another from McBurnie just before Ajayi buried it.

Lammens has provided a solid and calming presence at the back since his arrival from Royal Antwerp 11 months ago and it was his defence who let him down in the early stages. Luke Shaw lost John Egan at the front post, Ayden Heaven lost McBurnie at the back post and Ajayi was completely unmarked to power home the rebound after Lammens' save came back off the post.

‌



View 5 Images Semi Ajayi opened the scoring for Hull (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

2. Direct and deadly

Hull's game plan was obvious right from the off. Get the ball wide and put it into the box to challenge United in the air. McBurnie is the perfect striker for this tactic; aggressive and awkward. But it was their centre-backs who did the damage from set pieces.

On both occasions the delivery was exceptional, flat and fast. But the lack of leadership and presence in the United defence was remarkable, with Harry Maguire's fabled 'slabhead' nowhere to be seen. Hull's aggression clearly unsettled United, yet it was their quality from dead balls which did the damage.

‌



View 5 Images Nobel Mendy put Hull 2-0 up with a header (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

3. United way off the pace

When you start a new season, the hope is that your players will be highly motivated and raring to go. There was only one side who that appeared to be the case for. United were slow to the ball, lost duel after duel and looked all at sea while defending.

Watching on, it was hard not to wonder whether any other top Premier League sides would still be happy with the statis in defence, with Shaw in his 13th season with the club and Maguire still first-choice at the start of another season.

‌



It was little better in central midfield, either, where new arrivals Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos failed to offer much protection without the ball, or push United forward on the ball. The tactical set-up frequently left players occupying the same positions in the centre of the pitch.

View 5 Images Manchester United's new-look midfield struggled (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

4. Tenacious Tigers

Not many people have given Hull a chance of staying in the Premier League this season after coming up via the play-offs. The Tigers conceded a whopping 66 goals in the Championship last season, but turned it on when it mattered in May.

‌



On this evidence, Sergej Jakirović has a plan for keeping them up. His five-man defence didn't look defensive, with wingbacks Giles and Lewie Coyle getting forward and putting crosses into the box. Mendy made the perfect start on debut, meaning that club-record signing Tzolakis barely had anything to do.

View 5 Images Konstantinos Tzolakis had a comfortable time in goal (Image: Getty Images)

5. Ponderous and toothless

United were supposed to come out after the half-time break on a mission. They were supposed to get Bruno Fernandes on the ball and turn it around through sheer willpower. But it was simply just more of the same lacklustre stuff.

Article continues below

Tielemans looked well off the pace. Heaven's performance was riddled with errors. Fernandes' trademark defence-splitting passes were nowhere to be seen. Matheus Cunha, dropping deep time and again, was completely bypassed. Rashford didn't return a hero. Mbeumo looked the most threatening, but really that is grasping at straws. It's back to the drawing board after this shambolic display.

Sports.title: 'I played against Gerrard, Lampard and Scholes – one was a tougher opponent'
Sports.content:
'I played against Gerrard, Lampard and Scholes – one was a tougher opponent'

Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and Paul Scholes regularly locked horns during their illutrious careers

View 3 Images Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and Paul Scholes were part of a long-running debate in the 2000s (Image: Getty Images)

A former Premier League star found Paul Scholes a tougher opponent than either Steven Gerrard or Frank Lampard. The trio are among the most celebrated players of their era and were key figures for England.

‌



Scholes often found himself the odd man out for his country, with Sven Goran Eriksson often shunting him out to the left flank to accommodate the other two, which led to his early retirement from the international scene in 2004 at the age of 29.

‌



That came amid a long-running debate over whether Gerrard or Lampard was the better player and whether they could play together. However, according to former Blackburn and Birmingham midfielder Barry Ferguson, Manchester United's Scholes was the hardest man to play against.

‌



He told William Hill's podcast, The Warm-Up with Chris Boyd and Chris Sutton: "Paul Scholes was the toughest opponent I faced in the Premier League.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"He could do everything with a football. I could say the likes of Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard, Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira because they were all world-class players, but I didn't like playing against Scholes."

‌



Paul Scholes handed six-month driving ban after being taken to court twice in two days READ MORE :

Frank Lampard's incredible net worth with celeb wife blows away all Premier League rivals READ MORE :

Explaining the difficulty of facing Scholes, the Scot added: "I never knew where he was or what he was going to do and he had a nasty side to him as well.

"But he really could do anything he wanted with a football, he was top class. The other players I mentioned were all top class, but there was just something about Scholes.

View 3 Images Scholes was constantly compared to Gerrard and Lampard (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"You couldn't pin him down, you didn’t know where he was, and he had a range of passing which was ridiculous. He was a top player."

Scholes, one of the most decorated players in Man United's history, is now a pundit and football director at League Two Salford City, where he is a former co-owner. Scholes hasn't dipped his toe into full-time management like Gerrard and Lampard.

View 3 Images Barry Ferguson played against all three (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Gerrard has had spells at Rangers, Aston Villa and Saudi side Al-Ettifaq. After stints at Derby County, Chelsea (twice) and Everton, Lampard led Coventry City to the Championship title last season.

Sports.title: Former Premier League referee admits players more likely to get penalty if they go down
Sports.content:
Former Premier League referee admits players more likely to get penalty if they go down

An ex-top-flight official has addressed an issue that frustrates players and fans

View 3 Images Graham Scott has given an insight into decision-making (Image: Under The Cosh)

Players are more likely to get a penalty if they hit the deck, a former Premier League referee has conceded. A frustration among many players is when fouls aren't given if they attempt to stay on their feet when they are fouled.

‌



That has resulted in players deliberately taking a tumble in a bid to force a decision from the official, which others would regard as simulation or diving. It's a thorny issue that doesn't have an obvious solution.

‌



Graham Scott, who retired as a top-level referee at the end of the 2024/25 season, has explained the difficult position officials are in. Speaking on the Under The Cosh podcast, he admitted a player going down in the event of a foul was often more likely to get the decision.

‌



After a recent example of Sunderland's Brian Bobbey not getting an obvious penalty after staying on his feet was put to him, Scott said: "There are some situations where if the player doesn't go down, they're not going to get a pen, it's as simple as that.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Brobbey is a very strong player, he would be difficult to ref as he also holds the other player a lot. Sometimes your assistant is telling you about holding by the other player and I say, 'Don't give anything because I can see the other player doing it from this side.'

‌



Premier League introduce nine new rules for 2026/27 season including more VAR READ MORE :

"You do get a lot of what we call mutual holding but that can also be a cop-out for not dealing with an actual foul. Clearly, if you stay on your feet, it's much less likely to be given.

"It's also much less likely to be accepted. If a referee gives a penalty against you and the player isn't even on the deck. It's like, 'Really, for that?' It works both ways."

View 3 Images An incident involving Sunderland's Brian Brobbey (left) was put to Scott (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Numerous rule tweaks have been introduced ahead of the new season, including a harder line being taken on grappling and holding at set-pieces. Referees' chief Webb insists physicality must always remain a feature of English football, but believes there were still too many instances of defenders dragging attackers to the ground last season that went unpunished.

He is keen for referees and VARs to be even more vigilant about it. Webb said: "I think fans can expect less warnings from referees [before fouls are given] than they might have seen previously, and I know [those warnings were] a source of frustration.

View 3 Images Howard Webb has explained a key change for the Premier League season (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



"[Fans can expect to see] more situations being penalised, but not only in August or September, throughout the season. I'm not going to commit to say we're going to go from here to penalising lots of contact. Contact's still part of the game.

"We still maintain a high threshold, but I would imagine we'll be sat here this time next year and we’ll be able to reflect on a season where more offences have been penalised. There'll be subtle actions that aren’t penalised, which are all part of the game, we are looking at those clear actions that are clearly unfair."

Sports.title: Arsenal star Bukayo Saka sets record straight on injury battle and sends Ezri Konsa message
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Bukayo Saka sets record straight on injury battle and sends Ezri Konsa message

Bukayo Saka started and scored in Arsenal's 3-0 Premier League triumph over Coventry on Friday evening, putting concerns over his fitness after a patchy World Cup firmly to bed

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka is over his injury problems

Arsenal star Bukayo Saka insists his World Cup injury frustration is already a distant memory. The 24-year-old marksman had to manage Achilles' pain carefully at the back end of last season and throughout this summer's tournament in North America.

‌



However, Saka has hit the ground running in the Premier League, starting and scoring for the champions in their 3-0 demolition of Coventry.

‌



He claims the secret to his sharpness is not prolonged rest - but even more training - explaining: "The World Cup was a couple of months ago, but I've put in a lot of work since then. It was more about balancing my time off and not having too much of a break.

‌



"So, I took seven days off and then I started to train again. I'm just trying to come back in good shape so I'm on top of my game."

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Saka's stunning hat-trick in the electric 6-4 third-place play-off victory over France in Miami ignited the fire within his belly for the new season. It's partially why he refused to take his foot off the gas, especially as his condition gradually improved during the World Cup.

He admits it was a challenging and mentally-taxing summer, so much so that he reported back to London Colney for pre-season training two days early. The tricky dribbler continued: "Yeah, it was [difficult].

"It didn't necessarily go how I wanted it to. Myself and for the team as well. But, yeah, I put the World Cup behind me mentally and just worked on the team."

‌



Arsenal are now reaping the rewards of his hunger, and he has one mission on his mind: retaining the club's domestic crown. Saka said: "That's the mindset. We want to do it again, and we're going to give our best."

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka rifled in Arsenal's second goal against Coventry

After Mikel Arteta's Gunners netted all three goals from open play, the efficient right-winger was quizzed on whether we are going to see 'a more attacking Arsenal' this season.

‌



The England international responded sternly: "I don't like this narrative, to be honest. I think it's a great start for the team. We played beautiful football and we scored, what the game required. Sometimes it's a set piece, sometimes it's open play. It's about winning and that's what matters."

Saka knew there was somebody special waiting for him as soon as he left the field. It was his close friend, Ezri Konsa. The pair have struck a unique bond while playing together for England - Konsa even FaceTimed Saka from Aston Villa's open-top bus Europa League parade - and now they are team-mates at club level.

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka (right) and Ezri Konsa (left) are close friends

‌



The 28-year-old centre-back has joined the Gunners in a deal worth an initial £51million plus £4m in add-ons and was in attendance to watch Arsenal romp their way to victory while securing the first of many clean sheets this season.

Saka can't wait to see Konsa pull on the red and white shirt. He said when asked to explain their bromance: "I don't know how to describe it, man. Ever since I met him at England, we've just got on.

"Yeah, I'm so happy to have him here. Not only because he's a brother to me, but I know the level of player he is and I'm excited for him to show it at this level."

Sports.title: 14 wonderkids to keep an eye on this season including Man Utd and Chelsea gems
Sports.content:
14 wonderkids to keep an eye on this season including Man Utd and Chelsea gems

We're taking at look 14 wonderkids who could be about to take English football by storm

View 9 Images Tottenham's Luca Williams-Barnett is one of 14 wonderkids to watch out for this season (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

There is nothing in football quite like the sudden, electrifying emergence of a teenage prodigy. Big-money marquee transfers might dominate the summer back pages and social media feeds, but nothing gets fans off their seats faster than watching a kid who technically still needs a lift to training casually nutmeg an international defender.

‌



As the 2026/27 campaign kicks off, a fresh wave of absurd talent is threatening to smash open the breakwall. From viral 15-year-olds making non-competitive senior debuts to tactical wildcards ready to snatch a spot in their respective starting XIs, these young guns are no longer waiting politely in line for their turn.

‌



Old Trafford, Stamford Bridge, Anfield and beyond are packed with frighteningly good academy gems, and managers across the top flight are running out of excuses to keep them on the bench. With that in mind, Mirror Football takes a look at 14 wonderkids primed to steal the show this season.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Premier League odds as top four favourites emerge and Newcastle most backed for relegation READ MORE :

Harry Kane performs u-turn on Premier League return as stunning transfer plotted READ MORE :

Trey Nyoni, 19, Liverpool

Nyoni is entering his fourth season in and around the Liverpool first team - remarkable for a player who only turned 19 at the end of June. Much to the frustration of many Liverpool fans, many of whom felt he deserved more of an opportunity, Nyoni amounted only 237 minutes of first team football across 14 appearances in all competitions last season.

However, Nyoni has been one of Liverpool's stand-out players across pre-season and will likely feature much more regularly in the Reds' first team.

‌



View 9 Images Trey Nyoni is looking to build on his six Premier League appearances last season (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Ethan Nwaneri, 19, Arsenal

Nwaneri is an interesting case, as the midfielder made his Premier League debut almost four years ago away to Brentford, but he is still just 19 years of age. Nwaneri has shown flashes of brilliance, notably his wondergoal in Arsenal's 5-1 thrashing of Manchester City in February 2025.

However, after limited first-team opportunities in the first half of last season, he found himself on loan at Marseille in search of more first-team football. It was underwhelming to say the least, with the then-Marseille manager Habib Beye questioning Nwaneri's commitment and attitude. Nwaneri's potential is undeniable, but this season will be hugely significant in determining his trajectory.

‌



View 9 Images Ethan Nwaneri will be eager to capitalise on his loan spell at Marseille (Image: Getty )

Shea Lacey, 19, Manchester United

Throughout his young career, Lacey arguably has not had the rub of the green. Injury troubles have prevented him from getting more first-team experience, his cameo against Brighton in the FA Cup was cut short by two yellow cards - deemed by interim manager Darren Fletcher to be 'poor refereeing' - and the crossbar denied him a magical winner away against Burnley in January.

Nonetheless, Lacey has talent and confidence in abundance and will seek to demonstrate this season why United have such high expectations for him.

‌



View 9 Images Shea Lacey is highly-rated at Man Utd (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Brian Madjo, 17, Aston Villa

The six-foot-four London-born striker was acquired by Villa for a £10million fee in January and has thoroughly impressed throughout pre-season, having scored four goals, including a brace against Walsall for the claret and blue side.

His registration was a source of dispute between Villa and FIFA and after Villa's appeal was upheld by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, Madjo has been cleared to be registered and can now play competitively, which serves a huge boost for Unai Emery's Aston Villa side.

‌



View 9 Images Brian Madjo could make a serious splash this season (Image: Getty Images)

Luca Williams-Barnett, 17, Tottenham Hotspur

Labelled a 'precious diamond' and a 'special player' by Tottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi, Williams-Barnett is certainly a player to keep an eye on in the upcoming season.

He registered six goals and five assists in ten games in the Premier League 2 after his promotion from the Under-18s side, and the 26/27 season could offer the forward an opportunity to demonstrate his talent on a more regular basis in the Tottenham first-team.

‌



Ryan McAidoo, 18, Manchester City

View 9 Images Ryan McAidoo is looking to follow in the footsteps of the likes of Phil Foden and Cole Palmer (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Last year's Premier League Young Player of the Year, Nico O'Reilly, is a Manchester City academy product and McAidoo is the latest talent to emerge.

McAidoo was awarded his debut last season in City's 10-1 battering of Salford in the FA Cup and having thoroughly impressed new manager Enzo Maresca - who labelled him the 'kind of winger I love' - after City's friendly against Inter Milan, McAidoo is certainly one to watch.

‌



Dastan Satpayev, 18, Chelsea (on loan at Burnley)

Satpayev is a Kazakhstani forward, who has signed for Chelsea this summer from Kairat Almaty. He scored seven goals in fifteen appearances in Kazakhstan's Premier Liga this season and scored his first Champions League goal against Copenhagen back in November. He has been sent out on loan to Burnley for the season, though, so he won't play Premier League football.

Sean Steur, 18, Newcastle

Newcastle acquired the teenager from Ajax for a fee of around £23m this summer, despite Ajax's eagerness for Steur to stay. A product of the infamous Ajax academy, Steur made 25 first-team appearances last season. Replacing the outgoing Sandro Tonali, Steur has big boots to fill, but his talents would suggest he could well live up to such expectations.

JJ Gabriel, 15, Manchester United

View 9 Images JJ Gabriel is being tipped for the very top (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Fifteen?! Fifteen?! Last season, Arsenal's Max Dowman served to demonstrate that if you are good enough, you are old enough and Gabriel is widely tipped to be the next player to prove such a hypothesis.

Having gone viral as 'Kid Messi' over six years ago on several SV2 YouTube videos, Gabriel's progression has continued to soar and he recently made his non-competitive debut against Atletico Madrid. Fans should always be careful not to place too much expectation on someone so young, but it cannot be denied that Gabriel could well be a generational talent.

Veljko Milosavljevic, 19, Bournemouth

Bournemouth are not unfamiliar with possessing young talent in their ranks. Eli Junior Kroupi and Rayan, both 20 years of age, had the highest increases in market value in the Premier League last season, with Alex Scott, 22, also having stamped his authority on the league.

‌



So keep an eye on young Serbian centre back Milosavljevic, who signed in 2025 from Red Star Belgrade for £13m. His season was cut short in January by a knee injury, confining him to seven Premier League appearances, but the returning Serbian may prove to be another wise Bournemouth acquisition.

Joshua Abe, 16, Liverpool

View 9 Images Joshua Abe has been turning heads at just 16 (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

Before signing his scholarship at Liverpool this summer, Abe was the source of widespread interest from a number of clubs. The highly rated young winger only turned 16 back in July, but was a feature of Liverpool's pre-season squad, and was awarded a start against Wrexham in New York.

‌



Braiden Graham, 18, Everton

Everton have not been overly active so far in the transfer market, and with first-team strikers Beto and Thierno Barry both serving as very hit or miss, an opportunity could be afforded to young centre forward Graham. Shortlisted for the 25/26 Premier League 2 Player of the Season, Graham netted 12 times for the Toffees' Under-21s side.

George Hemmings, 19, Aston Villa

Morgan Rogers has left Villa Park, but in pre-season, it seems another gem has been unearthed. George Hemmings, who joined Villa's academy from Nottingham Forest in 2024, has looked at home in the first team and shone during the Super Cup defeat to PSG. Much like Madjo, he could play a role under Unai Emery this season.

View 9 Images George Hemmings looks a star in the making (Image: Getty)

‌



Josh King, 19, Fulham

Fulham and King felt hard done by when his first Premier League goal was harshly ruled out against Chelsea last season, but that first goal finally came against Burnley in March.

King's performances were rewarded by Thomas Tuchel, who took him to the US in England's pre-tournament squad. Fulham's loss of Harry Wilson may offer King a more established role in Fulham's starting eleven. Regardless, you can expect King to continue to progress.

Sports.title: Humbled on Humberside! Lacklustre Man Utd stunned by brilliant Hull
Sports.content:
A lacklustre Man Utd were left stunned as they slipped to a 2-0 defeat to newly-promoted Hull City in their Premier League season opener at the MKM Stadium.

There was plenty of optimism around United, who finished last season strongly under Michael Carrick, heading into the season, but that bubble was quickly burst in Hull as Semi Ajayi capitalised on defensive issues (17) to poke home the opener from close range.

Image: Semi Ajayi fires Hull into the lead against Manchester United

In an interview before the game, Hull owner Acun Ilicali revelled in the fact everyone was writing his side off this season and backed by a buoyant atmosphere, the Tigers played with real confidence. Physically, Man Utd struggled to cope with the intensity Hull were playing at.

Every time Hull went forward, Man Utd looked unsure at the back, and the pressure eventually told again as Nobel Mendy powered a header past Senne Lammens to double the lead (38).

Carrick sent for Marcus Rashford for the second half - his first competitive appearance for United in 618 days - but the England forward's introduction didn't have the desired impact.

Image: Second-half substitute Marcus Rashford appeals for a decision

Man Utd's only real chance in the second half came through Bryan Mbeumo, but his shot was was well saved by goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

In reality, United hardly laid a glove on Hull, who looked comfortable as they cruised to a victory that leaves Carrick already looking for answers, with Sky Sports readers calling for defensive reinforcements with around 10 days remaining in the transfer window.

Your views: Same old Man Utd...

Image: Burno Fernandes shows his disappointment after Manchester United fall 2-0 behind at Hull

Clive228: Until Manchester United sign better defenders then they will not make progress. This obsession with signing midfielders and strikers when our defence is broken is ridiculous. We should be going all out and bringing in Quansah.

Tom: Michael Carrick won't last six months if this carries on.

Adam Probert: Hull have been unbelievable, but same old Man Utd.

Rambo741: Manchester United must splash the cash on a top central defender and full backs. That was awful.

GDM: The quality of defenders at Man Utd will cost Carrick his job this season.

Tom: I told you. False dawn for Man Utd. Embarrassing.

Dan: Different season, same story for Man Utd. Problems are never fixed at this club. Michael Carrick is already under massive pressure.

Ethan: Credit to Hull but as a United fan this story is a common theme. No backing in the window and then we struggle throughout the league against not as good teams. It is going to be a tough couple of months.

The key moments from the MKM Stadium

Image: Nobel Mendy celebrates after doubling Hull's lead against Manchester United

13: SAVE! Tzolakis is forced into action, pulling off a one-handed save to keep out Mbeumo's half-volley.

15: SAVE! With the game opening up, Lammens dives at full stretch to push away McBurnie's header.

17: GOAL! Lift-off for Hull on their Premier League return as Ajayi scores from close range to give them the lead.

38: GOAL! More defensive problems for Man Utd as Mendy's header doubles Hull's lead before the break.

46: SUB! Rashford replaces Dorgu at half time to make his first competitive appearance for United in 618 days.

78: SAVE! Man Utd's only real chance of the second half through Mbeumo on the break, but Tzolakis stands up to keep out the winger's shot.

Sports.title: Lincoln beaten by Portsmouth as second-tier football returns to Sincil Bank
Sports.content:
Portsmouth claimed their first win of the Championship season with a comprehensive 3-1 success at Lincoln.

Pompey, who had lost their first two games of the campaign by the same scoreline, found themselves under the cosh early on, but a seventh-minute goal from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen put them in the driving seat.

Adrian Segecic doubled the lead nine minutes later before Reeco Hackett pulled one back from the spot for the Imps just past the half-hour mark.

Substitute Ebrima Adams then made the game safe with a superb strike after 69 minutes to leave Lincoln still searching for their first win back in the second tier for more than 60 years.

Image: Ryan Kavuma-McQueen celebrates after opening the scoring for Portsmouth at Lincoln

The Imps started well and were awarded a free-kick just outside the box inside two minutes, with Adam Reach's effort tipped over by Portsmouth goalkeeper Nicolas Schmid.

After Ivan Varfolomeev's initial corner was cleared behind, his second set-piece delivery was met by skipper Tendayi Darikwa, whose first-time effort was deflected away for another corner.

Freddie Draper then put Ben House through on goal, but the City frontman's shot lacked power and Schmid was able to save comfortably.

Portsmouth hit Lincoln with a seventh-minute sucker-punch, scoring with their very first attack.

The ball found Kavuma-McQueen on the left side of the City box and he arrowed a low effort straight into the bottom corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 17-year-old Ryan Kavuma-McQueen fires Portsmouth into the lead against Lincoln City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Adrian Segecic scores a superb free-kick for Portsmouth against Lincoln City in the Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ebou Adams unleashes a superb long-range strike to put Portsmouth 3-1 ahead against Lincoln City.

Colby Bishop's looping header was gathered by Imps keeper George Wickens before Segecic doubled Pompey's lead after 16 minutes.

The Australian schemer smacked a bullet of a free-kick past Wickens with his left foot from the edge of the box to make it 2-0.

Hackett reduced the arrears from the penalty spot after 32 minutes after Reach's 20-yard effort was adjudged to have been handled by Zak Swanson as he attempted to block the shot.

Hackett and Varfolomeev both dragged efforts wide before Wickens had to be alert at the other end to push a Bishop strike out for a corner.

Darikwa was forced off with a knee injury 10 minutes into the second half, which meant a home debut for City's record signing Andrei Coubis.

Wickens blocked Bishop's shot in the first meaningful attack of the second period around the hour mark as both sides struggled to carve out opportunities as the sun shone brightly at the ProAmpac Stadium.

It took one of the Pompey subs to light the match up when Adams was given far too much space in the middle of the pitch and he strode forward and unleashed a stunning 25-yard strike past Wickens after 69 minutes.

Segecic nearly made it four five minutes from time, but his low shot was saved by Wickens.

Sports.title: Promising signs for new England but Pakistan absolutely dire
Sports.content:
Joe Root's return match as England Test captain could hardly have gone better - a three-day win and a weekend off.

The fact that fast bowler Josh Tongue had the opportunity to focus on his beloved Manchester United's Saturday-lunchtime Premier League opener against Hull City owed much to England's excellence but more so Pakistan's ineptitude.

A game that started on Wednesday was done before tea on Friday. Had rain not fallen across the first two days, it could conceivably have concluded on Thursday evening.

As a result, there are similarities between this England reset and the one they had at the start of the summer against New Zealand at Lord's, in that the speed of the game rendered it hard to assess how much progress had actually been made.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer claimed the final wicket as England thrashed Pakistan in Leeds to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series

Against the Black Caps in June, in the last knockings of Bazball, the poor pitch was chiefly to blame for the Test lasting only 166 overs. At Headingley this week, Pakistan's lack of quality was a key factor in the game being over in 175.3.

This Leeds deck was a good one. It was how Pakistan batted and bowled on in that was the problem, allied with how they fielded. The tourists had a shocker on all three fronts.

That has to be a caveat when it comes to assessing England but Pakistan's myriad issues should not entirely detract from a fine performance from the home side.

What did we learn from England in Leeds?

While too early to make sweeping calls about this new England - the permanent coach, Stephen Fleming, is not even in the country yet, although did chat to Root on the phone during the Headingley Test - there were a few learnings. Root's captaincy for one.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain and Stuart Broad were impressed with Root's return to captaincy

The Yorkshireman had been left broken at the end of his first stint in the role, as the losses totted up and he had to navigate Covid bubbles, but he looked refreshed and revitalised on his home ground as he chalked up a record-extending 28th win in charge.

Switching from slip to mid-off allowed him to be closer to his bowlers, while a switch from mid-off to leg slip at one point paid off as he caught Azan Awais off Jofra Archer.

We also saw a ruthless streak when Root withdrew Archer from the attack on day one after two unimpactful overs with the new ball. There was much to admire as Root made tactical tweaks but did not try to lead like predecessor Ben Stokes.

We also saw a maturity in Harry Brook's batting with the vice-captain parking the dancing down the wicket and the falling-over scoops to play in a more orthodox, restrained manner. There was no need for any "rash shots", he later told Sky Sports.

Brook simply waited for Pakistan to bowl a bad ball - and, boy, did they bowl lots of those - rather than attempt to force the issue. If he can mix that measured approach with his breath-taking talent going forward, there is no limit on what he could achieve.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook speaks to Sky Sports after his 91 at Headingley and if he wants to be England Test captain in future

England were assured with the bat as a whole. No Bazball going on here. Just positive, clinical strokeplay, against an admittedly powderpuff and profligate attack.

We discovered that England have depth in their middle-order batting with Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence scoring sprightly half-centuries after replacing Jacob Bethell (injured) and Stokes (retired) in the side - Cox, especially, looks at home at this level.

Unfortunately, Pakistan wilting twice means we did not learn whether having Lawrence as the main spin option around a four-pronged pace attack is the way England should look to replace Stokes long term. Lawrence only bowled one over in the game.

The success of the pace quartet - Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue, Archer and Gus Atkinson - makes it unlikely a frontline spinner will be picked for the second Test.

Plus, would selecting one actually weaken England in that their best bowlers are their quicks? A spinner would improve the over rate, for sure, but perhaps not much else.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Urooj Mumtaz was disappointed with Pakistan's performance in Leeds, saying the tourists lacked discipline and skill

Poor Pakistan look set for long series

What we learned most of all, though, is that this Pakistan side is not very good.

Yes, they were missing captain and best batter Babar Azam due to a hand injury and had the misfortune of losing the toss to be stuck in on day one under leaden skies.

And, yes, this is Pakistan so a rousing comeback from nowhere should not be completely discounted. They have done it plenty of times in the past.

But that feels fanciful right now with the batting line-up not accustomed to English conditions, the bowling attack lacking venom and the fielding at Headingley appalling.

The lack of Pakistan fans in the ground was also extremely disappointing and probably speaks volumes for the connection they have with this team at the moment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pakistan were on the back foot from the first ball of the opening Test when Azan Awais was pinned lbw by Ollie Robinson

It could be a long series for Pakistan - and a very short one in terms of how many days of cricket we actually see. England winning well inside the distance at Lord's and Edgbaston appears the likely outcome here, provided the rain holds off.

Babar's return will bolster the batting but there is no mystery or express pace to the bowling, traits that Pakistan have been famous for producing in the past, through Wasim Akram, Waqar Younis, Shoaib Akhtar, Saeed Ajmal, Abdul Qadir et al. It's all too samey.

Resets have been England's thing of late. Maybe it is time for Pakistan to undergo one, having lost 14 of their last 19 Tests.

Everyone loves a weekend off, although you suspect Pakistan won't be enjoying theirs, after a match that could hardly have gone worse.

Sports.title: ​​​​​Russell wins Dutch Sprint to trim title gap to Antonelli
Sports.content:
George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint to maintain his perfect start to Formula 1's return to action and trim his championship deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

The polesitting Russell held the lead from Lando Norris at the start and and withstood an initial challenge from his fellow Briton before the McLaren fell into the clutches of Charles Leclerc's Ferrari behind.

Despite being on the more brittle soft tyres compared to the mediums of those around him, Leclerc overtook Norris for second with an impressive move into the first corner on lap 18 of the short-form contest.

But Norris was at least able to hold off Antonelli for third, the championship leader having taken fourth from the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri on the first lap.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell keeps lead in the Sprint at the Dutch Grand Prix as Lando Norris holds off Charles Leclerc.

While Russell is now 56 points back on his team-mate after victory, Antonelli's overall championship lead has extended to 53 points after Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished where he qualified in seventh.

A downpour arrived just as Russell was taking the chequered flag for his third Sprint win of the season with the Mercedes driver admitting the final tour would have been "very sketchy" had the rain arrived any earlier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc overtakes Lando Norris in a 'BEAUTIFUL' move to take second place

Fifth-placed Piastri finished with home favourite Max Verstappen right on his tail.

Hamilton, though, was 1.6s back on Verstappen in seventh and will now hope for sufficiently better over the rest of race weekend after being unhappy with his set-up into Sprint Qualifying.

Pierre Gasly took the final point on offer in the Sprint with eighth for Alpine.

The Zandvoort weekend is now effectively reset with teams able to make changes to their cars ahead of Grand Prix Qualifying at 3pm later on Saturday, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event.

Dutch GP Sprint Result: Top 8 1) George Russell, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Lando Norris, McLaren



4) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



5) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



6) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



7) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



8) Pierre Gasly, Alpine

Russell maintains 'great start' to F1's resumption

Having seemingly got his inconsistent championship challenge against Antonelli back on track at the start of July when he reduced his title deficit to 25 points, Russell dropped 34 points further to his team-mate in the space of the final two race weeks before F1's summer break.

So a fast start to F1's return at Zandvoort was therefore imperative for the 28-year-old, which he has managed to deliver so far.

"A great start to the weekend," said Russell. "The Ferraris look really fast, so it's going to be a tight one this afternoon [in Qualifying].

"I knew if there were going to be any overtakes, they were going to be towards the end of the race. So, I knew I just wanted to manage my tyres a bit through the high-speed corners and have a bit more in the tank come the end of the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch George Russell win the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint, as Lando Norris loses second place to Charles Leclerc.

"I knew if Charles got past Lando at all, he would be fast. As soon as I saw Charles behind, I dropped the hammer a little bit and the two of us pulled away."

Norris, the dominant race winner last time out in Hungary, had initially looked a threat to Russell himself but he was reeled in and eventually overtaken by Leclerc.

"Not a bad result, not the best. Would have been nice to have been a little bit faster today, but Charles was just too quick," he said.

"I don't think it was the tyres, just that we lacked pace. We're not quick enough and we have some work to do."

Leclerc said: "I knew Lando didn't have much deployment on the main straight so I knew I had to maximise that but we still arrived at the braking point more or less at the same level and it worked out."
