Sports.title: Antonelli to take Monza grid penalty for engine change
Sports.content:
World championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed.

Each driver is permitted a capped amount of various power unit parts for the season, and two separate technical issues for Antonelli have left Mercedes resigned to the fact the Italian will need to exceed the limit before the end of the campaign.

If possible, teams will generally choose to incur grid penalties at tracks where overtaking is easier, which is why Mercedes are set to install a new power unit for Antonelli at his home race in Monza from September 4-6.

Antonelli, who turns 20 on Tuesday, holds a 53-point lead over Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton at the top of the drivers' standings after extending his advantage over the Brit by finishing fourth in the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint on Saturday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli gained a place at the start of the Dutch GP Sprint

Looking ahead to the rest of Antonelli's weekend as he spoke to Sky Sports F1 after the Sprint in Zandvoort, Wolff said: "We need big points.

"Kimi is going to probably lose some in Monza starting in the back, so hopefully we can pocket some here."

George Russell, who reduced his championship deficit to his team-mate Antonelli to 56 points by winning Saturday's Sprint, is in a similar position in terms of power unit parts used and is expected to need to incur a penalty before the end of the season.

Neither Mercedes nor Russell have yet to offer any indication as to where the Brit will take his penalty.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli suffered a nervy moment as he went off into the gravel during SQ1 at the Dutch Grand Prix

The severity of Antonelli's punishment in Monza will depend on how many different parts Mercedes install, given he is one away from breaching the limit for several elements.

The penalty will be a minimum of 10 places, but if multiple parts are installed Antonelli could be consigned to starting at the back of the grid regardless of where he qualifies.

Before the start of the Sprint, Antonelli's father Marco had hinted to Sky Sports F1 that his son would be taking a penalty in Monza.

Antonelli snr said: "Monza we will see. It will be difficult, for sure - for a lot of reasons."

Sports.title: Andy Burnham says he wants to bring men’s World Cup back to UK in 2042
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham has said he wants to bring the men’s World Cup to the UK in 2042, returning the tournament to Britain for the first time in almost eight decades.

At a meeting in No 10 North in Manchester on Friday, the prime minister told regional mayors he was keen for the tournament to be played in the British Isles.

When the 1966 World Cup took place in England, with the home side beating West Germany 4-2 in the final after extra time, it was the only time the country has either hosted or won the contest.

Burnham, a keen football fan who has a season ticket at Everton, said earlier this month that it was “insane” only one World Cup had been held anywhere in the UK.

It is understood a formal application to stage the competition could also involve other home nations, none of which have ever hosted any World Cup games.

In recent years, joint bids between countries for major football tournaments have become more common. Alongside the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will host the men’s European championships in 2028.

A Downing Street source said: “We support the FA’s priorities in terms of the tournaments they are already hosting, and any others they’d like to bid for.

“It would always be great to host more tournaments. These are broad aspirations – it’s a general ambition. The prime minister is a sports fan and loves his football.”

England made a doomed bid to host the 2018 World Cup, which was awarded to Russia amid allegations of corruption.

In 2014, while serving in the shadow cabinet, Burnham said he was uncomfortable that the tournament was still allowed to take place in Russia after its annexation of Crimea.

Under Fifa regulations, no European country would be eligible to stage the World Cup until 2042.

In 2000, Fifa introduced rules that meant the tournament would be rotated around its six continental confederations. It led to South Africa hosting its first World Cup in 2010, but the strict system was scrapped in October 2007.

Nations are not allowed to bid to stage a World Cup if either of the previous two tournaments have taken place on the same continent.

The 2030 World Cup will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with some early matches taking place in South America to mark the tournament’s centenary. The first World Cup was played in Uruguay in 1930.

Fifa has also confirmed that the 2034 tournament will take place in Saudi Arabia. The location of the 2038 World Cup has not yet been announced, but under the rules, games are likely to be played in North America or Oceania, which includes Australia and New Zealand.

At Friday’s meeting, Burnham is also understood to have spoken about the possibility of hosting the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the north of England in the 2040s.

Earlier this year, under the previous prime minister, Keir Starmer, UK Sport was commissioned to assess whether a bid would be viable.

It is understood that the government is considering the possibility of a “multi-city bid” in an attempt to spread any economic benefit between several northern cities.

Sports.title: Fifa general secretary Mattias Grafström sounded out about standing against Infantino
Sports.content:
Senior figures in African football have held talks with Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, to sound out his interest in standing against Gianni Infantino, the Guardian can reveal.

As many as 15 federations in Africa are also said to be ready to turn their backs on Infantino when he seeks re-election as Fifa president next year, despite the Confederation of Africa Football (Caf) claiming that its executive committee (exco) had “unanimously reconfirmed” its support for the under-fire 56-year-old.

Grafström initially distanced himself from Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), with the second-in-command of world football’s governing body telling staff that “individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go” in a memo three days after the plan to sell off 20% of the World Cup’s commercial rights was abandoned. The 45-year-old Swede has since fallen into line, having signed a letter of “full support” for Infantino 24 hours later before informing employees in an email that chief operating officer Kevin Lamour – who heavily criticised the FFE proposal – had been sacked.

But it is understood that Grafström’s initial opposition to the controversial plans encouraged some of Infantino’s opponents in Africa to attempt to gauge his willingness to stand against him in next year’s election. Two presidents of African federations spoke to Grafström on the phone separately last week, although he is said to have been surprised to be approached and was non-committal either way at this stage.

“They think that Matthias can group all the continents together and then go forward,” a source who is a member of the exco told the Guardian. “I don’t know what his position is right now but if he can bring all these people together then he would get some support. Matthias is a very open-minded guy and he always listens to what we think.”

Grafström, who did not respond to the Guardian’s request for comment, was appointed as Fifa’s permanent general secretary in May 2024 after previously serving in an interim role and has worked closely with Caf and some African federations over the past two years, although it remains to be seen if he emerges as a rival for the presidency.

Caf has traditionally been a stronghold for Infantino but it is understood that discontent has been growing in several countries after the decision to only stage the Africa Cup of Nations every four years rather than two that many believe was imposed on them by Fifa at the end of last year.

Multiple sources have told the Guardian that only four of the 21 exco members publicly declared their support for Infantino at their most recent meeting on 7 August, including Caf president, Patrice Motsepe, and vice-president, Fouzi Lekjaa, from Morocco. “The rest remained silent,” said one who attended the meeting. “People don’t want to give their views in public because they are waiting to see what happens.”

With 54 members in total, Africa could hold the key to attempts to unseat Infantino given that any opponent would require 106 of the 211 Fifa members to vote against him. Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al-Khalifa, the president of the Asian Football Confederation, which has voiced its opposition to Infantino in alliance with Uefa and Concacaf, is also believed to still have significant support from within Africa having lost to Infantino in the 2015 elections. “If Salman is coming for sure he’s going to be elected,” the source added. “If Europe will give him support, he will get the support from Asia, he will get support from Concacaf. And he will get some support from Africa. For sure, 10 to 15 people will vote for Salman.”

But any prospective opponents to Infantino have been warned they will have to show their support for football on the continent by coming up with a similar plan to FFE, which it was hoped would result in around $20m a year being given to each association.

“If Uefa or anyone else has something better, they should propose it – if anyone has anything better than Infantino then people will vote for them,” said the exco member. “If someone will come and say, ‘OK we are going to have an agreement with Uefa that means we support poor countries so we can build good infrastructures there’ then they will support him.”

Sports.title: Martin Ødegaard resumes his role as Arsenal’s smoothing agent and pass master | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
We’re back, baby. Welcome to the content zone. And yes, we did actually go away for a bit. Seriously. Check back. We really did.

In the lead-up to this Premier League opener, Sky Sports had been trailing the fact it will show a total of 1,500 live games this season. Lay these end-to-end and that adds up to about 3,000 hours, or 125 whole days doing nothing but watching football. Chuck in the endless over-gorge of clips, highlights, noises off, VAR rage, furious punditry shemozzles, and that’s pretty much the next eight months spent slumped in your memory foam chair, cramming in those great dripping handfuls of sweet, sweet football-derived product.

For Arsenal’s supporters, on this evidence at least, it might just be a slightly easier experience this time around. They say retaining a title is never easy. Well winning it wasn’t exactly painless either. But how do you manage that altered gravity? On the one hand there’s the Roy Keane approach, performative hunger, serial victory as an act of self-harm. Win the league, stab yourself in the leg, and win it again.

Does hunger matter so much with the game so mechanised, a matter of patterns, systems, processed movements? For Arsenal it is more a case of finding other rhythms and deeper gears. Even before this straightforward 3-0 defeat of Coventry, the goal was clear enough. Win the league, but win it better. Make these games less interesting, or at least less painful.

Well, stage one complete. Two things happened here. First, Arsenal won this game as comfortably as any in the last two seasons. This was like watching a team in demo mode, just trying out the new software, revving the throttle in neutral. And second, Martin Ødegaard played, once again, a little bit more like the half-remembered Martin Ødegaard: 75 minutes, 72 touches, 55 short, clipped little passes. And this is significant.

In the absence of a headline attacking signing, attention has fixed on Ødegaard and the chance he can become himself again after the injury-addled figure of last season. At his best he is just such a constant ferret, a press machine, master of space and of the nudged pass, the look of a thrusting young corporate actuary and the feet of a cage-ball urchin.

Ødegaard’s goal here was the obvious headline moment, Arsenal’s third on 48 minutes. In the moment of execution it felt like a fun and slightly silly thing, the kind of goal Prince Edward might have scored in It’s A Knockout in 1981, set up by Brian Blessed, Emu in goal. But the move to get there was the real deal.

The Norwegian made it in the way he likes to make things, driving the move from just behind the attacking line, twitching the threads. There was a nice delayed pass to Ben White, a drift into space. The finish was comical. Ødegaard sometimes has a strange way of shooting, sidling up to the ball, his foot connecting at an odd angle, a kind of power-stub. Here he miskicked in front of goal, but still sent the ball floating weirdly to the left of Carl Rushworth, who clawed at it helplessly, like a cat flapping its paw at a shadow on the wall.

View image in fullscreen Myles Lewis-Skelly impressed again in midfield. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images

Ødegaard laughed as he wheeled away. But the celebration was real. This was his first goal at the Emirates since last December. And either side there were signs of something else too, a reawakening of the link-up with Bukayo Saka. Just before half-time they pinged the ball between each other six or seven times, eventually finding space for Declan Rice to shoot just wide. This was like old times. Here they are, the guys, with something between them that is genuinely rare in elite teams: a sense of play, invention, pleasure in the connection.

North London had been agreeably crisp and even a little chilly at kick-off. As a contest, Arsenal-Coventry has Classic Barclays energy: Darren Huckerby running the channels, your TV screen making whooshing noises, Richard Keys with a filthy late-August tan, lemon-yellow blazer sleeves hitched up.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Frank Lampard and Mikel Arteta were up on their feet from the start in identical outfits – black slacks, black knitted mock-turtleneck, white soled black trainers – like the advance party for an executive ninja golf day. And the opening goal on 15 minutes was a high-end three-beat move.

First, Christos Tzolis block-tackled the ball back off Milan van Ewijk by the right touchline, then fed it to Riccardo Calafiori. His pass across the front of the penalty area was pinged hard and low through a narrow arc to Kai Havertz. The finish was luxurious, a first-time left-foot volley so relaxed you half-expected to look down and notice Havertz was playing in a pair of tailored leather parlour slippers.

It was 2-0 soon afterwards, as Coventry found themselves overwhelmed, up against something quicker, slicker and more smoothly geared than many of these players will have ever come up against. This was a good Rice moment, his forward run the catalyst. But it was also an Ødegaard moment, a quick little nudged pass making the space for the shift wide and the killer cross. This is what Ødegaard does best, the pass that makes the pass, the smoothing agent, footballing WD-40.

Equally important, perhaps, Myles Lewis-Skelly was also excellent here, tigerish and always involved, barely misplacing a pass. And yes, he was excellent against the champions of the Championship, but he was also excellent in his last game, against the champions of Europe. Who knows, maybe he’s just a really good midfielder.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi fined for slapping opposition player in MLS game
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has been fined for slapping an opponent during a Major League Soccer game. The 39-year-old Inter Miami forward lashed out at Quinn Sullivan of Philadelphia Union during their match on Wednesday, catching the midfielder around the back of the head.

The Argentinian appeared to be angry Sullivan had elbowed him after he had played the ball, with the referee intervening before the situation could escalate. The match at Subaru Park finished 2-2.

A statement on the competition’s website read: “The MLS disciplinary committee has fined Inter Miami CF forward Lionel Messi an undisclosed amount for violating the league’s policy regarding hands to the face/head/neck of an opponent in the 101st minute of Miami’s match against the Philadelphia Union on 19 August.”

A bad-tempered fixture finished with two late red cards as Miami’s Yannick Bright and Sullivan’s brother, Cavan, were dismissed in stoppage time. Miami’s Ian Fray has also been fined by the MLS for clashing with Sullivan.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Miami sit second in the Eastern Conference, seven points behind the leaders Nashville.

Sports.title: ‘See you at the hairdressers’: Infantino’s bizarre reply to bald reporter
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino told a reporter “I’ll see you at the hairdressers” after he was asked whether he had betrayed football over his aborted World Cup sell-off plan.

The Fifa president was stopped outside a hotel in the Dominican Republic by the Sky News US correspondent, James Matthews, who challenged the under-fire leader of football’s governing body over why he had not resigned, despite calls from across the game for him to step down.

Last week, three continental confederations accused the president of “deception” over his plans to secure private investment in Fifa tournaments, while the European governing body Uefa has threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions having “lost confidence” in his leadership.

Having tracked Infantino to a hotel in the Caribbean country where he has travelled to attend a youth tournament, Matthews, who shares Infantino’s recognisable bald pate, asked the 56-year-old whether he had “betrayed the game of football”, to which came the reply: “You have a nice haircut. Thank you so much.”

As the president walked away, Matthews continued: “Why won’t you resign? Fans, Fifa associations want you to step down. Why won’t you? Have you betrayed the trust of Fifa?”

As he stepped inside a waiting black car, Infantino replied: “I’ll see you at the hairdressers.”

Meanwhile, the Concacaf president Victor Montagliani has asked Infantino ⁠to stay away ​from the youth tournament, saying his presence would overshadow the event. ​Infantino, who could potentially face a vote ‌of no confidence from ‌world football’s regional powerhouses, is visiting the Dominican Republic this weekend and was reportedly planning to ‌attend a competition organised by the Caribbean Football Union (CFU).

In a letter sent to Infantino on Friday, and seen by Reuters, Montagliani cited the “governance crisis surrounding Fifa” as reason for its president to reconsider attending the CFU U-14 Series event.

“As you may be aware, your proposed attendance has garnered significant media attention,” Montagliani, who is also a vice-president ‌on the Fifa Council, wrote. “...the media will focus on this situation, which will unfortunately significantly take away from the technical nature of the CFU youth ​competition.

“As such, I respectfully ask you in the name of football to reconsider your attendance as it will unfortunately undermine the technical nature of this important youth development activity.“

Reuters has contacted Fifa for comment.

Infantino was received at Punta Cana by the Dominican Republic’s minister of sports, ⁠Kelvin Cruz. “We deeply appreciate your visit to the Dominican Republic, without doubt ​that your presence in our ​country puts us on the international ​football radar and opens us great prospects for growth and development of ​Dominican football,” Cruz ‌said in a ​statement.

Infantino is seeking a fourth term until 2031 but several national associations and key officials have withdrawn support for the Swiss administrator.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak braces himself for daunting reunion with Newcastle
Sports.content:
When Liverpool’s team bus turns a tight corner and inches down the narrow, covered, access road behind Newcastle’s Milburn Stand on Sunday, Alexander Isak will know there are no hiding places. After that coach pulls up, its occupants must navigate a set of painted steps before reaching the glass-doored sanctuary of the players’ entrance at St James’ Park. It is a short climb but only a handful of portable metal barriers separate visiting sides from congregated Newcastle fans. When particularly disliked opponents arrive, it can all feel loudly claustrophobic.

Once inside, Isak, who spent most of last summer staging a form of unilateral industrial action in order to force a £125m move from Tyneside to Merseyside, must negotiate a human chicane of once-familiar club staff stationed along the route to the away dressing room. If eye contact may be minimal, two factors should soften the pre-match mood surrounding his first return to St James’ Park. Eddie Howe has been replaced by Matthias Jaissle and the latest meeting between Newcastle and Liverpool will play out against an outpouring of love for Kevin Keegan, following his death in July.

Isak will find the pitch that was once his playground surrounded by tributes to a player and manager revered and adored by both clubs. Despite scoring 54 goals in 86 Premier League appearances for Newcastle, including the decisive goal in their 2025 Carabao Cup final triumph against Liverpool at Wembley, the Swede’s north-east legacy is very different. He can expect to feel the more feral side of the home crowd’s emotional power as they recall that, on the evening of 25 August last year, he remained locked inside his rented mansion in Northumberland. Barely 10 miles south, Newcastle lost 3-2 to Liverpool. By 1 September, Isak was shaking hands with Arne Slot and Mohamed Salah at Anfield.

View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak, pictured scoring Newcastle’s second, decisive strike in the 2025 Carabao Cup final, scored 54 league goals for the club but faces a frosty reception from fans. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images

His old friends on Tyneside would, rather like the protagonist in the William Hughes Mearns poem Antigonish, be subsequently haunted by images of “a man who wasn’t there” throughout a season when Newcastle finished a disappointing 12th in the league. Similarly, Isak’s less-than-ideal preparation during a summer when he skipped Newcastle’s pre-season tour of south east Asia ensured that he became a shadow of the striker Slot craved, let alone the teammate an ageing Salah needed. Granted, the broken leg he sustained in December further disrupted that maiden Liverpool campaign, but several parties involved in this most protracted and painful transfer lost an awful lot.

With Slot and Salah gone, Isak must now win over a new head coach in Andoni Iraola as he strives to recapture that extraordinary ability to glide gazelle-like across the pitch before sending a series of often first-time shots from sometimes improbable angles beyond assorted goalkeepers. Part of that imperious ability can be attributed to three years of stellar coaching as Howe refined the former Real Sociedad striker’s game to the point where even the very best defenders found Isak to be unplayable.

There were other occasions when he drifted to the margins rather than through the lines, and odd games when mysterious niggles sidelined him. But, until last July, the quiet 26-year-old appeared an unlikely rebel. Howe perhaps underestimated the immense determination of a player whose reserved demeanour he possibly mistook for malleability.

Isak certainly blindsided Newcastle when on 19 August last year he upstaged Salah at the Professional Football Association awards. The striker was a no-show at the ceremony and as the Egyptian collected his player of the year trophy, the audience were distracted by a barrage of vibrating phones. An Instagram message from Isak had accused Newcastle of breaking pledges to sell him. “When promises are broken and trust is lost, the relationship can’t continue,” he posted.

View image in fullscreen The manner of Alexander Isak’s departure from St James’ Park didn’t go down well with the Toon Army. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

As Howe denied offering a striker deeply disappointed not to be awarded a pay rise in 2024 an exit strategy, the club’s ownership appeared anxious to avoid the loss of face involved in permitting Liverpool to poach their prize possession. Newcastle’s oft-reiterated message was that Isak would eventually be “reintegrated” but things changed on the afternoon of 25 August when a delegation featuring senior figures from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) visited Isak’s home in well-heeled Darras Hall for conciliation talks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

They departed without any rapprochement and five days later the Germany forward Nick Woltemade joined Newcastle from Stuttgart for £69m. Forty-eight hours on, Isak was a Liverpool player, leaving Newcastle’s dressing room divided between those sympathetic to his decision to in effect go on strike and others, most notably Bruno Guimarães, who were outraged.

By then Hugo Ekitiké had also moved to Anfield for £69m from Eintracht Frankfurt. The French forward had been a long-term Howe target and the enduring puzzle about “Isakgate” is why Newcastle, then struggling to comply with football’s spending rules, did not sell Isak to Liverpool earlier in the summer, when Slot would subsequently have been unlikely to move for Ekitiké. Matters were complicated by Newcastle’s then outgoing chief executive, Darren Eales, being absent on medical leave and the lack of a sporting director after Paul Mitchell’s departure following a power struggle with Howe.

This vacuum promoted the manager’s nephew, Andy Howe, into a senior recruitment role as Newcastle reinvested £55m of the Isak money on Brentford’s Yoane Wissa. While knee trouble derailed Wissa’s season, Howe senior struggled to marry Woltemade’s talent to his tactics and the 24-year-old ended a dispiriting campaign failing to convince in central midfield. By then, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Guimarães were feeling disillusioned and also wanted out of St James’ Park. Having breached Uefa spending rules, Newcastle also needed to sell.

It all dictates that Isak is returning to a much-altered club at a moment when he needs to remind Liverpool precisely why so much drama was involved in him becoming the most expensive player in Premier League history.

Sports.title: Hull deliver brutal message to Man United fans over stadium PA system during shock win
Sports.content:
Hull deliver brutal message to Man United fans over stadium PA system during shock win

Manchester United's nightmare start to their Premier League season went from bad to worse on their way to defeat against Hull.

With the newly-promoted Tigers leading 2-0 as the game entered its final 15 minutes, the travelling Red Devils supporters then had insult added to injury by an announcement at the MKM Stadium.



4 Nobel Mendy's 38th-minute header put Hull 2-0 up and in dreamland against Man United Credit: Getty

4 An already-jubilant home crowd then cheered as the stadium announcer shared that trains to Manchester had been cancelled Credit: Getty

Already staring at a bleak journey home, the away fans were then informed that this was set to take them longer than planned.

The stadium announcer shared over the tannoy that 15.03 and 17.03 trains back to Manchester had been cancelled.



With a party atmosphere already building in Hull, the news sparked even more delight from their home fans, who erupted into cheers.

The taunts didn't stop there either, with the Tigers faithful brutally chanting: “You're going home in a taxi,” towards the United end.



Tough start

This capped off a miserable afternoon for Man United as their Premier League season began in disastrous fashion.

Michael Carrick's side had no answer to the fast start of Hull, who broke the deadlock after just 17 minutes when Semi Ajayi turned home from a corner after Senne Lammens denied Oli McBurnie's initial effort.



Making their Premier League return after a nine-year absence, this sparked bedlam at the MKM Stadium as Tigers fans delighted.

And their dream start soon got even better, as Nobel Mendy added a second with a powerful header on 38 minutes.

This was no less than Hull deserved, whose intensity and battling first-half display saw United struggle to conjure up any clear chances.

The Red Devils' poor first-half led head coach Carrick to call upon the returning Marcus Rashford, who was introduced at half-time to make his first competitive United appearance in 20 months.



4 Marcus Rashford endured a difficult return to action with United Credit: Getty

But the England star - now wearing the No.9 shirt - was unable to inspire a comeback, as a lacklustre United fell to a 2-0 defeat.

This sparked jubilant scenes from Hull's players and fans alike at the full-time whistle, as Sergej Jakirovic's side delivered an immediate message to those tipping them for relegation.

Meanwhile, United were handed a reality check as Michael Carrick's first game as permanent head coach ended in disappointing fashion.



It marked an unwanted first for the Red Devils, with the first time in their history they had lost on the opening day of a league season to a newly promoted side.

Smile for the camera

Worse still for the players, every unseen detail from the disappointing defeat is likely to have been captured by television cameras.

That is because United are set to be the next Premier League team to feature on an Amazon Prime 'All or Nothing' series.

4 Michael Carrick was given food for thought as his United side kicked off their season with a defeat Credit: Getty



Back in June, the club announced they had signed a record-breaking deal with the streaming giants, allowing cameras to follow them for an access-all-areas documentary covering the 2026/27 season.

Previous instalments of the series have focused on Premier League rivals Manchester City, Tottenham Hotspur and Arsenal.

And with all of their lowest points being documented in past seasons', fans can no doubt expect the Hull defeat to become a focal point of the upcoming docuseries.

Sports.title: Chelsea make Jamie Gittens decision as loan bid received before season opener
Sports.content:
Chelsea have rejected a loan offer from Roma for winger Jamie Gittens, talkSPORT understands.

Gittens was a bit-part player for the Blues in his debut campaign, having signed from Borussia Dortmund for £51.5million.

4 Jamie Gittens has been in resurgent form for Chelsea in pre-season Credit: Getty

The English winger made 27 appearances last term, scoring just once and providing five assists.

However, after emerging as a potential target for Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini, he now looks set to be given a second chance at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea are understood to have blocked the Italian giants' attempts to sign Gittens on loan, after he has impressed in pre-season.

The 22-year-old grabbed a goal and an assist under new manager Xabi Alonso in the Blues' tour of Asia and Australasia.

And talkSPORT understands Chelsea want Gittens to stay this season.

Despite shelling out over £300m this summer, the west London outfit could do with cover out wide.

British record signing Morgan Rogers is capable of playing on the left flank, while the Blues also have Pedro Neto and summer arrival Geovany Quenda.

Mykhailo Mudryk is also among Chelsea's options, who has recently been cleared to return to playing after his FA doping ban was resolved.

However, his future at Stamford Bridge is unclear, with an approach from Leeds to sign the Ukrainian on loan being rejected.

While the Blues appear keen to keep Mudryk too, the Whites are expected to return with another offer.

4 Gittens failed to score in the Premier League last season Credit: Getty

4 Gian Piero Gasperini's Roma are gearing up for Champions League football this season, and wanted to add Gittens to their ranks Credit: Getty

Fresh start?

Roma's attempt to sign Gittens isn't the first time this summer he has been linked with a move away from Stamford Bridge.

The England Under-21 international was recently linked with Fenerbahce, only for the Turkish giants to release a statement angrily denying these rumours.

Gittens endured a difficult start to life in the Premier League, as he struggled to make his mark following his big-money arrival from Germany.

In his 27 appearances last season, he only scored one goal and provided five assists across all competitions.

The forward's tough first year at Stamford Bridge was interrupted by injury, as he missed more than 100 days with a hamstring issue.

He sat out of 22 games for the Blues in total, with his last competitive appearance for the club coming on January 31.

4 Xabi Alonso would benefit from having Fernandez among his midfield options, insists Foster Credit: Getty

However, Gittens now looks set for a fresh start under new boss Alonso, who appears to be a fan of his.

The Spaniard played him in five of Chelsea's six pre-season friendlies this summer, and after Roma's approach was knocked back, the wideman could feature in Chelsea's Premier League opener against Fulham on Monday.

talkSPORT will have live coverage from Craven Cottage, with commentary coming from Sam Matterface and former England midfielder Danny Murphy.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi slapped with MLS fine after violating American league’s policy
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has been fined for slapping an opposing player during an MLS fixture.

The Inter Miami star appeared to lash out at Philadelphia Union’s Quinn Sullivan during the match between the two teams on Wednesday.

3 Lionel Messi was embroiled in a tense exchange with an opposing player on Wednesday Credit: Getty

Messi was infuriated after Sullivan appeared to elbow him after he had played the ball.

The pair became embroiled in a tense exchange during the second half of Wednesday's 2-2 draw.

Messi’s hand then appeared to make contact with Sullivan's face before referee Filip Dujic stepped in to try to settle the conflict.

The Argentine was lucky to escape without a booking at the time with the game quickly resuming.

But the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner was retrospectively sanctioned by MLS for breaching its rules regarding contact with an opponent’s face, head or neck.

A costly incident

MLS later announced Messi had been handed an undisclosed fine for breaching its rules regarding contact with an opponent’s face, head or neck.

A statement on the competition’s website read: “The MLS disciplinary committee has fined Inter Miami CF forward Lionel Messi an undisclosed amount for violating the league’s policy regarding hands to the face/head/neck of an opponent in the 101st minute of Miami’s match against the Philadelphia Union on 19 August.”

The ill-tempered clash saw the referee brandish two red cards late on with Inter Miami’s Yannick Bright and Sullivan’s brother, Cavan, both dismissed in the dying moments.

It is the second sanction handed out to Messi since his arrival in MLS in 2023.

The 39-year-old was fined back in February 2025 following a post-match fracas with New York City FC assistant coach Medhi Ballouchy.

3 An angry Messi lashed out at Sullivan during the match Credit: sujoy

3 The pair then squared up in the heated exchange Credit: sujoy

On that occasion, Messi was penalised for grabbing Ballouchy around the neck during a tense exchange.

Inter Miami are currently second in the Eastern Conference, seven points behind leaders Nashville.

Messi and co are aiming for a historic back-to-back MLS Cup success this season, following on from their maiden title last December.

The ex-Barcelona star recently returned to Miami following the tragic passing of his father.

Jorge Messi, died two weeks ago aged 68 following a long illness and as a result, Messi admitted he may not continue his football career for much longer.

It came just weeks after Messi's Argentina were beaten 1-0 by Spain in the World Cup final, capping off a difficult summer for the star both on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim warned AC Milan overpaid for player who Chelsea sold for £1.7m
Sports.content:
European football expert Andy Brassell believes Diego Moreira is an exciting addition to Ruben Amorim's AC Milan side, but suspects they may have 'overpaid'.

The former Chelsea winger completed a £56million move from Strasbourg to the Rossoneri in a club-record sale for the French outfit.



3 Moreira has signed a five-year deal through to 2031 at the San Siro Credit: Getty

The exit fee smashes the Ligue 1 side's previous record departure of £30m, which saw Dilane Bakwa join Nottingham Forest last summer.

Moreira's move comes just two years after Chelsea sold the Belgian international to their sister club for a fee of £1.7m.

The 22-year-old joined the Blues from Benfica yet struggled to make an impact at Stamford Bridge, making just one senior appearance for the club.



He established himself in France making 32 league appearances for Strasbourg and continued to improve the next season, featuring 42 times in all competitions and scoring five goals in an historic campaign.

Now managed by Amorim, AC Milan will fancy their chances in the Europa League following their latest statement signing.



Is it a good deal?

Brassell said: "Wing-backs who are creative and can get through a lot of work off the ball are integral to an Amorim system. I'm sure Manchester United fans got tired of him trying out players who are ill-suited for that role.

"They are essentially the two most important positions in his setup, so Moreira is ideal for them.



"We're looking at someone who can contribute a lot from a left-sided attacking role. It sort of makes you think even more that Rafael Leao's time at Milan might be coming to an end. I like Moreira a lot.

"I like Moreira a lot, but just as I felt they overpaid a little for Goncalo Ramos, I think they're overpaying for Moreira as well."

He added: "He's a good player who I think can go on to become a really good, top-level player. For an Italian team to go out spending near the thick end of 50 million euros on a wing back, I think is quite something.

3 The Belgian enjoyed a resurgence under Liam Rosenior at Strasbourg Credit: AFP



"Obviously they're trying to get a lot of players off the books at the moment as well. Wages will be part of it and they've got some big wages that they want to move on. It feels like an overpay to me, but it won't be an overpay if Moreira ends up being what Federico Dimarco is for Inter.

"That’s the benchmark they’re looking at, especially given how Inter's formula has relied so heavily on wing-backs in recent years. And that's why the Djed Spence signing is so important.

"They need a big personality at wing back to make their system work. and it’s interesting that Milan are now heading in that same direction with their choice of coach.

"This is a huge moment for Moreira. He gets to play for a massive club under a lot of pressure."



Inter Milan have re-established complete domestic control in Italy by utilising a 3-5-2 system where wing-backs like Dimarco and Denzel Dumfries act as the main goal providers.

When out of possession, the wing-backs drop deep immediately alongside the three central defenders to block any attacking threats.

3 Amorim will be hoping to re-establish his reputation as an elite European manager Credit: Getty

Amorim attempted to adapt a similar system during his time at Manchester United, tasking his wing-backs with pushing high up the pitch, though the tactical experiment proved unsuccessful.



However, it's clearly proved a successful system in Italy and the Portuguese manager will bring a fresh identity to the San Siro.

Brassell added: "Moreira should be stepping in for Pervis Estupinan, who has not had a great season. So they're looking to really upgrade that sort of area.

"In one way with the change of system he's probably looking at replacing Estupiñan and maybe Leao at the same time.

"Amorim said this weekend it's going to be really hard for Leao to get back in the starting XI. And this is a point where Morena can really kick his career on. Make himself a regular for Belgium and really get himself in the top bracket of European players."



Moreira was a member of the Belgium's World Cup squad this summer, featuring as a second-half substitute during the Red Devils' 3-2 comeback victory over Senegal.

The 22-year-old will now hope to prove in Serie A that he should be a part of Belgium's starting lineup ahead of Euro 2028.

Sports.title: Brighton eye possible Yankuba Minteh replacement already wanted by Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Brighton are keen on signing Spanish winger Yeremay Hernandez, talkSPORT understands.

The Deportivo de A Coruna star has been linked with a move to Hull but the Seagulls are beginning to show interest.

3 Yeremay Hernandez is attracting interest from two Premier League sides Credit: Getty

This comes as Brighton seek out a potential replacement for Yankuba Minteh, who is being hotly pursued by Liverpool.

The Reds have had two bids rejected for the Gambia winger, the latest of which was worth £60million.

Liverpool are looking to strengthen out wide before the end of the transfer window, who are still yet to replace Mohamed Salah.

Minteh has emerged as their latest target, with the Merseyside outfit reluctant to meet Paris Saint-Germain's £130million asking price for Bradley Barcola - despite the Frenchman wanting a move to Anfield.

Seagulls swoop?

While it is unclear if Liverpool will return with a third bid for Minteh, Brighton appear to be lining up a potential replacement should he end up leaving.

Having turned their attention to Spanish winger Hernandez, the Seagulls could now rival newly-promoted Hull for his signature.

The Deportivo star appeared close to joining the Tigers earlier this week, after pictures emerged on social media of him in Hull.

Hull owner Alcun Ilicali then fed speculation further by revealing the Hernandez was keen to sign, but was weighing up his options.

He told BBC Radio Humberside: "We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself.

"This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. He is young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come.

3 Liverpool have had two bids of £60million and £50m for Minteh rejected by Brighton Credit: Getty

"We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure."

But with Hernandez yet to put pen to paper on a deal at the MKM Stadium ahead of their Premier League opener against Manchester United, this could allow Brighton to swoop.

The 23-year-old has earned a strong reputation in Spain's second tier, playing a key role in Deportivo's promotion to LaLiga last term.

In the 2025/26 campaign, he netted 10 times and provided a further 11 assists in 38 LaLiga2 outings to help the Galician outfit seal a return to the top-flight after an eight-year absence.

A season before this, Hernandez notched an impressive 15 league goals in 39 games, assisting five times.

And while the prospect of top-flight football in Spain remains an option, the Spain Under-21 international could instead decide to try his hand in the Premier League.

3 Hernandez appears destined for top-flight football, either in Spain or England Credit: Getty

Should he head to either Brighton or Hull though, it is unclear when Hernandez would be fit to play.

The wideman missed Deportivo's LaLiga opener against Elche last week due a groin injury which has seen him miss all of their pre-season fixtures.

Should Brighton find themselves needing to replace Minteh, it would mark their latest high-profile exit.

The Seagulls have already lost Jan Paul van Hecke to Tottenham and Danny Welbeck to Chelsea earlier in the window.

Meanwhile, they have agreed a £70m deal to sell midfielder Carlos Baleba to Manchester United.

Sports.title: Tyrhys Dolan can make 97-year history against ‘legend’ Jose Mourinho after earning respect from ‘humble’ Jude Bellingham
Sports.content:
Real Madrid facing any team in LaLiga not named Barcelona is often billed as a David-versus-Goliath fixture.

And fittingly for Espanyol - who are based a stone's throw away from the Nou Camp - they are spearheaded by an Englishman who has slingshot his way from the Championship to Spanish stardom.



7 Espanyol's English winger Dolan hit the ground running with a goal on matchday one Credit: Getty

Tyrhys Dolan, in his own words, has already achieved his childhood dream and yet he continues to create pinch-me moments.

The latest of which came in Espanyol's opening game of the season, firing home the third and final goal in the club's 3-0 win over Levante.

Their return to the RCDE Stadium on Saturday will see them come up against none other than Real Madrid, who have yet to get their domestic campaign underway.



Espanyol 'feeling confident' against Real Madrid

Los Blancos did the double over Espanyol last term, but their postponed matchday one fixture due to several of their stars going deep in the World Cup has opened the door for the Parakeets to spring a shock.

“Yeah, I've been saying that. I've been saying I feel like it's a good time to play them,” Dolan enthusiastically told talkSPORT.com.



“We've got the love back for playing football after missing it in the off-season. The buzz is back around football again.

“Some of them have been playing throughout the summer and stuff. Like you said, we've got one competitive game under our belt, and we've got a win. So I think it's a really good time to play them and we're feeling confident.”



Dolan's heroics in Espanyol's LaLiga opener have been just reward for a gruelling pre-season in which, ironically, he's begun to mirror a Real Madrid winger who made his name in England before undergoing a dramatic transformation during his second year in Spain.

“I probably had two weeks where I just did nothing really,” he added. “But then you're kind of straight back on it for the next four weeks.

7 Dolan and Espanyol fancy their chances of causing an upset against Madrid Credit: Getty

“Then you've got a seven-week pre-season," Dolan continued to talkSPORT. “So it's like the work kind of doesn't stop really.



“But I like to keep working. Of course, the mental switch-off is needed, but I end up missing it once I'm at a couple of weeks off.”

Dolan on journey from Blackburn to Spain

It's been a much more straightforward summer for the 24-year-old compared to last year, when he decided to move abroad to join Espanyol after bringing an end to his five-year stay at Ewood Park.

Dolan recalled: “It was all like in the blink of an eye. I remember having the call with them on the Tuesday about the interest, and then come Thursday I'm on a flight, and I asked the question of like, 'Am I flying and then am I coming back and like getting my thing sorted?'

“They're like, 'No, no, no, get everything sorted. Once you sign, it's ready to go.' So I was like, wow, like it's a 40-hour turnaround, and your life just changes like that, and then you need to like get a car, you need to get a place to live.



7 Dolan has undergone a remarkable transformation since his Blackburn tenure Credit: Getty

7 A full pre-season has given the 24-year-old the perfect platform to take his game to the next level Credit: Getty

“It's not easy at all. Like you're going from hotels to apartments and stuff. It's a lot.

“I think now I feel better knowing that I've got my home. I've got a fan base that knows what I can do. They love me.



“I've got a team that are quality, and they support me and a manager that now believes in me because he's seen me do it for one season.

“I just think now for me, it feels so much better. I feel like I'm going into it seasoned with also more tools to my trade.

“An actual pre-season under my belt; the first year, I was just training on my own. So, yeah, definitely a big, a big change within myself this year that I feel more confident about.”

Proud moment facing Real Madrid

Dolan, who is from Broadheath in Greater Manchester, trod a path few English players take - especially in joining a club like Espanyol.



The Catalan outfit are among the founding LaLiga members, but the last Brit to play for them was ex-Everton star Adrian Heath in 1988.

It's been a meteoric rise to the top for Dolan, who was on loan at non-league side Clitheroe five years before playing at the Bernabeu.

“It's just a proud moment,” he said of facing Madrid last season. “But then just interacting with some of the players after the game and stuff, it's just a really, really nice feeling.

“And a lot of them are at the top of the game, and they're giving you some gems.”



One of those came from Jude Bellingham, who pulled his fellow Englishman for a chat after the game.

7 Dolan enjoyed his battles with fellow Englishman Bellingham during Espanyol's clashes with Madrid last season Credit: Getty

Bellingham is a 'top and humble human'

“We had some mutuals, but me and him had never had that conversation until we'd played him for the first time.

“Just obviously a world-class player. And, you know, it's great to be sharing the pitch with him. But like I said, a top and humble human.



“We had some good conversations after the game. Just a really, really top guy. You can see in the way he carries himself that that's just in his nature.”

7 Bellingham knows the journey of going from playing in the EFL to Spain's top division Credit: Instagram

Bellingham's support has continued in the months since, regularly 'getting the most interactions when he's dropped a little comment' on Dolan's Instagram.

“But no, it's nice for him because he doesn't need to do any of that.

“I think that he felt as well that another English player coming to the league and doing well, like I think he respected it because I feel like for me, watching him, it kind of kicked down that door of like making that abroad move and not just staying in your comfort zone.”



By Dolan's own admission, he doesn't get starstruck - but that's not to say he's unaware of the magnitude of being involved in Jose Mourinho's first competitive game back in the Madrid dugout.

"No, he's a legend," Dolan told talkSPORT. "He is a legend, I'll be honest. But it's just an exciting game.

"These are the games that you do want to play in; it speaks for itself really when you talk about these fixtures. So yeah, just excited for it. And we feel like we're ready."

7 Dolan played 38 games for Espanyol last season across La Liga and the Copa del Rey Credit: AFP



"We tackle it as any normal game. We kind of like to keep the same routine because that's all we know come match day.

"But to the outside world and your friends and your family, they think like, 'Oh my God, like you need to do this, you need to do that.'

"For us, just keeping that plane sailing, knowing that it's just another team of 11 players that obviously hold a lot of quality, as everyone does in this league, and we just need to do what we can do.

"But yeah, I've got a lot of family and friends who want to come out for this game," he added, smiling.



The chance to make history

Espanyol have never had an English goalscorer against Madrid in the 97 years since the club first helped establish LaLiga.

But facing a team renowned for Bellingham's outstretched arms or Kylian Mbappe's crossed ones, Dolan has a signature celebration of his own if he does indeed write himself into the history books.

"I might even hit the double backflip!

"This weekend I might have to bring two out, but no, no matter who I score against, it's that joy.

"I've achieved my childhood dream, so I could score against the bottom of the league or top of the league, and for me it genuinely feels the same.



"I just buzz whenever I do something that helps the team, and it boosts the kid in me, because that's all I thought about when I was younger.

"So, yeah, hopefully this weekend I can have a reason to pull it out there again..."

Sports.title: Man United make last-minute Marcus Rashford announcement after programme confusion
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford was given Man United's No.9 shirt after being listed without a squad number on the matchday programme for the trip to Hull.

The Red Devils kick off their Premier League campaign at the MKM Stadium on Saturday lunchtime - live on talkSPORT - buoyed by the return of the forward following his season-long loan at Barcelona.



3 Marcus Rashford arrived for Man United's game at Hull amid confusion Credit: Getty

3 Rashford wore the the No.9 jersey against AC Milan Credit: Getty

Rashford, who was named on the bench for the clash at Hull, was handed the No.9 shirt for last Saturday’s pre-season defeat to AC Milan, although United insisted the squad numbers were not yet finalised.

Just two hours before their season begins, the club finally announced its official list of squad numbers for the upcoming campaign, confirming that Rashford will don the No.9 shirt this season.



The 28-year-old previously wore the No.10 shirt at Old Trafford prior to his loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona but the number was taken by Matheus Cunha upon his arrival last summer.

Rashford was expected to be handed the No.14 shirt – the number he wore last season at Barcelona.



But bizarrely, the England international was the only Manchester United player listed without a number on the match programme’s squad list.

The mishap appears to show that the final say on Rashford’s shirt number was a late decision that was taken after the programme went to print.



Will Rashford be staying at Old Trafford after transfer deadline day?

Rashford’s new shirt number could be viewed as a hint that the forward will not be leaving Old Trafford before the end of the transfer window.

His No.9 shirt, vacated by Rasmus Hojlund last summer, could signify that the forward is set to play a prominent role this season under boss Michael Carrick.

It comes after Barcelona opted against the terms of a permanent deal this summer, instead electing to sign Anthony Gordon from Newcastle.

Carrick paid a glowing tribute to the star’s output since his return to the club.



3 Rashford's squad number was confirmed just two hours before kick-off Credit: Getty

“He’s come back really well. Very well,” the Manchester United boss said.

“I think the way it is now and not having so much time off really, and looking at three weeks, maybe just under three weeks, give or take.

“Boys don’t lose an awful lot in that time. It’s certainly the case of managing it, coming back in though and being sensible, knowing it’s a whole season for all the players to deal with.



“So in terms of the team this week going into next week as well, getting that balance right with all the group.

“But Marcus has come back particularly bright, particularly sharp, as I’ve said, and looks really good."

Sports.title: Unlikely Premier League striker can beat Erling Haaland to the Golden Boot
Sports.content:
Unlikely Premier League striker can beat Erling Haaland to the Golden Boot

Igor Thiago will be the man to end Erling Haaland's stranglehold on the Premier League Golden Boot this season.

That is the view of talkSPORT pundit Tony Cascarino, who has backed Brentford's No.9 to pick up where he left off last term and top the league's goalscoring charts ahead of Haaland.



6 Igor Thiago broke the Premier League record for the most goals scored by a Brazilian in a single season last term Credit: Getty

Thiago was one of the surprise packages of the 2025/26 campaign, as he fired in 22 goals after an injury-hit debut season in England.

This saw the Brazilian nominated for the Premier League Player of the Season award, with his exploits earning him a call-up to Brazil's World Cup squad in North America this summer.

But his impressive goal haul was only enough for him to rank second in the league's goalscoring charts, with a familiar face at the top.



For the third time in four years, Manchester City goal machine Haaland clinched the Golden Boot award after a 27-goal campaign.

Only Mohamed Salah prevented the Norwegian from making it four from four when he top scored with 29 goals in Liverpool’s 2024/25 title-winning season.



And after Haaland cemented his status as one of the world's very best at the World Cup, he is rightly the favourite to retain his goalscoring crown.

Can anyone beat Haaland?

While many speculate over how many goals will win Haaland the Golden Boot, Cascarino has instead named Thiago as an outside bet.



On talkSPORT's Weekend Sports Breakfast, the former Premier League striker was asked if anyone other than the Man City talisman could top the goalscoring charts.

To this, Cascarino replied: “Thiago - he was close [last year]. I'd go for the outsider.

"It's hard to ignore Haaland. So if I'm talking realistically, if you want to have a bit of a flutter and second [guess] the guy that may beat him, it'd be Thiago.

6 It will take a lot to beat Haaland for the top scorer title this season Credit: AFP



6 But Cascarino believes Thiago is the best bet to disrupt the Norwegian's Golden Boot dominance Credit: Getty

“If he stays fit, he's going to get a lot of goals, Erling Haaland.”

Best of the rest?

Despite a stellar 2025/26 campaign, Thiago faces question marks over whether he will be able to replicate his form this year, with talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor suggesting he may be a 'one-season wonder'.

But Cascarino backed him to challenge Haaland ahead of two more-fancied stars in Chelsea's Joao Pedro and Liverpool's British record signing Alexander Isak.

After his £60million move from Brighton last summer, Pedro notched an impressive 15 league goals in his debut season at Stamford Bridge.



Meanwhile Isak has a point to prove - starting with a hostile reunion with old club Newcastle - after struggling to justify his huge price tag by scoring just three times in a season largely written off by a broken leg suffered in November.

After co-host Katie Shanahan suggested Isak and Pedro as potential candidates, Cascarino replied: "Not so sure with Isak.

6 Almost exactly 12 months after controversially leaving for Liverpool, Alexander Isak is poised to play against Newcastle for the first time on Sunday Credit: Getty

6 Joao Pedro has been backed to star again for Chelsea after recently penning a new eight-year contract with the club Credit: Getty



“He has injuries every season. He always has. He's not a durable player. He's a very good and exciting one, but he's not durable."

Haaland in the Premier League: Season by season

Beating Haaland to the Golden Boot will certainly take some doing.

Since his arrival at the Etihad Stadium in 2022, the Norwegian has smashed the 20-goal mark in all four of his Premier League seasons.

This includes breaking the record for the most goals scored in a single Premier League season in his debut campaign, when he fired in 36 in 2022/23.

He followed this up with another Golden Boot-winning 27-goal haul the following year, before his 22 goals in the 2024/25 season were bettered by Mohamed Salah.



But after his tally of 27 saw him win back top prize last season, Haaland's rivals may sense a potential chink in the armour this year.

6 For the first time in his Man City career, Haaland won't be managed by the legendary Pep Guardiola Credit: Getty

With Man City possibly going through a period of transition as Enzo Maresca replaces the legendary Pep Guardiola in the dugout, the towering striker may not receive the same service as in past years.

Sports.title: Gloating Hull City fans taunt Joe Cole after his bizarre claim he had snubbed covering their Premier League return for TNT Sports - as they race into two-goal lead against Man United before half time
Sports.content:
Gloating Hull City fans taunt Joe Cole after his bizarre claim he had snubbed covering their Premier League return for TNT Sports - as they race into two-goal lead against Man United before half time

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Hull City taunted Joe Cole - who wrote them off for this Premier League season - in their thrilling first match against Manchester United.

Supporters chanted 'are you watching, Joe Cole?' as they stunned Michael Carrick's side with goals from centre-backs Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy.

Cole has drawn criticism for laughing at the newly promoted club, saying they are 'gone' on The Dressing Room podcast in the build-up to the season.

He also bizarrely claimed that TNT Sports assigned him to the Hull-Manchester United match and that he put his phone on Do Not Disturb to avoid contact about it.

Daily Mail Sport has since exclusively revealed that he was never lined up to cover the match anyway.

Fans have taken to social media to highlight what they see as Cole's ‘condescending’ and ‘disrespectful’ attitude, with some even claiming that the Championship play-off winners should ban Cole from its stadium.

Hull City fans mocked Joe Cole - who laughed at their Premier League chances - as they went 2-0 up against Manchester United in their opening match

Hull City are GOING DOWN! 🗣️🐯



The lads don’t rate Hull’s chances this season 🥺



Watch in full 👉 https://t.co/PuonqV3D90#TheDressingRoom #PremierLeague #PL pic.twitter.com/B1xa8RV4nI — The Dressing Room Podcast (@dressingroomaa) August 19, 2026

Cole drew the wrath of Hull City fans with the disrespectful comments he made on his podcast

Hull owner Acun Ilicali responded to his comments, writing on social media: 'It is disappointing to see my beautiful city criticised by people who should know better.

'As a club we are used to being underestimated and we enjoy it, and we enjoyed it more when we were promoted last season.

'The true beauty of a place is in its people, and that’s why, for me, Hull is one of the most beautiful places in the world.

'For me, seeing two ex-players making fun of a deservedly promoted club, is more laughable than the things they were laughing at.'

The Yorkshire outfit took viewers by surprise with their quick start against United and, to make matters worse for the visiting fans, the train home between 3.03pm and 5.03pm were cancelled.

'You're going home in a taxi,' chanted the home fans.

Hull were tipped by some to be relegated from the Championship last campaign but Ilicali has always been bullish about his side's chances under manager Sergej Jakirovic.

They have spent around £76million on 11 players since promotion and are targeting more signings, but kicked off against United with eight players from last season in their starting line-up.

Hull fans were enjoying themselves after taking a 2-0 lead against Man United 🐯



📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/IqEq4lg2FE — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) August 22, 2026

Former Chelsea and England Cole triggered outrage in East Yorkshire thanks to the comments he made with former West Ham team-mate Carlton Cole on a podcast.

When asked who would be going down this season, Cole said ‘Hull are gone, man’ before claiming that they had arrived in the Premier League ‘through the back door’.

He then added that he had ‘a confession to make’, saying he had been contacted by TNT Sports who ‘tried to slip in Hull on the first day of the season’. ‘I put my phone on Do Not Disturb,’ he said.

Daily Mail Sport understands the comments have left bosses at TNT Sports bemused, with insiders saying Cole was not down to cover the opener at the MKM Stadium, and never had been.

Regardless, it has stoked plenty of emotion in Hull. Sources have disclosed that players and staff are well aware of what was said and intend to use it as motivation for what would appear to be a tough mission ahead.

They will look to the achivements of Sunderland last season as inspiration after the Black Cats qualified for European football in their first year back in the top flight.
