World.title: Cuando el fenómeno fan se vuelve tóxico: de la agresión a Karol G a las críticas a Ariana Grande y el ‘review-bombing’
World.content:
Los comportamientos reprobables de unos pocos ensombrecen la figura del seguidor, más exigente que nunca en un tiempo en el que las redes sociales promueven una falsa sensación de cercanía a los ídolos a la vez que proporcionan cierto anonimato para lanzar ataques

Durante el concierto que la cantante Karol G ofreció el pasado julio en Toronto, como parada de su Tropicoqueta Tour, un fan irrumpió en el escenario mientras la colombiana cantaba. Le agarró del brazo sin soltarla, después del cuello e incluso llegó a zarandearla cuando el equipo de seguridad intervino y trató de reducirle. Escasos días después, la actriz y cantante Ariana Grande anunció que se retira de la vida pública cuando finalice su actual gira, Eternal Sunshine Tour, el próximo 1 de septiembre. ¿El motivo? Su hartazgo frente a las críticas vertidas hacia su cuerpo. La reacción a esta decisión no convenció a muchos seguidores, que aseguraban estar preocupados por su aspecto. “En este punto, estoy juzgando a su equipo, amigos y familia. Esto es una locura”, se lee en uno de los comentarios de su videoclip Petal. Luego ella ha asegurado encontrarse bien, pero con ello no han cesado los comentarios acerca de su físico e incluso sobre si padece un trastorno de la conducta alimentaria, un rumor con el que la artista lleva años conviviendo.

Otro incidente que puso de manifiesto la facilidad con la que algunos fans pasan del apoyo al acoso lo vivió el pasado abril el actor Walker Scobell. El joven de 17 años, que ha saltado a la fama como protagonista de la serie de Disney+ Percy Jackson, explicó en stories que renunciaba a acudir a su graduación de instituto porque sus fans estaban enviando amenazas de muerte a diferentes chicas de su entorno, con las que imaginaban que podía acudir a la graduación, un acto social de gran trascendencia en Estados Unidos que se realiza en pareja. “Para que todos lo sepáis: no iré a mi graduación. Por favor, dejad de enviar amenazas de muerte a TODAS las chicas adolescentes que remotamente puedan vincularse conmigo por vivir cerca de donde yo resido. No es justo para ellas ni para sus familias (…)”, dijo.

Si bien esa toxicidad representa un ínfimo porcentaje de los fans que se integran como una comunidad de apoyo a sus ídolos, se expande con facilidad gracias al poder multiplicador de las redes sociales, un entorno que ha cambiado la manera en que los anónimos del mundo pueden relacionarse con quienes admiran. “Las redes sociales han creado una sensación de cercanía entre los artistas y su público. En general, esa relación es muy positiva, pero también puede crear la falsa impresión de formar parte de su vida privada”, explica Toño Sánchez, CEO de Superstruct Entertainment Iberia, compañía especializada en ofrecer experiencias musicales y culturales.

En ello coincide Tomás Palacios, CEO de Artist Publicist, agencia española de relaciones públicas y comunicación de artistas: “Hemos normalizado actitudes poco aceptables entre público y artistas. Las redes sociales han democratizado la conversación entre artistas y fans, pero han difuminado los límites”, sostiene. “Desde la propia industria llevamos años trabajando para que la experiencia del público sea cada vez más cercana: encuentros con artistas, contenidos exclusivos, nuevos formatos y conciertos diseñados para que el fan sienta una conexión más directa”, continúa Sánchez antes de matizar que “es clave que la cercanía no se confunda con disponibilidad permanente ni con el derecho a decidir sobre la vida de un artista”.

Parar los pies a los fans parasociales

El relativo anonimato facilitado por las redes sociales, donde muchos supuestos fans se esconden detrás de la pantalla para lanzar todo tipo de ataques, es otro factor clave. Además del caso del actor de Percy Jackson, se ha visto recientemente con Belmont Cameli, protagonista masculino de Off Campus, la serie de Prime Video convertida en un fenómeno de masas desde su estreno en mayo. La novia en la vida real de Cameli, Raina Morris, se convirtió en el objetivo de los seguidores del actor que no han sabido discernir ficción de realidad y buscan que el intérprete se empareje con su compañera de reparto en la pantalla, la actriz Ella Bright, con quien comparte trama romántica en la serie. El acoso a Morris llegó a tal punto que ella pidió vía stories de Instagram que cesaran de mandar mensajes a sus familiares. “Si eres fan de mi novio: ¡Ey! Por favor, para de mandar mensajes a miembros de mi familia. Están muy confundidos. Escribid en vuestro diario o id a dar un paseo (…)”, dijo al respecto.

Los actores de 'Off Campus', Ella Bright y Belmont Cameli, el pasado mes de mayo, en Nueva York. TheStewartofNY (GC Images)

Connor Storrie, el actor de Más que rivales, la otra gran serie del año (al menos por su capacidad de generar conversación en internet), fue el centro de una disputa ocurrida en la semana de la moda de París el pasado junio, cuando dos fans se pelearon en una trifulca que no tardó en viralizarse en redes sociales. Un seguidor de Storrie que le esperaba en la puerta de su hotel se enzarzó con Simone Cromer, creadora de Club Chalamet, una cuenta nacida en 2018 como fan account de Timothée Chalamet que ha crecido tanto en visibilidad a lo largo de los años que ha convertido a su fundadora casi en una famosa más. Desde hace un tiempo, Cromer también apoya públicamente a Connor Storrie, a quien ha dedicado una cuenta específica. El enfrentamiento físico, al que aludieron ambos implicados en sus redes sociales, dividió a internet y evidenció cómo los fans a veces parecen querer buscar su propio momento de fama.

En el caso de Cromer, la mujer de 59 años detrás de Club Chalamet, esto resulta evidente. Cromer, a quien incluso The Wall Street Journal dedicó un perfil en diciembre de 2025, lleva varios años analizando cada detalle de la vida del actor de Marty Supreme. Su apoyo al intérprete se enfrió cuando este inició una relación con Kylie Jenner. Tras la primera aparición pública de la pareja en 2023, organizó un directo de casi una hora en Twitter (ahora X) para desacreditar la relación, que consideraba un fraude. A raíz de este hecho, la revista Rolling Stone señaló en un amplio artículo la misoginia palpable en la cultura fan y en sus ataques y críticas a mujeres (novias, esposas, amigas…). Sin embargo, otras voces apuntan a que la propia Cromer es víctima de la misoginia, y que existe una doble vara de medir y juzgar a mujeres y hombres fans. Así lo refleja la periodista Kat Tenbarge en su Substack Spitfire News!, donde analiza las noticias de la cultura de internet, cuando dice que Cromer sufre una misoginia similar a la que ella misma perpetúa.

El actor de 'Más que rivales' Connor Storrie, en París, en junio de 2026. WWD (WWD via Getty Images)

Si hablamos de toxicidad y fans, el juicio de Johnny Depp y Amber Heard marcó un antes y un después al retratar cómo para algunos el apoyo a sus ídolos está siempre justificado, incluso con la violencia de por medio. Durante el caso por difamación que en 2022 enfrentó en los tribunales a la expareja de actores, analizado hasta la saciedad, los fans de Depp iniciaron una campaña de acoso y derribo contra Amber Heard y su entorno. Además de realizar review-bombing (puntuar negativamente y en masa) en las películas de la actriz, e incluso en la consulta del psiquiatra que testificó a su favor durante el juicio, sembraron las redes sociales de mensajes de odio hacia cualquiera que mostrara simpatías por la intérprete. Amber Heard fue vilipendiada y denunció haber recibido amenazas de muerte.

Kylie Jenner y Timothée Chalamet, en la fiesta de 'Vanity Fair' tras los Oscar de 2026, el pasado 15 de marzo, en California. Steve Granitz (FilmMagic)

El fandom tóxico no se circunscribe al ámbito de la música, el cine y la televisión. Basta con pensar en el mundo del deporte, donde se normalizan actitudes cuanto menos cuestionables que, realizadas en otro contexto, resultarían inadmisibles. Y precisamente por resultar tan habitual y cotidiano no acaparan titulares, como sí sucede en el ámbito del entretenimiento.

La pregunta obvia es: ¿por qué no se paran los pies de esos fans exacerbados e incluso parasociales? El debate es complejo y repleto de matices. En un artículo publicado por Wired en junio, titulado Hollywood prospera gracias a los fans fanáticos. Para los publicistas, son una pesadilla, se puso de manifiesto cómo esa devoción desmedida de algunos juega a favor de la maquinaria hollywoodiense, ya que funciona como una suerte de publicidad gratuita. Cuando una multitud de personas jalea el nombre de su ídolo en la puerta de un hotel o le pide fotos y autógrafos al llegar a un restaurante puede resultar una intromisión a la intimidad, pero esos mismos fans no dejan de multiplicar la visibilidad de cada uno de los movimientos de las celebridades. Estas, a su vez, forman parte de un sistema que alimenta el interés constante y deja mirar a través de una ventana virtual aquello (y solo aquello) que quieren compartir. “Nunca el público había estado tan cerca de los artistas y, precisamente por eso, nunca había esperado tanto de ellos”, reflexiona Sánchez acerca de cómo los fans se han vuelto cada vez más exigentes.

Por otro lado, cuando cruzan líneas rojas de manera sistemática en nombre de un artista (aunque no con su consentimiento), pueden llegar a perjudicar la imagen de la celebridad en cuestión y echar por tierra el trabajo de los publicistas. Tal y como sostiene Sánchez, cuando eso sucede “la conversación deja de centrarse en la música [o el cine] y empieza a girar alrededor del conflicto”. Y apunta: “Eso puede condicionar la percepción pública del artista, aunque no haya promovido directamente esos comportamientos. Los artistas y sus equipos no pueden controlar cada reacción individual, pero sí pueden contribuir a marcar un tono y a dejar claro que la admiración no justifica el acoso”.

La peligrosidad que pueden alcanzar estos comportamientos de fans tóxicos no pasa desapercibida y en la ciudad de Shanghái se acaba de lanzar una campaña institucional para concienciar de ello y tratar de evitar ciertos comportamientos. Algunos de los aspectos que aborda la iniciativa tienen que ver con la manipulación de rankings a través de puntuaciones falsas, con la creación y divulgación de rumores falsos y con el acoso contra celebridades. Deberán tomar nota en otros países.

World.title: Regular las redes sociales o prohibir su acceso a los menores: un debate mundial que se está resolviendo en los tribunales
World.content:
Las redes sociales son terribles para niños y adolescentes. En una época marcada por la polarización, esta idea genera un abrumador consenso; es más popular que las croquetas. Un Eurobarómetro del pasado mes de julio señalaba que el 72% de los padres están preocupados por el contenido online que consumen sus hijos. La idea es transversal y va en aumento, así que gobiernos de todo signo y tribunales de medio mundo han empezado a actuar. El diagnóstico es compartido, pero las recetas difieren. Estos días, las dos más importantes se han visto en los tribunales.

Meta, el multimillonario imperio tecnológico que lidera Mark Zuckerberg, se enfrenta al juicio más transcendental de su historia, que busca determinar el impacto de Facebook e Instagram sobre la salud de los menores. Hasta ahora, y llevamos una década de litigios, estos han servido para poco. Ha habido acuerdos extrajudiciales, indemnizaciones y se han creado cuentas para adolescentes con más restricciones. Pero los mecanismos que convierten a las redes sociales en plataformas adictivas por diseño siguen ahí. El scroll infinito, el algoritmo de recomendación, las notificaciones constantes, la polarización… Son los pilares sobre los que se asienta la arquitectura de las plataformas. Lejos de renunciar a ellas, en estos años solo se han perfeccionado. TikTok tiene un algoritmo más oscuro y con más capacidad de enganche que Instagram. X es hoy un lugar mucho más agresivo y extremo de lo que nunca fue Twitter, su antecesor. La desinformación y los discursos de odio no solo no son perseguidos, sino que muchas veces es el propio dueño de la compañía, el magnate Elon Musk, el que los comparte. Ante la imposibilidad de regular y moderar las prácticas de las empresas más poderosas del mundo, algunos gobiernos han optado por algo más drástico: prohibir su acceso a los menores. Ya lo han hecho Francia y Australia. Una docena de países, entre ellos España, están trabajando en esta dirección.

Pero esta alternativa, discutida por muchos expertos, está empezando a mostrar sus flaquezas. La semana pasada, el Consejo Constitucional de Francia anuló esa ley impulsada por Emmanuel Macron que prohibía acceder a las redes a menores de 15 años al considerar que supondría “una vulneración desproporcionada de la libertad de expresión”. El varapalo al modelo francés va más allá de lo legal, y plantea dudas morales y sociales, ya que los chavales se expresan y se informan en las redes, no son únicamente un producto tóxico como el tabaco. “El fallo es revelador porque no cuestiona el objetivo —proteger a los menores—, sino el instrumento: una prohibición general, que discrimina por edad o madurez”, explica la socióloga especialista en sociedad digital Liliana Arroyo. “Ese es precisamente el punto ciego de muchas propuestas regulatorias que surgen del pánico moral: se legisla contra el síntoma (el tiempo de pantalla, el acceso) en lugar de contra la causa (un modelo de negocio basado en capturar la atención y los datos de los usuarios, también de los menores)”, abunda.

La ley francesa asume la incapacidad de luchar contra los efectos perniciosos de las redes y corta el problema de raíz. Es como si se supiera que la reproducción automática engancha al usuario (se sabe), y en lugar de prohibirle a Netflix que lo ponga por defecto en su plataforma, prohibiéramos a los niños ver Peppa Pig. “No deberíamos poner el foco en apartar a los adolescentes del espacio digital donde construyen buena parte de su vida social”, señala Arroyo. La prioridad debería ser asegurarse de que ese espacio digital sea más seguro.

Las redes sociales se han vuelto el principal canal de socialización de los jóvenes en España. El 79% de los españoles entre los 15 y los 29 años asegura usarlas “de forma masiva” como su vía para relacionarse, también para informarse y entretenerse. Además, pueden servir de tabla de salvación digital para adolescentes que se sienten aislados y diferentes, ya sea por su ubicación, por su sexualidad o por sus gustos y aficiones. Pueden conocer a gente como ellos y sentirse menos solos. Pueden conocer a gente opuesta a ellos, ofreciendo una ventana a otras realidades.

Antes, los adolescentes empezaban a informarse cogiendo el periódico de papel de sus padres o viendo el telediario juntos frente a la tele. Esos días quedaron atrás y hoy, la abrumadora mayoría de personas se informa a través del móvil. “Cerrar el acceso a las redes sociales también cierra una ventana de información, participación y vínculo social que hoy es parte de la ciudadanía digital”, opina Arroyo. “Y eso el Constitucional francés lo ha entendido bien al hablar de libertad de expresión y comunicación”.

La misteriosa depresión de los Z

Las propuestas de prohibición surgen de un deseo comprensible de mantener a los jóvenes seguros y sanos. Las tasas de depresión y ansiedad entre adolescentes se han disparado un 50% desde 2010. Las de suicidio lo han hecho en un 32%. Los miembros de la generación Z —nacidos a partir de 1996— han empezado a padecer ansiedad, depresión y otros trastornos mentales, alcanzando niveles más altos que cualquier otra generación en la historia. Esto ha coincidido con el momento en que los adolescentes de los países desarrollados cambiaron sus teléfonos por smartphones y trasladaron gran parte de su vida social a internet. Muchos estudios han relacionado ambos fenómenos, fomentando un debate social y cierta desconfianza hacia la tecnología. Pero correlación no implica causalidad y el debate está lejos de ser resuelto.

Algunos expertos demonizan las redes sociales en sí. Otros creen que lo perjudicial es el continente, no el contenido. No serían las frívolas rutinas de skincare de las influencers las que deprimen a tu hija, sino unos mecanismos que hacen que después de ese vídeo quiera ver otro, y otro, y otro. Las mecánicas perniciosas de las redes depredan el tiempo libre de los menores (y de los mayores), recluyéndolos en casa. Se ha reducido progresivamente el tiempo que dedican a estar con sus amigos, a las actividades físicas o a dormir, para pasarlo interactuando a través de las pantallas.

Esta idea ha estado muy presente estos días en el juicio a Meta. “Este caso no trata sobre si las redes sociales ofrecen algún beneficio a ciertas personas. Sí lo hacen”, afirmó la fiscal adjunta de California. Lo que se juzga es si la empresa manipuló a esos jóvenes para que pasaran más tiempo en su plataforma. “Meta sabía mucho sobre el cerebro de los jóvenes: cómo buscan constantemente recompensas, su gran sensibilidad a la retroalimentación social y a la opinión de los demás, y cómo aún están desarrollando su capacidad para controlar los impulsos tal como lo hacen los adultos”, explicó la fiscal. Y usó esa información para manipularlos, ganando dinero y dañando su salud.

Teniendo en cuenta las prioridades de los tecnoligarcas, resulta comprensible que muchos prefieran alejar a sus hijos de su campo de juegos. Pero las prohibiciones categóricas pueden resultar contraproducentes, señalan los expertos. “Tiene muchas complicaciones. Para empezar, es difícil incluso delimitar el concepto de red social”, explica Borja Adsuara Varela, experto en Derecho y Estrategia Digital. “Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Twitter... está claro que lo son. Pero WhatsApp también es una red social, un videojuego que tenga un chat online también”. En los países que abogan por la prohibición, estas plataformas de mensajería quedarían libres.

La experiencia de otros países nos dice que es difícil poner puertas a internet y que los menores encuentran formas de burlar la ley. Cuatro meses después de la prohibición, casi dos tercios de los menores australianos de entre 12 y 15 años afirmaban haber recuperado el acceso a sus redes por la puerta de atrás, mintiendo sobre su fecha de nacimiento, usando VPNs o apuntando a la cara de un amigo mayor para pasar el reconocimiento fotográfico.

Otra forma de evitar la prohibición es migrar a otras plataformas. “En Australia muchos se fueron a Reddit y a otras plataformas que tenían su sede fuera del país, con lo cual no les podían obligar a impedir el acceso de los menores”, explica Adsuara. El riesgo, apunta el experto, es acabar empujándolos a redes más oscuras y menos reguladas.

En todo este debate se apela a la responsabilidad de los tecnoligarcas, o se confía en la capacidad de prohibir de las administraciones. Pero Adsuara cree que la responsabilidad primera empieza en casa. “No podemos descargar en las leyes lo que es la función de los padres”, opina el jurista. “Es como pensar que los ahogamientos en piscinas son responsabilidad exclusiva del socorrista. Los padres también tienen que seguir vigilando”. Siguiendo con este símil, lo que se debate ahora es si habría que poner más socorristas o unas normas estrictas de convivencia acuática. Quizá dar manguitos a los niños o enseñarles a nadar. O prohibirles el acceso a la piscina hasta que cumplan 16 años.

World.title: Las sanciones por no pagar horas extra se triplican pero siguen sin frenar a las empresas incumplidoras
World.content:
Las multas de la Inspección pasan de 5,3 millones en 2018 a 15,7 en 2025 mientras volumen de tiempo no compensado se mantiene estable. Los sindicatos calculan un ahorro empresarial de 3.378 millones

La Inspección de Trabajo realizó el pasado año 37.386 actuaciones para controlar las irregularidades en materia de tiempo de trabajo, en las que detectó 14.728 infracciones. Esto llevó al organismo a imponer sanciones a los empresarios infractores por un valor de 15,7 millones de euros. Una cuantía que demuestra la escasa capacidad disuasoria de la actual normativa a juicio de los sindicatos, que calculan que los empresarios ahorran anualmente 3.378 millones de euros en cotizaciones sociales y salarios con las horas extra impagadas, que apenas se han reducido en los últimos años.

España estableció en 2019 la obligatoriedad para todas las empresas de llevar un registro horario de la jornada de todos sus trabajadores, para que la Inspección y los propios empleados pudieran justificar los abusos horarios por parte de las compañías. Desde entonces la cuantía total de las multas se ha multiplicado por tres, pasando de 5,3 millones impuestos a las compañías infractoras en 2018,el último ejercicio antes de la implantación de la medida, a 15,7 millones en 2025. Y en el último año aumentó especialmente el número de trabajadores afectados por infracciones empresariales en la materia, pasando de los 178.456 de 2024 a 252.500 en 2025.

Pero la presión sancionadora apenas parece haber frenado el número de horas extra que se hacen sin pagar, que CC OO estipula en una media de 2,54 millones a la semana, según los registros de la EPA. En la serie estadística, que presenta altibajos debido a la estacionalidad del mercado laboral, el volumen semanal de horas impagadas se mantiene entre los 2,5 y los 3 millones en todos los trimestres desde finales de 2016. Y el porcentaje de horas extra impagadas sobre el total de las que se hacen es del 43%, el mismo que en 2018.

Por eso los sindicatos consideran que las multas no son disuasorias e incluso salen rentables para las empresas infractoras. Para ello exhiben la enorme diferencia entre el volumen de sanciones y el valor estimado de las horas extra impagadas, que CC OO calcula también a partir de fuentes oficiales. Mientras las multas permanecen estancadas en una horquilla entre 15 y 17 millones de euros anuales en los últimos años, el valor estimado por el sindicato de las horas extra sin compensar supera los 3.300 millones de euros anuales.

Esta es una de las circunstancias que hicieron que la vicepresidenta segunda y ministra de Trabajo, Yolanda Díaz, intentara endurecer el control horario en las negociaciones para reducir la jornada laboral a 37,5 horas. El plan, que fracasó junto al resto del proyecto cuando el Congreso lo tumbó, incluía la obligación de que el registro fuera telemático y de acceso inmediato y remoto para la Inspección. Pero también un cambio del régimen sancionador para elevar las multas. Estas se imponen actualmente por empresa infractora, independientemente del número de trabajadores afectados por el incumplimiento, el nuevo plan pasaba a imponer la multa por por cada empleado, por lo que se encarecerían sustancialmente.

Además de la individualización de las multas —una de las principales cuestiones que llevó a la patronal a luchar para impedir la aprobación de la norma— el proyecto de ley de reducción de jornada recogía una elevación de las cuantías económicas. Trabajo aumentaba la multa a las empresas por cometer una infracción grave en esta materia de 751 a 1.000 euros en su grado mínimo; y de 7.500 a 10.000 euros en su grado máximo. Estos cambios habrían supuesto, por ejemplo, que la sanción mínima para una empresa de 50 trabajadores pasaría de un mínimo actual de 751 euros actuales a la posibilidad de llegar a medio millón de euros.

Tomando los datos de la Inspección de Trabajo, que en las 14.728 irregularidades detectadas el año pasado cuantifica en 252.500 los trabajadores afectados, se obtiene que por cada infracción hay una media de 17 trabajadores. Dicho de otra forma, a igual gravedad de las infracciones, las individualización de las multas multiplicaría por 17 el montante que tendrían que satisfacer las empresas.

Además, Trabajo trató de introducir en el proyecto fallido un nuevo supuesto, cuando el abuso horario implicase un riesgo para la salud del trabajador. En su grado de mayor gravedad, esta infracción se sancionaba con cerca de un millón (983.736 euros), aunque en este caso sí se impondría por empresa y no por cada empleado.

Endurecer el registro horario

Todos estos intentos se convirtieron en papel mojado porque el proyecto de ley de las 37,5 horas no llegó ni a pasar el primer trámite en el Congreso de los Diputados, donde fue rechazado por PP, Vox, Junts y UPN en el debate de enmiendas a la totalidad. Trabajo ha insistido desde entonces en aprobar un endurecimiento del registro horario por la vía reglamentaria, algo que no necesita la aprobación del Parlamento. Pero esta vía impide reformar el régimen de sanciones, ya que esto requeriría modificar la Ley de Infracciones y Sanciones del Orden Social (conocida por su acrónimo LISOS).

Ante la imposibilidad de elevar sustancialmente las multas, el departamento que encabeza Yolanda Díaz sí ha concretado en el desarrollo reglamentario que prepara una modificación que afecta a las horas extra: los trabajadores deberán hacer los asientos personalmente en el registro y diferenciar ellos mismos qué el tiempo de trabajo ordinario del que debe abonarse como extraordinario.

Fuentes de Trabajo aseguran que el departamento “está centrado en sacar adelante el registro horario” porque “es una herramienta que servirá para atacar de manera directa el fraude en las horas extraordinarias”. Y agregan que esperan aprobar el reglamento a principios de septiembre.

En el ministerio de Díaz también señalan que, aunque no pueda acometerse en el reglamento, no renuncian a endurecer el régimen sancionador. Y esa es la principal demanda de los sindicatos. El secretario de acción sindical de CC OO, Javier Pacheco, considera que la única vía disuasoria es hacer las multas individuales por cada trabajador. Y asegura que el sindicato va a intentar, a partir de septiembre, que el Gobierno modifique la LISOS a través de enmiendas en alguno de los proyectos de ley que se tramitan en el Parlamento.

Fernando Luján, vicesecretario general de Política Sindical de UGT, está de acuerdo con la necesidad de individualizar las sanciones, pero echa un jarro de agua fría sobre las aspiraciones sindicales. “Será extremadamente complicado reunir los apoyos parlamentarios necesarios pasar sacar esta reforma adelante”, asegura.

Cómo se sanciona en Europa

El endurecimiento de las sanciones que pretenden Trabajo y los sindicatos por falsear o carecer de registro horario se encontraría entre las medidas más estrictas de Europa. Un trabajo comparativo de las distintas legislaciones laborales realizado por Eurofound señala otros países, como Austria o Rumania, donde las multas ya se ponen por cada empleado y no por empresa, aunque con cuantías en general más bajas. El régimen sancionador más severo es el de Finlandia, donde además de multas económicas, las violaciones de las leyes de tiempo de trabajo pueden castigarse con penas de cárcel de hasta seis meses.

Los autores del estudio de la organización que agrupa a patronales, sindicatos y Comisión Europea precisan que en países como Irlanda, Reino Unido, Países Bajos y Alemania no existe el derecho legal a recibir un pago adicional por horas extra (a menos que se acuerde por contrato o convenio colectivo). En esos territorios donde la regulación es más laxa, las sanciones dependen de lo estipulado en los convenios sectoriales o de empresa.

World.title: Las águedas de Tiedra aceptan al fin a solteras y divorciadas: “Una cofradía de mujeres no puede quitar a otras mujeres”
World.content:
La cofradía de Santa Águeda de Tiedra, documentada en este pueblo de Valladolid de 275 habitantes desde mediados del siglo XVII, ha modernizado sus estatutos: las mujeres que forman parte de esta agrupación han decidido eliminar el requisito excluyente de que, para unirse, las interesadas deben estar casadas por la Iglesia. La reforma, acordada en asamblea general extraordinaria, se ha adoptado por mayoría de las 140 cofrades, si bien no se ha tocado otro de sus preceptos clave: las mujeres han de estar bautizadas si quieren ser Águedas de pleno derecho. El artículo 4 de los estatutos de la cofradía rezaba así antes de su cambio el pasado 17 de agosto, que ahora deberá ser ratificado por el arzobispo de Valladolid, Luis Argüello, también presidente de la Conferencia Episcopal Española: “Será requisito indispensable para pertenecer a esta cofradía el observar buena conducta moral y estar bautizada y casada legal y eclesiásticamente”.

Belén Calvo, tesorera de la cofradía, comenta que por fin se ratifica un proyecto que viene de 2019, cuando se votó negativamente una idea que se venía años barruntando en la cofradía, consciente del giro de los tiempos. “Nuestra cofradía era para casadas legal y eclesiásticamente. Si una mujer se separaba, variaba; divorciadas tampoco… Un batiburrillo con todo lo que ha cambiado la sociedad. Una cofradía de mujeres no puede quitar a otras mujeres”, explica la vallisoletana, recordando que en junio se vieron con Argüello en una visita pastoral. “Nos recomendó hacerlo para mayores de edad y al menos bautizadas porque es religiosa”, anota.

Calvo reconoce que 28 de las 97 votantes se opusieron (hay 140 cofrades registradas), postura que respeta, y añade que todas las consultas han sido desde la tolerancia y el afán constructivo. “Muchas mujeres ya ni se casan, se quedan en parejas y en estos pueblos no hay ni bodas, las familias son como les da la gana, como debe ser. Los legajos se han ido actualizando; era lo único que quedaba por actualizar y mantenemos los ritos y la rica indumentaria, ir todas juntas al baile, a misa, los cambios de mayordoma…”, enumera, sobre la pertinencia del cambio.

La modificación, que ha adelantado El Norte de Castilla, ha sido también celebrada por Izquierda Unida (IU) en Tiedra, que ha valorado que esa tradición se adecúe a los tiempos. “Esta decisión permitirá la entrada de mujeres cuyo estado les había privado de poder hacerlo, apartando así una norma antigua heredada de la tradición”, han indicado en un comunicado en su perfil en la red social Facebook. “Enhorabuena a la Cofradía de Santa Águeda de Tiedra por caminar a la par de los tiempos actuales”, escribe el partido en su perfil, destacando que el porcentaje de mujeres que contraen matrimonio por la Iglesia actualmente apenas llega al 16%, lo cual podría significar que mantener estos criterios selectivos dificulte la supervivencia de las entidades que los conserven. “Los tiempos siempre son cambiantes, pero hemos pasado en pocas décadas de una sociedad profundamente sacralizada a otra mucho más laica, teóricamente aconfesional y más tolerante. Han cambiado las relaciones sociales y el propio concepto de familia y de matrimonio”.

“La realidad es que sin matrimonios eclesiásticos la Cofradía no tendría futuro, adaptarse a las nuevas situaciones es la única manera de perpetuar esta tradición”, explica IU, recordando que desde la fundación de las Águedas, un festejo religioso muy respetado y querido en el medio rural, en los cientos de años que se lleva celebrando se han vivido múltiples readaptaciones de sus líneas constitutivas.

World.title: Dutch privacy watchdog fines Uber €825m over drivers’ rights
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Dutch data protection authority AP has fined Uber €825 million for deactivating drivers’ accounts through automated systems without properly informing them, in what is the second-largest penalty ever issued under European privacy law.

The watchdog leads on privacy oversight of Uber across the EU because the company’s European head office is in Amsterdam.

Under the EU’s data protection rules, companies are not allowed to let an algorithm alone take decisions that significantly affect someone’s life. A human must be involved, and the person affected must be able to object.

The case relates to events between 2020 and 2022 and began with complaints from drivers in France, who had been suspended on suspicion of fraud, such as taking unnecessary detours to increase their fares.

Uber to appeal

Uber said it would challenge the fine. “We strongly disagree with this decision and disproportionate fine,” a spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the company took drivers’ rights seriously.

The firm said its current policies included human review and allowed drivers to contest suspensions, and that it no longer deactivated accounts permanently through automated systems alone.

The penalty easily exceeds the AP’s previous record, a €290 million fine imposed on Uber last year for transferring drivers’ data to the United States.

That case, which Uber is also appealing, grew out of the same complaints by French drivers. The regulator had already fined the company €10 million in early 2024 over drivers’ privacy rights and €600,000 in 2018.

The only larger fine under the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the €1.2 billion penalty handed to Meta by Ireland’s regulator in 2023, for transferring European Facebook users’ data to the United States, a case that Meta is appealing.

World.title: Wall Street Journal tips Groningen novelist for Nobel prize
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Wall Street Journal has named the Groningen-based novelist Anjet Daanje a serious contender for the Nobel prize in literature, in a review of her novel Het lied van ooievaar en dromedaris (The Song of Stork and Dromedary), first published in 2022 and recently translated to English.

The paper’s critic Sam Sacks said Daanje is “one of the continent’s leading writers.”

Sacks noted that the prize has never gone to a writer from the Netherlands, which he put down to bad luck rather than any lack of quality. He named the late Harry Mulisch as another Dutch author who deserved it.

The last Dutch author nominated was Simon Vestdijk, who received multiple nominations in the 1950s and 60s. The Nobel archive is sealed for 50 years, so any more recent candidates remain secret.

Inspired by the Brontës

Daanje, who was born in Drenthe, achieved a breakthrough with her novel Deherdenking soldaat (The Remembered Soldier) in 2019.

Het lied van ooievaar en dromedaris won both the Libris literature prize and the Boekenbon prize – the first book to take the Netherlands’ two main literary awards. Daanje went on to receive the Constantijn Huygens prize for her body of work.

The English edition runs to more than 700 pages. Loosely based on the Brontë sisters, it circles an Emily Brontë-like writer through interlinked stories spanning almost three centuries.

The 2026 Nobel prize in literature will be announced in Stockholm on October 8.

World.title: Cabinet still aims for majority budget support, Heinen says
World.content:
The Dutch cabinet still believes it can win support from across the political spectrum for its annual budget, finance minister Eelco Heinen has said, a week before the plans are due to be sent off for review.

“I’m confident that will work out,” Heinen told reporters ahead of Friday’s cabinet meeting. “We’re now really in the final phase.” He said he believed the opposition parties whose votes are needed are moving closer together and “don’t differ that much from each other.”

Heinen, who stayed away from the opening days of talks with opposition leaders this week, is now holding his own discussions with the parties. The cabinet wants a deal in place by next Friday, August 28, when it plans to send the budget to the Council of State.

Left or right

The minority coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is 10 seats short of a majority in the lower house and holds less than a third of the seats in the senate, leaving it reliant on opposition votes.

Support from opposition party PRO, which has 20 seats, would give it a comfortable majority, while a deal with the far-right JA21, which has nine seats, would leave it one short and dependent on a third party.

PRO, JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP have all said the cabinet will eventually have to choose between a majority on the left or on the right. But Heinen has resisted that, backing a call this week by Christian-social ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker for the parties to drop the left-right divide and judge the plans on their merits.

Welfare cuts

Talks with PRO, the most straightforward route to a majority, remain difficult. After a meeting on Thursday, the party’s finance spokesperson Luc Stultiens said he had seen little movement “and that will be needed if you want our support.”

PRO wants the cabinet to scrap €6.5 billion in planned cuts to social security and raise the money through higher taxes on wealth and corporations instead. Its position is backed by the unions, which have called a national public transport strike on September 9 in protest at the reforms.

JA21 and the SGP, which are working together, met ministers again on Friday morning, with the ChristenUnie due later in the day. The budget is set to be presented on Prinsjesdag, September 15.

World.title: Government condemns Israeli West Bank settlement plan
World.content:
The Netherlands has joined six other governments in condemning Israel’s decision to open bidding on a major settlement project in the occupied West Bank, and called on the Netanyahu regime to withdraw the plans immediately.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Norway called the project “unacceptable” in a joint statement, and said they have “grave concerns” over the potential impact it could have on achieving peace in the region, particularly amid “unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians.”

Israel’s construction and housing ministry opened bidding on Tuesday for 1,234 homes, part of a wider plan for 3,401 settler homes in E1, an area east of Jerusalem. Contractors have until October 19 to bid, a week before Israeli elections.

Critics say the project would split the West Bank in two and cut East Jerusalem off from it, making a contiguous Palestinian state impossible.

The condemnation comes as the Netherlands prepares to enforce its own ban on settlement goods, which takes effect on September 22. The three-year measure bars the import, sale and trade of goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories.

The Netherlands is also the main EU entry point for produce grown in Israeli settlements, according to research published in June, handling around a third of such shipments reaching the bloc.

Settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law. The E1 plan, approved last year, faces a legal challenge in Israel, where a court has asked the state to respond to the petitions by September 1.

World.title: Police shooting in Sittard wounds Nijmegen man

Police in Sittard in Limburg shot a man outside the city’s police station on Stationsplein overnight Friday due to what they called a “suspicious situation”.

The suspect, a 34-year-old man from Nijmegen, was injured in the leg and received first aid on the scene. He was then arrested and transferred to hospital.

Police shootings are rare in the Netherlands. Last year, officers shot at people 15 times.

Still, the national police are investigating the incident, as all cases involving an officer shooting that results in injury or death must be looked into.

Police are also looking into the cause and background of the incident.

World.title: New medicine gives hope to Dutch narcolepsy sufferers
World.content:
Some 8,000 Dutch people suffer from narcolepsy, a sleep disorder that leaves sufferers spontaneously falling asleep during the day.

Now, for the first time, a new drug approved earlier this month in the US is being touted as the first to target the disease’s roots rather than its symptoms.

“I have been trying to give people a reasonable life for 40 years,” Gert Jan Lammers, special professor of sleep disorders at Leiden University Medical Centre, told broadcaster NOS. “With this medicine, we finally saw real improvement.”

Several of his patients participated in the drug’s research trials, and he says the results are positive. “People feel normal again. I’ve been working on this for 40 years now and I haven’t seen this before. It doesn’t work perfectly for everyone, and it doesn’t work all day, but it’s fundamentally different from what we’ve been able to do so far.”

The drug, Orzeyful (oveporexton) still has to be approved by the European Medicines Agency before being prescribed in the Netherlands, which will likely not happen until at least the end of next year.

But for those who have taken it, including Dutch trial participants who can continue using it before its approval here, it’s been a life-changer.

“It’s like you’re finally getting a good pair of glasses,” says Leontien Sickenga, who has taken the drug for one and one-half years. “With other medication I saw the world a bit better, but with this medication the world is clear. When I’m awake, I’m really there.”

In addition to falling asleep in the day, Sickenga also suffered from muscle relaxation and sleep paralysis, common in narcolepsy patients. “It’s very drastic,” she said.

How it works

According to the US Food and Drug Administration, narcolepsy “is caused by the loss of brain cells that produce orexin, a chemical messenger that regulates wakefulness, sleep, and muscle tone.”

Without orexin, the brain has trouble controlling the boundaries between sleep and waking, resulting in narcolepsy’s debilitating symptoms. But the new drug, rather than trying to relieve those symptoms, “directly activates the same brain receptor that the body’s own orexin would normally stimulate, restoring the missing signal.”

Professor of sleep diagnostics Sebastiaan Overeem, who was not involved in the drug’s research, is positive. “This is fundamentally new and very promising,” he says. “Of course, there are no miracle cures, and we still have to see how this drug works in the long run. But in the field, everyone is impressed.”

Side effects of the drug include urinating more, and it’s not yet known how effective it will be in the long-term.

“I don’t want to be too positive, because some things we can’t know yet” says Lammers. “But so far, all the signals are on green.”

World.title: Frisian asylum center to remain open, frustrating locals
World.content:
The ministry of justice and security informed the municipality of De Fryske Marren earlier this week that the asylum seekers’ centre in Balk, which was due to permanently shut its doors on October 1 2026, will remain open for another three years, upsetting local officials.

“For the municipal executive, the following applies: a deal is a deal,” says the municipality’s website. “The fact that the agreements cannot be fulfilled now causes disappointment and frustration.”

And, reports Omrop Fryslân, will lead to legal action.

The asylum centre opened in 2016 for what was supposed to be five years. That period was extended several times, most recently in 2024, when a deal was also made to reduce the number of refugees living in the centre from 500 to 225.

While the number of asylum seekers has been reduced, refugee settlement agency COA said the lack of alternative shelters means it can’t meet the October closure deadline.

Closure not an option

“We have been looking for other solutions for as long as possible”, said COA’s Joeri Kapteijns. “However, we have the legal and social responsibility to welcome and guide people safely and with dignity. As a result, closure without an alternative is not an option.”

Closing the Balk shelter, said COA, would “mean that 300 people, families and children, will be on the streets.”

The municipality says it doesn’t want to see people on the streets, but it’s unacceptable that the deal has been broken.

“Although De Fryske Marren wants to prevent residents from being left without suitable shelter from a human point of view, it does not accept this situation,” said the municipality. “The responsibility for the residents and replacement shelter lies primarily with COA.”

But COA says the nationwide shortage of asylum spots means it takes time. “Although fewer people are registering for asylum in the Netherlands than before, the number of residents at our locations is increasing.” Some 80,000 people currently live in asylum centres.

COA attributes the problem to long asylum procedures and too few homes for people with a residence permit, meaning more people have to stay longer in shelters. “There are fewer new locations opening than there are closing,” it said.

The 300 asylum seekers in Balk, however, fulfil De Fryske Marren’s shelter obligations under the country’s distribution laws.

World.title: Ajax win at Sion, Twente lose at home in Conference League
World.content:
Ajax and FC Twente played the first legs of their Conference League play-off ties on Thursday evening, the last stage before the competition’s league phase. Ajax won 4-2 away at FC Sion in Switzerland, while Twente lost 1-0 at home to FK Qarabag.

Ajax fell behind to a goal just after 30 minutes but recovered after the break. Julian Brandt and Marcos Leonardo scored to put the visitors in front, before Sion equalised from the penalty spot through Ylyas Chouaref.

Tolu Arokodare headed in within a minute of coming on to restore the lead, and Davy Klaassen lobbed a fourth late on.

The match was shown in the Netherlands only on a €4.99 pay-per-view channel, a decision that had angered many fans in the build-up. Ajax will go through as long as they avoid losing by three or more goals in next Thursday’s return at the Johan Cruijff Arena.

Twente jeered at home

Twente had a good start in Enschede but faded, and Kady Borges scored shortly after half-time to hand Qarabag the lead. The home crowd began jeering the team, whistling at the players at full time and cheering the substitution of striker Wout Weghorst.

Qarabag, multiple-time Azerbaijani champions, reached the Champions League knockout stage last season. Both Dutch clubs had come through the previous qualifying round last week. Twente now face a difficult second leg in Baku next Thursday.

World.title: How will the Law and Justice split affect Polish politics?
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. By Aleks Szczerbiak The biggest-ever split within Poland’s main right-wing opposition party is a serious self-inflicted wound, signalling a more fragmented conservative landscape and complicating the right’s path back to power. While it provides a tactical boost for the Tusk government, there is still every chance of a conservative comeback if the right-wing parties cooperate effectively. Radical-right challengers At the end of last month, the right-wing Law and Justice (PiS) party, Poland’s ruling party between 2015 and 2023 and currently the main opposition grouping, saw the biggest split in its 25-year history. The rupture was the culmination of months of increasingly open and bitter factional conflict over the party’s future direction. PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right. However, it lost power following the October 2023 parliamentary election, which led to the formation of a coalition headed up by Donald Tusk, leader of the liberal-centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party. Since last autumn, PiS has seen its polling numbers decline to the party’s lowest level of support for 15 years. At the same time, it has been challenged by two radical right competitors: the free-market Confederation (Konfederacja) and the ultra-nationalist Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), which together began to match, or even exceed, PiS’s level of support. Responding to declining support At the heart of this conflict was a bitter clash between longtime party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and Mateusz Morawiecki, who served as PiS prime minister from 2017 to 2023 but grew increasingly impatient with the former’s dominance. Two main factions emerged centred on a bitter dispute on how the party should respond to declining support and political competition on its right flank. The hardline traditionalist-conservative faction, often referred to as the “butter-makers” (maślarze), was more Eurosceptic and advocated a clearer right-wing agenda that included pushing ahead with radical state reconstruction and promoting a conservative vision of national identity and traditional values. In their reading, PiS lost support to its right-wing competitors because it was not radical enough and the solution was to sharpen its ideological profile and double down on hardline rhetoric. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 This group gained influence in party structures and when, in March, Kaczyński designated one of its key figures, former education minister Przemysław Czarnek, as the party’s prime ministerial candidate in the next parliamentary election, scheduled for autumn 2027, this was widely seen as a clear signal favouring the traditionalist-conservative faction. Morawiecki and his allies in the modernising-technocratic faction, often called the “scouts” (harcerze), also had strong conservative values and at times were very critical of Poland’s post-1989 establishment. However, they advocated a strategy of stressing economic competence, pragmatic governance and boosting Polish prosperity over hardline rhetoric on moral-cultural issues as a more effective way of appealing to voters less influenced by traditional institutions such as the Catholic church. Although they were also critical of Brussels overreach, Morawiecki’s faction preferred to avoid escalating conflict with the EU and argued that PiS had to broaden its appeal to younger, urban, more centrist-conservative Poles who found radical cultural rhetoric off-putting. Programmatic differences and personal ambitions The conflict became so destabilising because, although rooted in genuine programmatic and strategic disagreements, personalities and individual ambitions also played a major role. While Kaczyński maintained formal control of the party, his advancing age escalated debates over PiS’s direction and leadership, and these tensions intensified after the party failed to translate its presidential candidate Karol Nawrocki’s surprise summer 2025 election victory into broader momentum. For his part, Morawiecki grew increasingly impatient and frustrated as hardliners sidelined him, while his supporters were afraid that they would be excluded from PiS candidate lists at the next election. These long-simmering tensions came to a head in April, when Morawiecki announced the formation of Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), a think tank-like platform focused on economic development The association was widely interpreted by Kaczyński and PiS hardliners as a direct challenge to party unity and the leader’s authority. The leadership ruled that Development Plus violated the PiS statute, which explicitly prohibits members from joining political organisations that conflict with the party’s goals. While Morawiecki insisted that it was simply a modest intra-party policy forum, by registering an organisation with dozens of parliamentarians, he gave his faction a formal institutional shell that could potentially act as a launchpad for his own rival breakaway party. Initially, Kaczyński and Morawiecki came to a compromise agreement whereby Development Plus would work within an official party expert group. However, in July the situation escalated when the PiS leadership issued an ultimatum banning members from participating in internal political factions (clearly targeting Development Plus) and instructing parliamentarians to sign loyalty declarations confirming that they were not involved in any such groupings. Most complied, but 40 parliamentarians affiliated with Development Plus refused to do so, accusing the leadership of political blackmail. Ultimately, Kaczyński announced that, by refusing to sign, Morawiecki and his allies had effectively left the party, while Development Plus framed it as expulsion over policy differences caused by “plotters” surrounding the party leader. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 An even more fragmented right The loss of 40 deputies means that PiS is no longer the largest parliamentary caucus, thus losing procedural advantages, committee control and visibility. The departing group includes many experienced and talented politicians, particularly in the economic and foreign policy fields. The split also reduces PiS’s funding, staffing, and in some regions local organisation, as well as creating the risk of demoralisation and further defections. Even if the Polish right secures a parliamentary majority at the next election, PiS’s relative influence could be greatly reduced. Although Kaczyński’s formal party leadership remains unquestioned, the split signals to the broader right that his authority is waning and undermines his claim to be the undisputed hegemon and central broker on the right; he is increasingly now one leader among several. It also further erodes the model that Kaczyński has built over many years as the main ideologue and ultimate arbiter of internal PiS factions. In earlier crises, this personal authority and control gave him leverage to keep everyone on board so that disagreements were managed internally, and even disillusioned figures usually stayed in, or returned to, the party. Indeed, by adding a fourth distinctive player, the PiS split further compounds the divisions on the Polish right that have deepened since the last election, transforming what was once a relatively consolidated “big tent” bloc into a multi-polar competitive field. For sure, polls conducted after the split show the combined right-wing vote as competitive overall, but even if this level of support remains stable, or even increases slightly, it is now divided across more options. This is significant because Poland’s proportional electoral system uses the d’Hondt counting system that favours larger groupings. It also creates the risk that smaller right-wing parties such as Morawiecki’s new grouping could fall below the 5% parliamentary representation threshold, so their votes are excluded from seat allocation. All of this makes it harder for the right to translate raw voter support into political power. Moreover, even if the right-wing parties win a combined parliamentary majority, post-election coordination becomes much more complex with four (or more) actors whose leaders’ rivalries, different priorities and historical animosities complicate forming a stable coalition government. Nawrocki’s role will be crucial In the light of this, Nawrocki has emerged as a critical unifier with crossover appeal across the fractured Polish right. His presidential election victory showed that he could attract support well beyond traditional PiS loyalists and consolidate a broad right-wing coalition, including the vast majority of voters from both Confederations. As president, he operates outside direct party control and has cultivated an image as an authoritative unifying figure on the right, which gives him much greater moral and symbolic stature than a partisan leader immersed in day-to-day machinations. Nawrocki has also used his constitutional powers and standing, including a legislative veto that the government lacks the three-fifths parliamentary majority to overturn, to position himself assertively as a powerful counterweight to the Tusk administration, and is currently Poland’s most popular politician. Nonetheless, Nawrocki’s potential to act as a possible right-wing unifier and broker is limited. For sure, he can use the presidency to set a broad conservative agenda and mediate negotiations among the various right-wing groupings to secure pre- and post-election agreements. Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland's largest opposition party, PiS, has called on President @NawrockiKn to help unify the country’s various right-wing opposition forces ahead of next year’s parliamentary elections https://t.co/Q3BFSOSfTG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 10, 2026 However, Nawrocki has no formal unifying mandate and his success ultimately depends on whether the various actors are willing to be led. Without broader cooperation, even his efforts will only mitigate, not eliminate, the damage from a divided right, and personal and ideological rivalries currently run deep and cannot be easily overridden. Moreover, not only is the president expected to remain formally above the fray and not engage too openly in day-to-day politics, he also lacks the control over party organisational machinery needed to micro-manage and enforce messy backroom deals. Pivotal but not transformative? Initial polling conducted since the split suggests that Morawiecki’s new grouping would likely clear the 5% threshold and enter parliament with a small-to-medium-sized fraction; according to Politico Europe, it is currently averaging around 6% support. Although this could make it a pivotal player in coalition talks, it does not suggest that the grouping can dramatically reshape the country’s political landscape. Moreover, its support appears to be drawn mainly from PiS’s traditional electoral base, so it is simply further fragmenting the existing right-wing vote rather than drawing in a significant number of new voters who hitherto supported the governing coalition parties. For sure, Morawiecki‘s project has advantages that many newcomers lack, notably its leader’s very high name recognition and a sizeable bloc of high-profile, political heavyweight allies, much larger than any previous PiS breakaway faction. His grouping immediately became the third largest parliamentary fraction, giving it visibility, funding, and organisational backbone. However, although there are some rare exceptions that usually involve major figures with significant resources breaking from established parties, it is a familiar pattern in post-1989 Polish politics for a brand new “startup” party to show an early bounce, benefiting from initial media coverage, only to fade or disappear as voters drift back to more established groupings or abstain at the next election. Sustaining momentum requires local organisational infrastructure, reliable funding, rapid professionalisation, and a clear identity, which new parties often lack. Indeed, to be successful a new startup should really attract at least 10% support initially simply because of its “newness”. Over the years, PiS breakaway politicians have established new parties that either quickly disappeared from the political scene or were eventually reintegrated into the grouping. Temporary relief for Tusk From a short-term tactical perspective, the PiS split is a welcome political gift for the Tusk government, shifting the media focus away from criticisms of its record and recent scandals and controversies. It has for example, blunted the opposition’s ability to maintain a sustained assault over a scandal involving high earnings for, and mismanagement by, a KO-connected doctor, alleged VIP access and potential patient harm at the Warsaw South Hospital, which had previously dominated the summer news headlines. The ruling coalition is likely to survive until next year's election, but its prospects are hampered by a weak domestic record, writes @AleksSzczerbiak The government has therefore made security key to its reelection narrative, but that also carries risks https://t.co/w2UeNaTwAO — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 1, 2026 However, the PiS split has not resolved the deeper image and performance problems that have dragged down the Tusk government’s approval ratings. The administration struggles with perceptions of slow delivery on promises while facing a hostile president, and if these problems persist, or new controversies reignite strongly once the PiS drama cools, the government will very quickly find itself back on the defensive. The PiS split only provides temporary relief; to win the next election, the ruling coalition needs to improve its own standing, not rely on opposition mistakes. World.title: Polish NGOs urge PM’s “right-hand man” to withdraw constitutional court candidacy
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A group of Polish civil society organisations has urged a former government minister to withdraw his candidacy to become a Constitutional Tribunal (TK) judge, saying his close ties to the prime minister could undermine confidence in the court’s independence. In a joint statement, the nine organisations say that restoring the legitimacy of the court, which has been in crisis since 2015 following illegitimate judicial appointments made by the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, requires not only addressing legal irregularities but also rebuilding public trust. “The existence of the Constitutional Tribunal as an organ of judicial power only makes sense if it is an independent arbiter,” they say. 🔴Wspólnie z innymi organizacjami apelujemy do dr. M. Berka o rezygnację z kandydowania do TK, a do Sejmu o wybór osoby niezależnej politycznie. Droga do praworządności to nie „odbijanie” Trybunału, ale odbudowa jego autorytetu. Przeczytajcie nasz apel, link w komentarzu ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/LPlbk39lNr — Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka (@hfhrpl) August 20, 2026 The appeal follows Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s announcement that Maciej Berek, who until recently served as a government minister and whom Tusk has described as his “right-hand man”, would be put forward as a candidate for the Constitutional Tribunal. The choice has drawn particular attention because Tusk came to power promising to “depoliticise” the court after the previous PiS government appointed former politicians as judges. “Regardless of the extent to which the tribunal has become politicised, the way to reform this institution cannot be for it to be ‘recaptured’ or ‘taken over’ by another ruling majority,” the NGOs write in the statement. The organisations, including the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights, the Institute of Public Affairs and the Stefan Batory Foundation, say Berek’s close ties to the current political leadership could cause his appointment to be perceived as political, regardless of his legal qualifications or personal integrity. “Not only must courts and tribunals operate independently and impartially, but citizens must also recognise and have confidence in that independence and impartiality. This is not possible when judges are appointed whose links to the government are immediately apparent,” the organisations add. “We therefore call on Dr Maciej Berek to withdraw his candidacy in the interests of the independence of the constitutional judiciary.” The proportion of Poles who negatively assess the justice system has increased under the current government, despite its promises to restore the rule of law. State pollster @CBOS_Info found 61% now hold a negative view, up from 55% in 2022 and 51% in 2017 https://t.co/P3fbTTbS5C — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 12, 2026 The organisations also argue that Berek’s nomination goes against a principle that the current ruling coalition sought to introduce: that anyone who has held political office within the previous four years should be barred from appointment to the tribunal. Berek was a government minister until last week. The coalition’s proposal was included in a bill approved by parliament in 2024. However, the Constitutional Tribunal itself later ruled the provision unconstitutional after former President Andrzej Duda, an ally of PiS, referred the legislation for review. “Although this law has not come into force, it would be reasonable for the Sejm to adhere to the standard it has adopted,” they said, referring to the lower chamber of the parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 However, the selection of Berek, whose candidacy was put forward by MPs from Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO), has exposed divisions within the ruling coalition, which ranges from centre-right to left. “We were supposed to be different from PiS; we were supposed to do things differently, not exactly the same way,” Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, told Polsat News. Paweł Śliz, leader of the centre-right Poland 2050’s (Polska 2050) caucus, said Berek would make an excellent Constitutional Tribunal judge were it not for his recent role as a government minister. “I consider him an excellent, outstanding professional; I value his experience and expertise. However, my position on this matter is unequivocal. I will not compromise my principles,” he told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The chief justice of the constitutional court has refused to accept four new judges appointed by parliament but whom the opposition-aligned president has refused to swear in. The decision deepens an unprecedented standoff over Poland's top court https://t.co/B02DKA3uBL — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 9, 2026 Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition opposing Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. Last week, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Presidential spokesman Rafał Leśkiewicz told PAP on Thursday that “there are serious doubts” about Berek’s formal qualifications to become a Constitutional Tribunal judge. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland summons Israeli ambassador over discontinued investigation into killing of Gaza aid workers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has summoned Israel’s ambassador to express its “great disappointment” that the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) have discontinued an investigation into the strikes on an aid convoy in Gaza in 2024 that killed seven humanitarian workers, including a Pole, Damian Soból. “Partnership requires mutual respect,” declared foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, as well as the failure of accountability for [the] IDF’s excessive use of force[,] are undermining public support in even pro-Israel nations.” Partnership requires mutual respect. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, as well as the failure of accountability for IDF’s excessive use of force are undermining public support in even pro-Israel nations. https://t.co/9H0nhiDE4H — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) August 20, 2026 The incident in question took place in April 2024, when Israeli drones struck a convoy delivering humanitarian aid from World Central Kitchen (WCK), a major international food relief NGO. The attack killed seven aid workers, including Soból. The incident caused outrage in Poland, whose government demanded that Israel fully explain the circumstances. The IDF expressed “sincere sorrow” over the deaths and pledged to carry out a “thorough and transparent” investigation. On Wednesday this week, the IDF announced that it had closed the case after determining “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct that would justify the opening of a criminal investigation or the taking of additional measures against any of those involved in the incident”. The IDF said that its troops had identified a gunman on one of the trucks in the convoy. It also claimed that WCK had hired an armed security force to protect the convoy without coordinating that with IDF authorities and that the convoy deviated from the route previously agreed with the IDF. However, the IDF also acknowledged that it had mistakenly identified several individuals as being armed. It added that attempts to contact WCK representatives over a half-hour period while the convoy was on the move were unsuccessful. The IDF noted that, after the incident, two military officers were removed from their positions while three others were reprimanded. But it found that there was no basis for any further action. ⚖️ IDF prosecution rules on five FFAM cases: The IDF says its General Staff Fact-Finding and Assessment Mechanism has completed reviews of approximately 150 exceptional wartime incidents since the beginning of the war and transferred them to the Military Prosecution. Decisions… pic.twitter.com/H5g4qOu5e2 — Israel Realtime (@IsraelRealtime) August 19, 2026 On Thursday, Poland’s foreign ministry issued a statement saying that it was “greatly disappointed to receive the information provided about the discontinuation of the proceedings by the Israeli military authorities”. It announced that it had summoned the Israeli ambassador in order to “communicate a critical assessment of the actions taken to date to clarify the causes and course of the tragedy”. It also noted that Polish prosecutors are still conducting their own investigation and that the foreign ministry had informed the Israeli ambassador that they “expect the Israeli side will provide the relevant Polish authorities with all necessary explanations and materials requested”. “The circumstances of the tragedy should be fully investigated and [we] do not accept that the perpetrators are avoiding legal and moral responsibility,” concluded the ministry, adding that “the families deserve adequate compensation”. We strongly condemn the Israeli military prosecutor’s account of the deaths of our seven colleagues on April 1, 2024. And we fundamentally disagree with their decision about criminal investigations into the IDF airstrikes that killed our team. Read our full statement here:… — World Central Kitchen (@WCKitchen) August 19, 2026 The IDF’s findings were also condemned by WCK itself, which called them “inconsistent with the full truth and deeply offensive”. It added that, “at the time of the lethal attacks, the IDF knew that our team in Gaza was unarmed and posing a threat to nobody”. The NGO repeated its demand for an independent investigation into the incident, “because the IDF cannot credibly investigate its own conduct”. On Friday, the UK, Canada and Australia, whose citizens were also killed in the strike, issued a joint statement calling the IDF’s decision to drop the investigation “shameful” and another example of the lack of accountability for incidents in Gaza. Joint statement from the foreign ministries of Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom on Israel closing the investigation into strikes on the World Central Kitchen convoy in Gaza on 1 April 2024 ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/V3CZe286tN — Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (@FCDOGovUK) August 21, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
