World.title: Water, everywhere. What are we to think?
World.content:
NationalNSWLetters Water, everywhere. What are we to think? August 22, 2026 — 9:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Last week it was revealed that an extension to operations had been granted to a major coal mine. Somewhat paradoxically, massive challenges due to sea level rise were reviewed in The Sun-Herald (“Battling against Mother Nature to stop suburbs sinking into the sea”, August 16). Climate science unequivocally indicates that burning fossil fuel contributes carbon dioxide to the Earth’s atmosphere. This gas does eventually dissipate. However, while present production is maintained, even at half the rate, the greenhouse effect will continue to grow, leading to global warming and, at present, accelerating sea level rise. As portrayed in this excellent article, it is now acknowledged that the problems confronting NSW are immense – both in scale and cost to the private and public purse. Yet, some politicians advocate increasing the use of fossil fuel when they should be confronting the challenges and endeavouring to find solutions to this human-induced threat. Roger Epps, Armidale Do we want more of this in future? Lismore in the 2025 floods. Nick Moir The concerns of residents living in areas of coastal flooding are a human species concern. We chose to build at the edge of the water. Is that any concern of the sea, which expands to increase its own habitable space? Is anything we do of concern to the planet? It’s been here for billions of years and will be here long after we have become extinct either by dint of our own bellicose nature or by dint of cosmic processes. Frederick Jansohn, Rose Bay From Nero to hero? Although the image of Nero fiddling while Rome burned is yet another example of politically motivated fake news, it is true to say that the contemporary world has its fair share of “Neros”, content to fiddle while this planet burns (“Scientists warn of grass fires in the Antarctic”, August 16). They fiddle with the inconvenient truth, they fiddle with resource inequity, they fiddle with international conflicts, and they fiddle with the prospects of future generations. Rome may have taken considerably more than a day to rebuild. But our home, Earth? It’s an ominous question. Steve Dillon, Thirroul



Asylum sunseekers The growing flow of temporary visa holders should be no surprise (“Holidaying Brits seek asylum to stay longer”, August 16). Our current visa systems were designed and developed for the Olympics in the late 1990s and intended to deal with the rapid entry of crowds of visitors in 2000. At the time, it was a world first digital system and a global benchmark. The single attempt at a comprehensive modern replacement – the Morrison government’s ill-fated $1 billion privatisation scheme – was scrapped in 2020. Several reviews since have found it no longer fit for purpose, trapping the skilled tradies and other workers we need in broken pathways to permanent residency. It will take time. Margaret Wright, Millers Point If the application is genuine, and not someone seeking more time in the sun sleeping or fruit picking, then immediately remove any asylum seekers to a secure location where their claim can be assessed in a timely manner by dedicated experts. Howard Springs? Woomera? Koolan Island? Those fleeing war and persecution will welcome this care and security. Those fleeing a northern winter will not. David Neilson, Uralla Take both barrels As one who believes that possession of firearms by anyone other than authorised law enforcement agencies should be prohibited, I am completely in favour of the plan to confiscate private collections (“NSW launches massive gun buyback program”, August 16). The figures revealed by The Sun-Herald show that gun ownership in suburban areas has risen to be a form of mental illness. New laws to be introduced will “restrict” primary producers and sport shooters to 10. This is ridiculous; does a first class cricketer need 10 cricket bats? You can hear Barnaby Joyce foaming at the mouth now, claiming that city folk have no understanding of their country cousins. What we do understand is that the more guns that are available, the higher the chance one is used to take a life. Ian Adair, Hunters Hill



The planned gun buyback in November is a great plan. Whether the gun is a “vintage” weapon or for sporting purposes, we read daily about how the proliferation and availability of guns in the US gives rise to daily shooting fatalities. TV gives us the constant scenario to use a gun to end any type of discussion. This buyback is an attempt to avoid those daily deadly headlines here. Marjie Williamson, Blaxland Pistons at electoral dawn With both the Parramatta Powerhouse and the Southwest Metro opening later this year, one could be forgiven for thinking we have a state election early next year (“Opening date of Powerhouse in west revealed”, August 16). Peter Miniutti, Ashbury ‘Lightweights’ and heavy weather What a debacle from Australia’s Test side (“Batters in the gun as Aussies face an embarrassing defeat”, August 16). For the first time in a long while, a full-strength Aussie XI – every top player was playing, so no selection excuses, no experimental lineups – and yet, they were comprehensively outplayed in every department by a Bangladesh team that is not considered a heavyweight in Test cricket, and that too on a home ground wicket in Darwin. This was a straight, undeniable defeat. No caveats, no soft landings. So, eat a big humble pie, acknowledge the failure, and reset. It looked like a complacent team. Summer tests will be challenging, with temperatures soaring, humidity draining energy and every side being tested physically and mentally. If Australia cannot lift its standards now, the season ahead will expose them further. Mukul Desai, Hunters Hill

World.title: Preston in hospital on drip before Bulldogs game, five players with Covid
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 Preston in hospital on drip before Bulldogs game, five players with Covid Chris Barrett August 22, 2026 — 11:54pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Canterbury have kept alive their slim finals hopes despite back-rower Jacob Preston spending two days in hospital on a drip, five players contracting Covid-19 and winger Jacob Kiraz secretly playing with a torn calf for the past three weeks. In yet another pre-match disruption, centre Matt Burton missed training in the lead-up to Saturday night’s must-win clash with St George Illawarra to return home to Dubbo for a family issue. Jacob Preston and the Bulldogs celebrate a try on Saturday night. Getty Images And before kick-off, Enari Tuala was ruled out with a knee injury which he aggravated at training. As far as preparations go, it is hard to envisage there being more interruptions.



The Bulldogs, however, performed as if it had been plain sailing for them all week, beating the Dragons 44-14 in a free-flowing and clinical display before a crowd of 14,711 at Allianz Stadium. The victory leaves the ninth-placed side two points behind South Sydney and North Queensland with two matches remaining. They still need results to go in their favour to make the top eight and their penultimate opponents of the regular season, Penrith, will present a steeper challenge next Friday night at CommBank Stadium. Loading But Canterbury will approach the round 26 blockbuster in the knowledge that they were the first team to beat the Panthers this season and with renewed verve after taking care of St George Illawarra comfortably.



The fact that they did so after the week they had - and following a deflating last-start defeat to South Sydney - was another vote of confidence. “These things happen in a footy season. Every team goes through them. A lot of them you don’t hear about,” Bulldogs coach Cameron Ciraldo said. “I was a bit harsh on the boys last week, and then you rock up Monday and about five of them have tested positive for COVID, so no wonder they were a bit flat.” On top of that, Preston, who has been in high-profile contract negotiations with the club, had been hospitalised ahead of the contest with an injection in his elbow. “So he was on a trip over the last couple of days,” Ciraldo said.



Not done with the post-game revelations, the coach then let slip that Kiraz had been quietly playing with a tear in his calf, having incurred the same injury on his other leg earlier this season. Burton, meanwhile, switched from left to right centre to accommodate the return of Bronson Xerri after having to skip training for family reasons. Along with Preston, he was a standout with a pair of tries and some try-saving defence. “I just feel like it balanced the team up a little bit,” Ciraldo said of Burton’s shift to the right. “Burto wanted that challenge of going on Val Holmes. They’re both Origin players and I think Burto was pretty excited by that.”



Related Article Match report The Warriors can challenge for the title. Souths need Latrell back to stand a chance In an impressive all-round outing, Burton and Preston were in good company. Xerri, making his first start in six weeks, demonstrated what he can provide to Canterbury before he heads to Melbourne next season with a try of his own, while halfback Lachlan Galvin scored one and set up two. A busy Jaeman Salmon and Bailey Hayward were other top performers while Ciraldo credited fullback Connor Tracey with his best game of the year. With Tuala due back next week, the only concerns for Canterbury as they turn their attention to Penrith were Salmon being placed on report twice and a groin injury that forced utility Kurt Mann off the field in the second half. They were too strong for the Dragons despite two periods in which they were reduced to 12 men.



Dean Young’s team gave a better account than the scoreline suggested but were undone by mistakes. They also lost hooker Jacob Liddle with a suspected torn calf. There were concerns the 29-year-old had ruptured his achilles, but those fears were eased by Dragons medical staff. “I hope it is just a calf,” said departing captain Damien Cook, who replaced Liddle when Liddle went off at the half-hour mark. “I was pretty worried for him. He’s someone I’ve enjoyed working along with. He’s been playing really good footy of late. He deserves to be starting and he’s going to do a great job for the team next year.”



The result snapped a two-game winning run for St George Illawarra and all but assured they will collect the wooden spoon. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Monday.

Geelong star Jeremy Cameron knew he needed to get tackled and run out a full game again before he could be fully ready for the finals.

Cameron missed the past four games with an AC joint issue and broken collarbone injury suffered in July.

Jeremy Cameron of the Cats handballs. Getty Images

“The medicos did a good job of putting me back together and getting me back out here. It was nice to get some run in the legs, I really needed it with what is ahead of us,” Cameron told Kayo Sports.

“I was sort of everywhere tonight. I was all over the place. I was just trying to get some run in the legs and get a feel for it. It will be really important for what is to come in the next month.

World.title: Wildcards locked in: Blues, Pies, Demons and Dogs learn their fate for history-making round
World.content:
Loading

In today’s AFL Briefing, your wrap of footy news: Carlton CEO Graham Wright opened up on the future of Elijah Hollands on the day their wildcard opponent was locked in.

Scott Pendlebury and Brayden Maynard are both set to miss the Pies’ wildcard clash with the Bulldogs. Elijah Hollands could have played his final game for us: Carlton CEO By Danny Russell and Russell Bennett Carlton chief executive Graham Wright doubts Elijah Hollands will return to play for the club as the Blues set their sights on a remarkable wildcard final against Melbourne. Wright was speaking before Carlton’s barnstorming win against ladder leader Fremantle at Marvel Stadium, a victory that sees Josh Fraser’s side hit the finals series with undeniable momentum. The Blues, who finished the home-and-away season in 10th, will now face the 7th-placed Demons in one wildcard final next week, while the Bulldogs will host Collingwood in the other.



Elijah Hollands suffered a mental health episode during a game early this season. AFL Photos Hollands, the 24-year-old midfielder-forward, hasn’t played at any level since round six of the AFL season, when he experienced a mental health episode on the field against Collingwood at the MCG. The Blues were later fined $75,000 for bringing the game into disrepute over their handling over the matter in April after the AFL said Hollands should have been removed from the field earlier than he was, citing visual clues, performance data during the match, and knowledge of his individual circumstances. “These findings have been made against the Carlton Football Club collectively, not against any individual,” league CEO Andrew Dillon said in a press conference in May. Speaking on 3AW on Saturday, Wright was asked directly if he thought Hollands would return to play at the club.



“I doubt it,” he said, adding that Hollands continues to receive support. Hollands (right) with then-Blues coach Michael Voss after the loss to Collingwood. AFL Photos “That’s coming through the club, but also, too, wider than that,” he said. “He hasn’t been back to the club, and he’s considering what he does, but certainly we’re just trying to be there and support him. “We’ll work out what that looks like from a futuristic point of view a little bit later on.”



The Blues fell four goals behind against the Dockers in the opening 12 minutes on Saturday, looking slow, outnumbered and second-rate. That’s when the Fraser way took hold. They rallied to close to within three points at the first break, led by 11 points at half-time and then dominated the second half to win 18.11 (119) to 12.10 (82). They had 114 more disposals and 56 more marks. The key to the early turnaround, midfield star Sam Walsh revealed, was “not making it a bit a bigger deal than it needed to be”. View post on X “At the moment, we’re probably assessing what’s not working and changing in game, which has been a growth,” he told The Age.



Carlton’s growth since round 10 was enormous. They had a devastating 1-8 start to the season and a series of second-half fadeouts that cost Michael Voss his job. They were continually hamstrung by the absence of a Plan B. Not any more. Under Fraser, they have catapulted themselves into the wild card round with an ominous momentum, winning 11 of their final 14 matches of the home-and-away season. But did they ever think finals were possible? “No, we couldn’t have,” Walsh said. “But the best thing we have done is that we didn’t even speak of getting to that point.



“Like we focus on, when Frase took over, what do we want to stand for? And then, from there, how do we get after it every week?” Getting after it was second nature for Walsh on Saturday. He was again outstanding. He had 32 possessions and kicked a goal against Fremantle to marginally shade boy wonder Jagga Smith, who helped himself to 31 disposals and also booted a major. Harry McKay with the Blues faithful after stunning the Dockers at Marvel Stadium. AFL Photos But it was the performance of the lesser lights under Fraser that helped the Blues climb into the finals. Cult hero Frankie Evans booted five goals against the Dockers, Gold Coast recruit Ben Ainsworth managed three and former Sydney rebound defender Ollie Florent was instrumental in their attacking thrusts, amassing 29 disposals at Marvel Stadium in their final home-and-away game.



Even the returned Ollie Hollands had an opportunity to shine. He brought the Carlton faithful to their feet with an inspiring run-down tackle on super villain Patrick Voss that saved a certain goal. But despite this growing adulation and rising expectation from the success-starved Blues army, there was no way the new Blues coach would allow the lid to come off. That was old Carlton. “I think the context of where we’ve come from, and maybe the context of the club more broadly, that maybe in the past it’s been outcome-based,” Fraser said. “Maybe I’m speculating a little bit because I haven’t really lived it. But we’ve got a method right now that is working for us, and I think if we stray too far away from that, then there’s some danger attached to it as well.” Fraser was right. While the Blues had beaten flag favourites Fremantle and the Brisbane Lions in the past month, there were caveats attached to those wins, especially on Saturday.



The Dockers were not at their best. They left Murphy Reid, Jye Amiss, Heath Chapman and Sam Switkowski in Perth. They also treated their bench like a game of musical chairs, constantly managing the game time of their biggest names – Luke Jackson, Caleb Serong, Alex Pearce and Shai Bolton. Fremantle coach Justin Longmuir said he was disappointed in the loss, but he was hardly convincing. “I thought we got out of it pretty well in terms of what we wanted to do with minimising risk and game time,” Longmuir said. View post on X



The low point for the Dockers was losing Brennan Cox with a calf injury that will rule him out of their first final in a fortnight. “There was a lot of moving parts today in terms of the team we picked, who we left out, and then Coxy going down didn’t help,” Longmuir said. “But we’ll put it behind us pretty quickly, and reflect on the season. And we should have really good belief [going forward].” The Blues stand to regain Nick Haynes and Will Hayward next week, and were able to rest key defender Jacob Weitering for a large slice of the final term. Pendlebury’s playing future clouded following injury



By Jon Pierik Scott Pendlebury will miss Collingwood’s cutthroat wildcard final next week against the Bulldogs and could well have played his final match in black and white. The Magpies revealed on Saturday that the VFL/AFL games-record holder (on 442) had suffered a hamstring strain in the club’s loss to the Brisbane Lions at the MCG on Friday night, ruling him out for “two to three weeks”. Will Ashcroft and Scott Pendlebury after their blockbuster clash on Friday night. AFL Photos In a further blow to Collingwood, rugged defender Brayden Maynard strained the MCL in his left knee during a Saturday-morning training session and will also miss their wildcard clash against the Western Bulldogs next week.



The Bulldogs have a worry of their own. Despite a courageous 21-point win over Melbourne at the MCG to hold on to eighth place, the Dogs will sweat on an ankle injury to key forward Aaron Naughton, who hobbled from the ground after landing heavily in a marking contest. View post on X The Pendlebury injury will leave coach Craig McRae lamenting a decision to play his veteran leader in a match that ultimately had no bearing on their ladder position. Many felt he should have rested the former skipper. “These are obviously disappointing setbacks for both Scott and Brayden,” Magpies head of football Charlie Gardiner said on Saturday afternoon. “Scott experienced tightness in the back of his knee during last night’s game. Scans earlier today confirmed a hamstring strain, and we expect Scott to be sidelined for two to three weeks.



Related Article AFL 2026 The moment that might have ended the most storied of Collingwood careers “Brayden unfortunately left the track early this morning during a training session, with scans confirming he sustained a grade one MCL strain. This is the same knee but unrelated to his earlier injury. “These are unfortunate setbacks, especially at this time of year but Scott and Brayden are absolute professionals and will do all they can to get back as quickly as possible.” Australian Football Hall of Fame Legend, and 1990 Collingwood premiership coach, Leigh Matthews said it would be wrong for Collingwood to allow Pendlebury to make his own call on his playing future, declaring the Magpies needed to deliver honest feedback. Pendlebury, 38, finished the clash against the Lions with what was initially thought to be a knee bursa issue (swelling near the joint).



He is set to become an unrestricted free agent, with several clubs linked to his services if he opts to play elsewhere in 2027. Magpies president Barry Carp said on Friday night that the choice was in Pendlebury’s hands, but Matthews said any decision should largely be the club’s call. “Not in my opinion, it’s never the player’s call,” Matthews told 3AW on Saturday. “But Scott Pendlebury is a high-class person. If [coach] Craig McRae and the football people said: ‘We think it’s probably time’, I think he would accept that. And that’s the way the conversation should go. “But a player just can’t say, ‘I want to play, I don’t care if you don’t think I am up to it, I just want to play and I want a contract.’



“But even Barry Carp, I don’t think he would go that far. I think if the football department said: ‘No, we just think it’s time’, I probably suspect Scott Pendlebury would accept that himself. “It’s a joint conversation, but it can’t be unilaterally [that] the player decides, otherwise he would play until he is 50.” Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: Black Ferns find their ruthless side
World.content:
Coach Whitney Hansen called for ruthlessness from her side, and unfortunately for the Wallaroos in their 100th test, the Black Ferns delivered.

New Zealand ran riot in Auckland with a 66-19 rout of the Wallaroos, scoring 10 tries to retain the O'Reilly Cup in emphatic style.

The relentless nature of the performance was particularly pleasing for Hansen.

"That's one of the things we've been searching for. We're pretty proud of the fact that it wasn't just a 40 minute effort, it was 80."

Ticking further boxes was the trio of debutants Elinor Plum-King, Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a and Amarante Sititi all seamlessly stepping up on the international stage.

"None of them let us down today. Pretty exciting to see two of them score, and that's off the back of King getting three last week too. I think they came in and they did their roles well and, to be able to be really confident in the black jersey, we've gained some real confidence in them, too."

Hansen said after a brutal domestic season, the players are primed for test rugby.

"We have competition in Aupiki that is the most physical internationally and that's a brand of rugby we want to play and we absolutely show that today. We are pretty proud of what we did do, but we also know there's lots out there that we can be better at too."

Skipper Ruahei Demant said the competition for places in the squad is fierce.

"I thought this week our girls who didn't get the opportunity to strip up really challenged us in every single training that we had. The girls respected the opposition, we respected each other and the ball, and we stayed really disciplined to stick to our game plan right from the start."

She said the senior members in the team have been sure to make the rookies welcome.

"I think that that is always the mark of a very healthy environment. Environments where people can be themselves. So for young players coming through, the future of our Black Ferns team, being able to be their authentic selves off the field, you see how that confidence translates into performances like today."

Demant again led a stirring haka prior to kick off, one which the Australians responded to by getting into boomerang formation and walking forward.

"We knew Aussie was going to be tough and we saw that with the response of the haka today, they were going to bring it and so I'm super proud of the physicality we brought in the first 20 minutes and then continue to do throughout the game.

"It's cool to see that they accept the challenge and respect our culture and respect our haka. I was really proud of the mana that the girls brought, you could feel that. The team feels that, and we use that to strengthen us as we lay down our challenge."

Despite the domination on display, Demant said they are still far from the finished product.

"There's lots of things that still need to be better and we'll dig into those because it's our next chance to do that will be South Africa. So getting really clear on what went well, where we can be better on."

A slight blight on the afternoon was the noticeably sparse crowd, numbering only around 6000.

Hansen however felt the game was still in a strong position in Aotearoa.

"I think it's growing in New Zealand and we've seen that our game can capture numbers .. across Aupiki and a couple of different times and our team's worked really hard to bring this one to life.

World.title: Warriors go top - for now - after thrilling win over South Sydney
World.content:
The Warriors have surged clear of South Sydney to win 45-26 to notch a fourth-straight win in the NRL and climb provisionally to the top of the standings.

After dominating the first half to lead 26-8 in Sydney, the Warriors needed to withstand a fightback from the Rabbitohs before late tries to Jacob Laban and Alofiana Khan-Pereira made the result safe.

Luke Hanson, introduced in the halves for just his second start because of a host of injuries in the Warriors playmaker ranks, then calmly slotted a field goal in the last play of the match.

It was enough to lift the Warriors one point ahead of the Panthers on points differential.

The Sydney Roosters could yet leapfrog both teams if they are victorious against the Wests Tigers on Sunday.

Either way, the Warriors are well-placed to push for a valuable top two finish, with their remaining regular season games both at home - against mid-table opponents Newcastle and Manly.

The Warriors unleashed another bright attacking display, although it was clouded by a shoulder injury suffered by Dallin Watene-Zelezniak.

Dallin Watene-Zelezniak holding an injured shoulder after scoring against South Sydney. photosport

The speedy winger was forced from the field after diving to score a try early in the second half, with initial reports suggesting it could be an AC joint injury.

Hanson slotted neatly into the Warriors patterns while once again Chanel Harris-Tavita shone, this time wearing the less-familiar No.7 jersey.

Harris-Tavita scored the last try of a dominant Warriors first half display, having also set up another to Leka Halasima via a towering bomb.

Mitchell Barnett of the Warriors scores a try against South Sydney. photosport

Front-rower co-captains James Fisher-Harris and Mitchell Barnett were the other early try-scorers, both off subtle playmaking from hooker Wayde Egan.

It was the first loss at Accor Stadium this season for the Rabbitohs and completed a memorable week for coach Andrew Webster.

World.title: Strong winds hampering firefighters at large Wānaka blaze
World.content:
A large fire that forced evacuations in Wānaka has been brought under control, but strong winds and steep terrain are making it difficult for firefighters to reach the remaining flames.

About 22 homes were evacuated in Wānaka's Albert Town on Saturday night, as the huge flames burned close to residential streets.

Fire and Emergency NZ said they were alerted to the vegetation fire in an area made up of gullies and steep hills, just before 7:30pm on Saturday, and had been attacking it from "multiple points".

In a briefing after 10pm on Saturday, Fire and Emergency District Assistant Commander Nic McQuillan said the fire was in about one kilometre of trees and scrub "alongside houses".

While it was now controlled, "firefighters are still dealing with hotspots, flare-ups and ember transfers," and firefighters would be at the scene working on it all night into Sunday, he said.

"No houses have caught fire, although initially it was thought seven to eight properties were threatened and Police evacuated 22 homes."

It was not known what caused the fire, or when people who were evacuated would be able to return home, he said. But a reporter at the scene said there were signs some people may have been allowed home shortly after that briefing.

Do you know more? Email iwitness@rnz.co.nz with information or images

Fire crews from right across central Otago, including Hawea, Tarras and Cromwell, had responded to the blaze, along with three support vehicles.

Fire and Emergency Queenstown Lakes group manager Nic McQuillan, on Saturday night. RNZ/ Katie Todd

Fire trucks could be seen in various streets around the Lagoon Avenue area, just minutes from central Wānaka and the Clutha River.

"We can contain the fire, but we are having to reposition to reach each spot ... But we are dealing with it," McQuillan told RNZ earlier in the night.

Del Tubb said the fire had come right up against his woodshed, near the back of his property:

"We were watching telly and there was a huge roar, which I thought was wind and thought - my God that's strong. Then [his companion] looked out the window - and it was like a blazing inferno."

"It was right across the garden - everything was bright red and it was embers. It was pretty scary stuff at that time, and you don't know what to do, you think 'shall I get out, shall I get my stuff out, move the cars' - all those things. It's really serious, you know."

Tubb said they quickly put on warm gloves and beanies before going out into the cold night, and he was able to move two cars away from the fire area.

RNZ/ Katie Todd

Michael Frankton, who uses a wheelchair, said it was a terrifying sight: "I looked out the window and I could see a raging fire heading towards our house, up the bank in the kānuka".

Sarah Dawson said neighbours acted quickly: "It just went up like these enormous, raging, high flames, just roaring towards us. It was absolutely terrifying," she said.

"All the neighbours rushed out and people were knocking on each other's doors and checking. People looked after Michael and gave him blankets."

RNZ/ Katie Todd

Images posted online showed huge flames rising into the night near houses.

Police were at the scene carrying out evacuations and controlling traffic. A cordon on the corner of Hunt-Lagoon-Sherwin was lifted earlier in the night.

Rain had been minimal this week, residents told RNZ, but by 10:30pm it was raining heavily.

Supplied/ Bernie Hewson

World.title: Late Hanson field goal puts Warriors atop NRL
World.content:
Rookie five-eighth Luke Hanson has slotted a last-minute field goal to put NZ Warriors atop the NRL table with a 45-26 win over the South Sydney Rabbitohs in Sydney.

With one eye on the scoreboard and the other on the points-differential column of the ladder, the visitors almost lost their way in a contest they were in complete control of at halftime on Saturday, but gathered themselves with a late rally for a convincing victory.

A fast start, with tries to skipper James Fisher-Harris and centre Leka Halasima, put the Warriors 12-0 ahead in the opening 10 minutes, and while Souths grabbed a couple of first-half tries, they were unable to stem the onslaught, as co-skipper Mitch Barnett and halfback Chanel Harris-Tavita scored tries before the break.

With incumbent fullback Charnze Nicoll-Kolkstad suspended, Taine Tuaupiki was handed the No.1 jersey and the kicking tee, and he responded with a perfect display that may keep him in the line-up long term.

The 26-8 halftime lead had the Warriors level with Penrith Panthers on the top of the live ladder and they grabbed the outright advantage, when wing Dallin Watene-Zelezniak was first to score after the restart.

Watene-Zelezniak aggravated a shoulder injury in the process and left the field, throwing the backline into disarray, with centre Adam Pompey moving out and second-rower Eddie Ieremia-Toeava into the midfield.

Souths began to take full toll of that confusion, with centre Tallis Duncan, wing Alex Johnson and halfback Cody Walker all scoring down that left side.

Back within six points, the home side seemed on the verge of a dramatic comeback, but Harris-Tavita produced the decisive moment of the game, putting up a high kick on the last tackle, chasing it and gathering to bounce, to put second-rower Jacob Laban over for a try that swung momentum back.

Wing Alofiana Kahn-Pereira scored next and the Warriors were again level with Penrith in the closing moments.

Hanson had also been called into action for his second first-grade game, after star halfback Luke Metcalf tweaked a hamstring last week.

As the final seconds ticked down, the Warriors entered the redzone and set up for the field goal. The ball initially came to Harris-Tavita, but he offloaded to Hanson, who made no mistake, bisecting the uprights for the competition lead.

Sydney Roosters can still reclaim the top spot, when they host struggling Wests Tigers on Sunday, but the result virtually cements a top-four position for the Warriors.

Fifth-placed Cronulla Sharks are now six points behind with three games to play, but lag 130 points behind on differential countback.

Kick-off was 7.30pm Saturday.

World.title: Three hurt in Lindis Pass crash
World.content:
Police are seeking witnesses after three people have been critically injured following a crash on Lindis Pass.

Emergency services were called to State Highway 8, between Lindis Pass-Tarras Road and Birchwood Road, at about 7.40am on Saturday.

Oamaru Police Sergeant Tony Woodbridge said two vehicles were involved in the crash, which happened near Dalrachney Station.

On Saturday evening Woodbridge gave an update: "Three people were transported to hospital, where they remain in critical condition, and our thoughts are with their families at this extremely difficult time".

The Omarama-Lindis Pass Road had reopened after it was closed for several hours after the crash while a scene examination was carried out, but police were still seeking more information, he said.

"Police would like to hear from anyone who witnessed the crash or who might have dashcam footage of it.

"In particular, Police are hoping to speak with a man we believe witnessed the crash and was one of the first people on scene.

"He left before Police arrived, and we are hoping he will come forward and speak with us to help us build a picture of what occurred."

Woodbridge also thanked the people who stopped at the scene of the crash to help and carry out first aid on the injured.

World.title: Police investigate Far North death
World.content:
A woman has been arrested and police have launched an investigation, after a man's death in the Far North.

Emergency services were called to a property in Haruru, near Paihia, about 4.30am Saturday, where a man was unresponsive, police said.

He was pronounced dead a short time later.

Northland Detective Inspector Rhys Johnston said the mean's death was unexplained and a 56-year-old woman was arrested at the scene.

"She has been charged with assault," Johnston said.

Enquiries were underway to find out how the man died.

A post mortem would be carried out on Sunday and a scene guard was in place.

The community could expect to see an increased police presence in the area.

World.title: Auckland City FC bag 14th Oceania Champions League crown
World.content:
Auckland City have won a fifth successive men's Oceania Champions League crown and a 14th in a total after beating Solomon Islands club Central Coast FC 2-0 in the final in Fiji.

Second half goals to Ryan De Vries and Matt Ellis proved the difference in humid conditions at Govind Park in Ba.

A tight first half was followed by a tense start to the second spell before the New Zealand side broke through, when Michal Doudera's stinging shot from the edge of the penalty area was parried by the goalkeeper into the path of De Vries, who tapped home.

The second goal came nine minutes after the first.

Substitute Ryan Watson burst down the right flank and cut infield before a pinpoint cross picked out a sliding Ellis.

Central Coast FC's hopes of a comeback were dealt a further blow in the 83rd minute when Prince Tahunipue was shown a straight red card for his part in a confrontation.

The decider came 10 days after the same two clubs played the tournament's opening game, in which Auckland City needed two late goals to prevail 2-1, with club great De Vries again finding the net.

The Navy Blues have now won all 14 finals they've contested in the 24-year history of the amateur-based OFC Champions League

World.title: Pendlebury could miss rest of season with his playing future undecided
World.content:
Scott Pendlebury's glittering Collingwood career could be over after the AFL/VFL games record holder suffered a hamstring injury.

The 38-year-old will miss up to three weeks, ruling him out of at least next week's historic wildcard match.

In an added blow for the Magpies, tough defender Brayden Maynard suffered a knee injury at training and is in doubt to return this season, no matter how far Collingwood progress in finals.

"These are obviously disappointing setbacks for both Scott and Brayden," Collingwood football boss Charlie Gardiner said.

"These are unfortunate setbacks especially at this time of year, but Scott and Brayden are absolute professionals and will do all they can to get back as quickly as possible."

Pendlebury was ruled out in the second quarter of Friday night's 63-point thrashing by Brisbane at the MCG with what Collingwood described as a "knee bursa".

But scans on Saturday revealed a hamstring strain that will sideline him for two or three weeks.

It comes at a critical time for the 21-season veteran, who is waiting until the end of the year to decide if he plays on in 2027.

McKenna, Morris magic lifts Lions to vital big win over Pies Brisbane Lions put the foot down against Collingwood, with magic from Conor McKenna and Logan Morris seeing the premiers take a strong grip on third spot.

If he does not retire, Pendlebury has also received an offer from Gold Coast to be effectively an on-field playing coach next year.

Collingwood are carefully balancing how they deal with an iconic player contemplating his football mortality.

Pendlebury was also substituted four-and-a-half minutes into last year's preliminary-final loss to Brisbane with calf tightness.

Collingwood would likely err on the side of caution, desperate to avoid a repeat, even if the Magpies are still in premiership contention when he is available.

The Magpies would have to play five straight weeks of knockout finals to claim the most unlikely of premierships.

"That'll all be weighed up," coach Craig McRae said.

"He (Maynard) might be right to go, but then do we want to take that risk?"

The Magpies were conservative with Isaac Quaynor, Patrick Lipinski and Maynard on Friday night.

All three were expected to return next week, but Maynard is now no chance.

"Brayden unfortunately left the track early this morning during a training session, with scans confirming he sustained a grade-one MCL strain," Gardiner said.

"This is the same knee but unrelated to his earlier injury."

Collingwood also managed the game time of Nick Daicos and Darcy Cameron against the Lions in anticipation of the wildcard game, which McRae insisted felt like a final.

AAP

World.title: By the narrowest margin possible, the Warriors are top of the NRL
World.content:
Rookie Luke Hanson has booted a field goal to give the Warriors a 45-26 win over South Sydney that sent the Kiwi outfit to the top of the NRL ladder by the barest of margins.

With hooker Wayde Egan pulling all the strings at Stadium Australia, Andrew Webster's side joined Penrith and the Sydney Roosters on 38 points with a 19-point victory.

The win — the first by the scoreline in premiership history — helps the Warriors (+295) move past the Panthers (+294) on points differential after Hanson nudged a one-point goal from 30m out on the buzzer in just his second NRL game.

The third-placed Roosters (+163) have a game in hand and will play Wests Tigers on Sunday.

"As a team we weren't saying let's go kick a field goal because we need to," Webster said.

"We said every point's going to matter from here to the end.

"Once we kicked it we knew as staff, but I don't know if the players knew — you'd have to ask Luke, he's a pretty smart guy."

The Warriors host Newcastle and Manly over the final two rounds, while Penrith face Canterbury and Wests Tigers.

After Sunday's meeting with the Tigers, the Roosters square off with the Dolphins and Souths to round out their regular season.

The Warriors defied another change at halfback to run up a big score. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor )

"It might not be for too long and you only want to be on top at the end," Webster said.

"That's why we didn't mention for and against between now and then — we could win all our games and it could look different at the end."

While Webster's club bolstered their chances of a first minor premiership since 2002, and the chance to have a home final in week one, Rabbitohs coach Wayne Bennett was left frustrated.

A win would have locked up a top-eight finish for Bennett's Bunnies, who must now beat Gold Coast or the Roosters in their last two fixtures to qualify for the finals.

"What's between their ears? We're not real smart at different times out there," said Bennett, who all but confirmed Latrell Mitchell would return against the Titans.

"I'm talking about the game generally — a lot of things put us under pressure, but I'm never disappointed in the effort."

Canterbury ran up their highest score of the season against the Dragons. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor )

Meanwhile, Canterbury have kept their NRL finals hopes alive with a 44-14 thrashing of St George Illawarra, who are all but certain to collect their first wooden spoon as a joint venture.

Shifted to right centre, Matt Burton grabbed a try-scoring double to help the ninth-placed Bulldogs to a 24-0 halftime lead at the Sydney Football Stadium on Saturday night.

The Dogs bit back at concerns over their attack with their highest score of the season, halfback Lachlan Galvin setting up two tries and scoring one to seal a comfortable win.

Canterbury's clearest path into finals is to win both their remaining games, hope North Queensland lose one of theirs and then leapfrog the Cowboys on for-and-against.

That scenario relies on the Bulldogs beating premiership heavyweights Penrith next week and the eighth-placed Cowboys losing to either Wests Tigers or Canberra, neither of whom will play finals in 2026.

But for now the Dogs remain a top-eight chance, some 12 weeks since languishing in the bottom four.

The win may have come at a cost as veteran Kurt Mann picked up a groin issue after winger Enari Tuala (knee) dropped out before kick-off.

Earlier, Newcastle were left sweating on a Dom Young hip-drop tackle charge after he was sin-binned and their hopes of a home final were put in jeopardy in a shock 44-24 capitulation to Manly.

On a humbling Old Boys' Day in Newcastle, the Knights blew an 18-6 lead early to leave themselves potentially needing to beat the Warriors next week to stay sixth.

Making matters worse is Young being at risk of missing the start of the finals, over a hip-drop tackle that left Sea Eagles star Tolu Koula with a syndesmosis injury.

Koula will require scans, but a grade-three charge would be enough to rule the star Newcastle winger out of the opening week of finals given they have a last-round bye.

AAP

World.title: Tex farewells Adelaide Oval in style as Crows, Cats lock in top six
World.content:
Taylor Walker has a perfect farewell to Adelaide Oval as the Crows and Geelong seal top-six spots, and Melbourne's loss to the Bulldogs re-shapes the finals.

Adelaide beat GWS by 56 points, with Walker kicking six and Izak Rankine four. The win saw the Crows temporarily jump above Hawthorn, who will finish third or fourth if they beat West Coast tomorrow.

In Geelong, the Cats beat Richmond by 57 points, with Jeremy Cameron returning to the side after injury. The Cats are fourth going into the final day of the home-and-away season.

Marcus Bontempelli recorded 27 touches and kicked two goals as the Bulldogs claimed a 16.12 (108) to 12.15 (87) win over the Demons, setting up a wildcard clash against Collingwood.

The Bulldogs win came at a cost though as star forward Aaron Naughton left the ground at the end of the third quarter with an ankle injury.

Earlier on Saturday, Carlton continued its hot form, recording a 37-point win over ladder-leaders Fremantle at Docklands Stadium.

After trailing by 23 points early in the first quarter, the Blues turned the tables in sensational fashion, running out 18.11 (119) to 12.10 (82) winners as Francis Evans kicked five goals.

Meanwhile, former Sydney Swans assistant Josh Francou says the club's scandal "wouldn't have unfolded" under previous coach John Longmire.

Look back at all the action in our live blog.

World.title: Wallaroos hammered in historic 100th Test by ruthless Black Ferns
World.content:
The Wallaroos' 100th Test match, and the Test debut of Australia's all-time leading rugby 7s try-scorer, has been soured by a dominant New Zealand performance in Auckland.

The Black Ferns maintained their unblemished record against the Wallaroos in Test rugby, with a 66-19 win at Mt Smart Stadium.

New Zealand came into Saturday's Test having not lost to Australia in all 30 Tests between the two nations, and a 10-try haul ensured that streak would continue.

The Wallaroos scored three tries, including a score from Waiaria Ellis who started at fly half for the first time.

Maddison Levi, Australia's all-time leading rugby 7s try scorer, made her Wallaroos debut with a 30-minute stint off the bench. Meanwhile, Emily Chancellor became the first woman to represent the Black Ferns and Wallaroos in Test rugby when she made her Australian debut off the bench.

Wallaroos captain Siokapesi Palu Sekona said her team was disappointed in the result, but was pleased the Australians continued fighting, managing to score two of the game's final three tries.

"New Zealand started off really fast, so we were on the back foot," she said.

"But you could see towards the end that we can get back, it's just a matter of starting well."

Highlights were few and far between for the Wallaroos as the Black Ferns dominated from the opening whistle.

Why Wallaroos are 'family' As the Wallaroos prepare for their 100th Test, past and present players reflect on the journey and challenges to reaching this milestone.

A brilliant counter ruck inside Australian territory gave the home side possession, and the Black Ferns then methodically worked their way to the goal-line before fullback Braxton Sorensen-McGee scored on the right flank in the fourth minute.

The Black Ferns continued their early dominance. The Wallaroos were forced to scramble on their goal line to hold out a rampant home side, with New Zealand lock Maiakawanakaulani Roos held up over the line from a line-out maul.

That was just a reprieve for the Wallaroos, as the Black Ferns continued to attack, with prop Chryss Viliko charging over from close range for the second try.

The Black Ferns had a third try in the 24th minute, with lock Maama Mo'onia Vaipulu making a big line break up the middle of the field before passing to fly half Ruahei Demant, who scored under the posts.

New Zealand's one blemish in the first half was Vaipulu being sent to the sin bin, not lowering herself enough in a tackle and making head-on-head contact with Wallaroos' flanker Lily Bone.

Being down to 14 women did not seem to matter to the Black Ferns, who scored a fourth try when Liana Mikaele-Tu'u touched down in the 35th minute.

The Wallaroos were able to take momentum into half-time with their first try of the afternoon. A free kick against the Black Ferns from their own line-out, gave the Wallaroos the ball near the opposition goal-line. The visitors seized the opportunity, with left winger Desiree Miller scoring and then converting her own try.

Down 26-7 at half-time, any hope the Wallaroos had of making a famous comeback was doused quickly.

After being held up early in the first half, Roos finished off a nice passage of play to score New Zealand's fifth try just three minutes into the second half.

By the time Australia's Rugby 7's all-time leading try scorer Levi came on for her Wallaroos debut, the game was not a contest.

Tries to Ayesha Leti-I'iga in the 50th minute and reserve hooker Vici-Rose Green in the 56th minute piled on more misery for the Wallaroos.

The Black Ferns crossed the half-century mark with a try to Maia Joseph, then Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a charged down a kick from Wallaroos fullback Faitala Moleka inside the Australian in-goal, and grounded the ball.

A lovely side-step from Wallaroos fly half Waiaria Ellis sliced open the Black Ferns defensive line for a try in the 67th minute.

That was the start of a bright spot for the Wallaroos, who produced a driving maul from close range, with reserve hooker Brittany Merlo scoring Australia's third try.

World.title: Third woman engages lawyer over 'incredibly traumatic' Sydney Swans scandal
World.content:
A lawyer representing a third woman involved in the Sydney Swans sexual assault scandal says a potential civil lawsuit is being looked at.

Slater and Gordon senior lawyer, Jackson Pannam, has been engaged to represent a woman who he said contacted police immediately following the alleged assault at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne in the early hours of Monday, August 17.

"Our client has had her entire world turned upside down and is now trying to navigate an incredibly traumatic experience," he said.

He said the firm's lawyers "see the profound and long-lasting impact that serious injury, loss and abuse can have on people's lives".

Jackson Pannam says the woman's world has been "turned upside down" by the incident. (ABC News)

On Friday, Carbone Lawyers announced separately that it was representing two women, believed to be adult entertainers involved in the incident, and looking into launching a civil claim.

Several adult entertainers are understood to have joined players at the Pullman Hotel after being hired in the hours after the Swans' victory against Essendon last Sunday night.

Five players — Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon — have been stood down by the Swans for breaching the club's standards on drinking and staying out late following the match in Melbourne.

Mr Pannam said following her initial contact with police, his client was continuing to speak to them as part of their investigation into the incident.

"Everyone deserves to be safe going about their life, at home, at work, and in public spaces without risk of being assaulted or harmed," Mr Pannam said.

"We're standing with our client to give her support at this difficult time, and to help her get the justice she deserves."

Mr Pannam described the woman as "extremely distressed" by what had occurred, and asked for her privacy, and that of the other women involved, to be respected.

He said his client had not spoken to the media.

A police investigation is still underway, but they have not made any arrests or laid charges.

On Saturday, police provided an update about the investigation being undertaken by detectives from the Sexual Crimes Squad.

"The exact circumstances of the matter are still being established, and a number of people have been spoken to," the statement read.

"As the investigation remains active and ongoing, we will not be commenting further, including providing information on the specific circumstances of the matter, movements of detectives and any statements or interviews taken."

In a statement, the Sydney Swans said the club "supports the action taken by Victoria Police in releasing today's statement regarding the investigation".

The club's statement also addressed comments relating to other men, beyond the five players identified by the club, being present in the hotel room at the centre of the allegations.

"The Sydney Swans categorically confirms that no member of staff is involved in the investigation. This includes being in the hotel room central to the police investigation," it read.

"The club reiterates that no player has been interviewed by police at this stage."

Swans chairman Andrew Pridham told The Age the club would "thoroughly" look into how the events of Monday morning took place, adding the club's standards were not the problem, but rather the fact they were breached.

A club representative later clarified there were no plans for an official inquiry.

World.title: Late collapse sees Australia surrender commanding position on day one in Mackay
World.content:
A stunning middle-order collapse has seen Australia surrender a commanding position on day one of the second Test in Mackay.

Towering quick Shoriful Islam, playing his first Test in Australia, took six wickets to rival a sensational new-ball spell from Mitchell Starc earlier in the day, with the two left-armers combining for 12 of the day's 18 wickets.

Cam Green, off the back of a drought-breaking ton in Darwin, was once again the only Australian batter to stand tall, guiding his side to a score of 8-165 and a 101-run lead at stumps on the first day of cricket to be played at Australia's newest Test venue.

If the afternoon and evening belonged to Bangladesh, the morning belonged to Mitch Starc.

The veteran spearhead took six wickets, five of them in a single, devastating opening spell, to deliver what looked to be the perfect response for Australia, still stinging from its shock defeat in Darwin.

Bangladesh, blitzed out for just 64 off the back off Starc's tremendous 6-12, were brought crashing back down to Earth with an unceremonious thud.

Starc struck with his very first ball and, 22 deliveries later, had a five wicket haul in a brutal passage of play that saw him take 5-5 in his six-over spell.

Mitchell Starc claimed a first ball wicket in both of this first two overs. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Shadman Islam, Tanzid Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto and Litton Das were all dismissed for ducks, while Mominul Haque managed just 9 as the tourists fell to 5-12 inside seven overs after loosing the toss and being asked to bat.

Pat Cummins (3-25) and Josh Hazlewood (1-18) also got in on the act, before Starc returned to claim the wicket of number 11 batter Shoriful Islam for 14, Bangladesh's top scorer on a chastening morning of cricket.

Bangladesh's score of 64 was the fourth-lowest Test total in their history and a return to normality as far as Australia were concerned.

In reply though, Australia was unconvincing to begin, then meek and brittle as shadows lengthened in Mackay.

Matt Renshaw was caught at slip off a leading edge for 8, and Travis Head chopped on for 22 to leave the Aussies 2-40.

Renshaw was dimissed cheaply on his return to the Test arena. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Head fell to Shoriful's second ball of the match, and later that same over he had another wicket to his name, the hapless Marnus Labuschagne bowled off his thigh pad for just 4 runs.

The conversation over the Queensland number three was already a clamour, and should Labuschagne fail in the second innings — if required — they could prove impossible to ignore ahead of a tough three-Test series in South Africa next month.

Smith and Green came together either side of tea to build Australia's lead with a 77-run partnership.

Smith was a touch unfortunate to be given out LBW on 42 to Shoriful, given out by umpire Kumar Dharmasena on field, with DRS showing the ball would have brushed the off stump to maintain the on field decision.

Alex Carey, playing his 50th Test and becoming just the seventh Australian wicketkeeper to do so, came and went quickly, mistiming his slog and being caught in the deep for 5.

Shoriful proceeded to tear through the Australian lower order, dismissing Beau Webster LBW for a first-ball duck, having Cummins caught for a second-ball duck and then Starc bowled for 1.

Green ended the day on 51, with Nathan Lyon alongside him as Bangladesh clung onto the hosts' coat tails in this series.

Relive all the action in our live blog below.

World.title: Lions coach 'feels sorry' for Swans as likely finals clash looms
World.content:
Embattled Sydney will brace for further fallout from the scandal that has rocked the AFL club, while finalising preparations for a dead rubber against North Melbourne on Sunday.

On Thursday, five players — Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon — were suspended for the rest of the season for "breaching club standards".

Separately, a police investigation continues into the events at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel in the early hours of Monday morning.

On Friday, coach Dean Cox distanced himself from any blame for the events at the hotel, while captain Callum Mills said "we believe that the five players have let us down".

Swans chairman Andrew Pridham on Wednesday said the club-imposed sanctions would "torpedo" the second-placed Swans' premiership hopes.

Swans coach Dean Cox (left) and captain Callum Mills spoke to reporters on Friday. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

In their SCG qualifying final, Sydney will most likely face reigning premiers Brisbane, who all but locked in third place with Friday night's 63-point win over Collingwood, unless Hawthorn leapfrog them on percentage with a big win over West Coast.

The team that finishes fourth plays runaway minor premiers Fremantle while third faces a decimated and embattled Sydney.

"I don't mind either or, to be honest with you," Lions coach Chris Fagan said after Friday night's match.

"It's just good to get the double chance.

"And I'm sort of thinking that Sydney have lost some players obviously due to the unfortunate thing that happened last week. But in some ways that can galvanise a club too.

"The guys that do get to play just might go that much harder and be that much more difficult to beat.

"So either way I'm just happy we finished top four. We travel well. Either way we're going to have to travel, so we'll take whatever comes our way."

McKenna, Morris magic lifts Lions to vital big win over Pies Brisbane Lions put the foot down against Collingwood, with magic from Conor McKenna and Logan Morris seeing the premiers take a strong grip on third spot.

Fagan hasn't spoken to his players specifically about the Sydney situation.

"There's been so much publicity around it — it almost goes without saying," Fagan said.

"I don't feel like I need to have a conversation with my players because it's pretty obvious, the repercussions for not thinking through your actions too clearly. And yeah, it's really unfortunate.

"I do feel sorry for Sydney because they have been such a terrific club in that regard for a long, long time but these sorts of things happen. It's just a bit of a head-scratcher, isn't it?

"You just wonder what was going through people's heads to let that occur."

Sydney on Friday disputed assertions there were more than five players in the East Melbourne hotel room on Monday morning.

James Rowbottom, Harry Cunningham, Angus Sheldrick, Caiden Cleary and Tom Hanily will replace the banned five players for the North Melbourne clash.

That game takes place after Sydney's AFLW clash with Essendon as part of a double header.

World.title: Argentina star hit with one of the biggest bans in World Cup history
World.content:
FIFA banned three Argentina players overnight, including a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents after losing the World Cup final.

The ban for Paredes — who grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground — ranks with the FIFA sanctions for Uruguay forward Luis Suárez in 2014 as among the most severe in World Cup history.

Argentina defender Nahuel Molina was handed a seven-game ban while Thiago Almada was given a one-game suspension. FIFA imposed fines of $US90,000 ($AU125,000) on Paredes and Molina, and $US30,000 for Almada.

The ban for Paredes is effectively a one-year expulsion from the Argentina team as the FIFA calendar for national team schedules includes 10 games through June 2027.

All of those games could be friendlies with no competitive games currently scheduled.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina is confronted by Spanish captain Rodri after the World Cup final. (Getty Images: Martin Rickett/PA Images)

Gavi also was banned for one game, which is a Nations League match for Spain against England at Wembley on September 26.

An Argentina coach, Roberto Ayala, was also handed a three-game ban and a $US30,000 fine.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) was fined $US110,000 for a range of incidents during the World Cup, including players carrying a political banner about the Falkland Islands after the semifinal win against England, and discriminatory chants by fans.

AFA was also ordered by FIFA to spend $US100,000 on anti-racism projects. Argentina received $US34 million in World Cup prize money from FIFA.

AFA can appeal the longer sanctions and fines to FIFA, and likely after at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"The AFA legal department will, in a timely manner, request from FIFA the grounds for the reviewable rulings in order to file appeals with the governing body's appeal committee, while retaining the future option of appealing to the CAS as a final recourse," the federation said in a statement.

Luis Suárez holds his teeth after biting Italy's Giorgio Chiellini. (Getty Images: Matthias Hangst)

In 2014, Suárez was banned from all soccer for four months, including for his new club Barcelona, and eight more competition games for Uruguay for biting Italian defender Giorgio Chiellini in a World Cup group stage game in Brazil.

Paredes' 10-game ban equals that in 2013 for Josip Simunic of Croatia after winning a World Cup qualifying play-off. Simunic used a megaphone to lead fans chanting a slogan used by the country's pro-Nazi regime during World War II.

The on-field clashes at last month's final in East Rutherford, New Jersey — which were charged by FIFA as assault cases — came after Argentina lost a testy final to Spain where the team was mostly outplayed and barely created a scoring chance.

Spain forward Ferran Torres scored the only goal in the second period of extra time, after Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off.

FIFA disciplinary judges also ordered Argentina to play its next home game in a stadium limited to 50 per cent of capacity. FIFA deferred a second stadium sanction and a $US100,000 fine for probationary periods.

Tech.title: Amazon just hiked the prices for Echo, Fire TV, and Kindle products by up to 60 percent
Tech.content:
is a senior reviewer with over twenty years of experience. She covers smart home, IoT, and connected tech, and has written previously for Wirecutter, Wired, Dwell, BBC, and US News.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Citing “significant increases in memory and storage component costs,” in a statement given to Fortune, Amazon has raised prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs, and Eeros by up to 60 percent.

The cheapest products in Amazon’s lineup were hit hardest, with the Echo Dot smart speaker jumping from $49.99 to $79.99. The Fire TV Stick 4K Max also rose by over 40 percent to $84.99, and the base level Kindle now costs $149.99, a nearly 37 percent increase.

Amazon’s flagship Echo Dot Max smart speaker, which launched last year, now costs $119.99, up from $99.99. Apple increased the price of its comparable HomePod Mini this summer to $129 from $99.99, also in response to rising costs. The Google Home Speaker remains at $99.99 for now.

The only Amazon hardware products apparently not affected are its line of Ring cameras and video doorbells, and the Echo Studio, its higher-end $219.99 smart speaker.

Tech.title: An okay laptop with 16GB of RAM is better than a nice laptop with 8GB, and this $520 HP OmniBook proves it
Tech.content:
is a reviewer covering laptops and the occasional gadget. He spent over 15 years in the photography industry before joining The Verge as a deals writer in 2021.

Laptop prices are out of whack. $500 used to get you a tolerable laptop, and $900 got you a really good one. They often had similar CPU, RAM, and storage options because that stuff was comparatively cheap; the difference was often in build quality and screen rather than power. But RAMageddon has thrown everything off. Even laptops like the $950 Surface Laptop now start with 8GB of RAM, which isn’t enough. And on the lower end, where manufacturers are struggling to compete with the $700 MacBook Neo, they’re cutting corners on storage, CPU, and build quality too.

However, one low-cost laptop has bucked this and genuinely surprised me. HP’s 16-inch OmniBook 3 is a basic productivity laptop that regularly goes for around $520 at Walmart and Amazon. It has Qualcomm’s base Snapdragon X chip, meaning passable everyday performance and excellent battery life. But it also has a humdrum screen, mediocre speakers, a run-of-the-mill trackpad, and a plastic build. Pre-RAMageddon, it would be nothing to write home about.

But 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD in an okay laptop for around $500? That counts as good news in 2026.

The entry-level OmniBook 3 I tested has an 8-core Snapdragon X processor, 16GB of RAM, 512GB SSD, and a 16-inch 1920 x 1200 anti-glare IPS LCD. And the OmniBook 3 is fairly portable for a larger laptop with lots of ports. It’s barely heavier than a 14-inch MacBook Pro, and at a maximum thickness of 0.63 inches / 16mm it’s decently thin. This big laptop doesn’t feel big. And despite a plastic chassis and low price it doesn’t feel too cheap either.

Component report card Screen: D

Webcam: C

Keyboard: C

Trackpad: C

Port selection: B

Speakers: D

Number of ugly stickers to remove: 2

As much as I would like to see more cheap Windows laptops with the sleek looks and sturdy all-metal build of the MacBook Neo, I wouldn’t mind if more of them were like the OmniBook 3. Its screen, keyboard, trackpad, and webcam are all at least passable to decent. There isn’t anything special here, but unlike the Chuwi UniBook there’s also nothing that feels like a punishment.

The 1920 x 1200 / 60Hz screen isn’t high-quality or bright enough to combat the sun when taken outside (it maxes out at 300 nits of brightness and covers a paltry 62.5 percent of the sRGB color space), but it isn’t washed out or bleeding light at its edges. The mechanical trackpad has a basic diving board-style hinge, but a confident and decent-feeling kachunk-y click. The 1080p webcam is actually fairly sharp, and it does a good job handling backlight from a bright window — with only a hint of green color cast. But hey, at least it has Windows Hello face unlocking. And at least this not-too-large large laptop has lots of ports and charges via USB-C with a very compact 65W GaN charger.

Just one USB-A and an audio jack on this side. But another USB-A, two USB-C, and HDMI over here. The left-aligned keyboard and trackpad allow for a generously sized numpad.

My biggest gripe is the dual speakers (unsurprisingly), which lack bass and sound too treble-y, but they’re just tolerable enough to live with. My next biggest is the keyboard (surprisingly). I usually like HP keyboards, but this one feels too stiff. If you’re the type to hammer your fingers down and you love a generously sized number pad you might be fine, but I get more typos than I’m used to from keys not registering. I could learn to live with it, but I’d still prefer not to have to.

HP OmniBook 3 16 / Qualcomm Snapdragon X X1-26-100 / 16GB / 512GB MacBook Neo / Apple A18 Pro / 8GB / 256GB Chuwi UniBook / Intel Core 3 304 “Wildcat Lake” / 8GB / 256GB Microsoft Surface Laptop 13-inch (2026) / Qualcomm Snapdragon X Plus X1P-46-100 / 8GB / 256GB Acer Aspire 14 AI / Intel Core Ultra 7 256V / 16GB / 1TB Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x / Qualcomm Snapdragon X X1-26-100 / 16GB / 256GB CPU cores 8 6 5 8 8 8 GPU Adreno X1-45 A18 Pro (5 GPU cores) Intel Graphics (1 GPU core) Adreno X1-45 Intel Arc 140V (8 GPU cores) Adreno X1-45 Geekbench 6 CPU Single 2142 3402 2385 2348 2769 2137 Geekbench 6 CPU Multi 10593 8508 6187 9421 10930 9728 Geekbench 6 GPU (OpenCL) 9577 19798 6019 9554 28556 9689 Premiere 4K Export (lower is better) 12 minutes, 8 seconds 8 minutes, 30 seconds 1 hour, 9 minutes, 29 seconds Crashed 7 minutes, 28 seconds 12 minutes, 59 seconds Sustained SSD reads (MB/s) 5017.12 1735.91 2394.57 3804.31 6391.51 5738.86 Sustained SSD writes (MB/s) 4370.35 1684.05 2092.66 3310.94 5524.22 2801.02 Price as tested about $520 $699 $449 $949.99 $1,049.99 $749.99

What I can totally live with is the performance. The OmniBook’s 8-core Snapdragon X processor is a little slower than the one in the $950 Surface Laptop I tested, but the OmniBook’s day-to-day performance is better because it’s not starved for RAM and its larger SSD is a little faster. Like other lower-end Snapdragon laptop chips it’s not going to wow you with graphics performance or tackle heavy content creation in Adobe apps, but it’s perfectly adequate for everyday multitasking work. Even when running several apps with a couple dozen Chrome tabs left open, including a video podcast playing, I didn’t feel it slow down the way the Surface Laptop or Chuwi UniBook, each with only 8GB of RAM, did.

And while a Snapdragon chip means this Windows laptop isn’t ideal for gaming, it does make it great on battery. You can pretty easily get around 12 hours of mixed web usage with a bit of music or video streaming.

It feels like the money went into the core specs of the OmniBook 3, and HP just barely stuck the landing on the right compromises elsewhere. As much as I adore the build quality of Microsoft’s Surface Laptops, if I were spending my own money I’d choose the OmniBook 3, never worry about how much RAM is in use, and save over $400.

Previous Next













1 / 8 The screen is bright enough to use it near a big window, but outside it’s difficult to see even in the shade.

If we reviewed the OmniBook 3 a year ago I might feel different, but it’s been a tiny breath of fresh air to use something this cheap and mostly think, “Not too bad!” Especially coming right after I tested the $450 Chuwi UniBook. An employee being issued this laptop for work shouldn’t feel like their IT department totally hates them. And while I think a MacBook Neo would still be a better all-around experience for a school-age kid, I’d totally understand saving nearly $200 to get the OmniBook 3 if a budget can’t be stretched.

My only worry is that the OmniBook 3’s price will go up like everything else. While there are more sub-$800 laptops coming, and I’ll be testing more very soon, the OmniBook 3’s price — and that of the OmniBook 5 I reviewed back in December — feel anomalous right now. The RAMageddon storm could eventually ruin them like it did many other laptops and devices. But, for now, there’s some safe harbor with this lowly OmniBook.
